See also Beams API reference Beam, light traveling along a path between two controls Light rays, shafts falling across the shape from a source outside it Starfield and Retro grid, other backgrounds

docs/effects/bokeh.html.title: Bokeh | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/bokeh.html.summary: Bokeh Bokeh paints soft, out-of-focus lights drifting at three depths over a background, the way a lens renders lights it isn't focused on: round discs with brighter rims, the nearest ones biggest and fastest. Use it behind an evening event, a music or nightlife screen, or a festive banner. It's a fill: it paints the host's shape under the child. Light Dark Add bokeh Put the host around the panel, and leave the panel without a background so the lights show through it. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Bokeh /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="260"> <TextBlock Text="Tonight" Foreground="White" FontSize="30" FontWeight="Bold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets A preset picks the palette of the lights: Value Description City (default) Warm street lights with a few cool ones. Sunset Coral, orange, yellow and pink lights, with a touch of violet. Neon Aqua, blue, purple, pink and yellow lights, like neon signs. Colors takes up to six colors of your own, and each light takes one of them at random. BackgroundColor is the color behind the lights. <fx:Bokeh Preset="Neon" /> <fx:Bokeh Colors="#FDE68A, #F472B6, #60A5FA" BackgroundColor="#111827" /> Set the focus and the drift Size is the radius of the nearest lights in DIPs; farther ones are smaller. Focus sets how sharp the discs' edges are, from 0 (very soft) to 1. Density sets how many lights there are. Drift multiplies how fast they drift, and Twinkle how much they brighten and dim, from 0 (steady) to 1. With both at 0 the lights hold still, and the layer asks for no frames. <fx:Bokeh Size="60" Focus="0.7" Density="0.6" Drift="0.4" Twinkle="0" /> To change the pace while it runs, change Speed or Drift: neither makes the animation jump, and the lights carry on from where they are. Fills run on one shared clock, so bokeh on different hosts, with the same settings from the start, drifts in step. Float the lights over content Set BackgroundColor to a transparent color to keep only the lights. Under the child, they then show wherever the child is see-through; with Placement="Over", they float over the content, such as a photo: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Bokeh BackgroundColor="Transparent" Placement="Over" Density="0.5" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Image Source="/Assets/city-night.jpg" Width="360" Height="240" Stretch="UniformToFill" /> </fx:FXHost> The lights are added as light, so they show best over dark content. Properties Property Type Default Description Preset BokehPreset City The palette of the lights, used while Colors is unset. Values: City, Sunset, Neon. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. BackgroundColor Color #0B0F1D The color behind the lights; transparent shows what is behind the host. To lay the lights over the content, also set Placement to Over. Density double 1 How many lights. Range 0.2–3. Size double 34 Radius of the nearest lights, DIPs; farther ones are smaller. Range 4–120. Focus double 0.3 How sharp the discs' edges are (0: very soft). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Drift double 1 How fast the lights drift down, a multiple; nearer lights move faster (0: still). Range 0–3. Twinkle double 0.4 How much each light slowly dims and brightens (0: steady). Range 0–1 (0–100%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1, and Seed picks where the lights are. Notes Light and dark surfaces: bokeh doesn't change with the surface. Its default background is dark, so it looks the same in both themes; with a transparent background, the lights fade out over a light surface. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the lights hold one fixed pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.44 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, among the heavier backgrounds. The cost grows with the area; the discs are soft, so on a large panel RenderScale="0.5" suits it. See Performance. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which paints only the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also Bokeh API reference Starfield, Caustics and Light leaks Mesh gradient, another fill painted from a list of colors Render scale

docs/effects/borderbeam.html.title: Border beam | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/borderbeam.html.summary: Border beam Border beam sends streaks of light running around the host's border, each fading from a bright head to its tail color, with a soft glow on either side. Use it on a chat input, a "new" badge, or a card that is working on something. The streaks run along the edge of the shape, following its corner radius, and draw over the child. Light Dark Add a border beam Color is the bright head and TailColor the end of the streak. Period is the time for one lap, in seconds, and Length the length of each streak along the border. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="22"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:BorderBeam Period="5" Length="110" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBox PlaceholderText="Ask anything…" Width="260" Height="44" CornerRadius="22" Padding="18,0" VerticalContentAlignment="Center" BorderThickness="0" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Run several streaks Count spreads up to four streaks evenly around the border. IsReversed runs them the other way around, and Offset sets where the first one starts, as a share of a lap. <fx:BorderBeam Count="2" IsReversed="True" Color="#22D3EE" TailColor="#7C5CFF" Length="80" /> Width is the thickness of the stroke. Glow scales the soft light on either side of it (0 for none) and GlowRadius sets how far that light spreads. Show it while working Bind IsActive to show the beam only while something is in progress. Switched off, the layer draws nothing and costs nothing. <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:BorderBeam IsActive="{Binding IsGenerating}" Period="3" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="280" Height="140" CornerRadius="16" Background="#15171C" /> </fx:FXHost> Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #FFAA40 The color at a streak's bright head. TailColor Color #9C40FF The color a streak fades to at its tail. Length double 120 Length of each streak along the border. Range 8–1000 DIPs. Period double 6 Seconds for one lap. Range 0.5–30. Width double 1.5 Thickness of a streak's line, in DIPs. Range 0.5–8. Glow double 0.6 The soft light either side of a streak, a multiple: 1 is full, 0 none. Range 0–2. GlowRadius double 6 How far the glow spreads either side of a streak, in DIPs. Range 1–30. Count int 1 Streaks, evenly spaced around the border. Range 1–4. IsReversed bool false Runs the other way around. Offset double 0 Where the first streak starts, as a share of a lap. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a border beam, Intensity dims the layer and Seed doesn't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the streaks add light. On a light surface they draw as tinted haze, and the glow stays mostly inside the shape, so it doesn't smudge the surface around it. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The streaks hold still. See Reduced motion. Cost. About 0.03 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. It shades only a ring around the border, not the interior. See Performance. Room around the host. The glow spreads a little past the edge, about 2.5 × GlowRadius. A clipping ancestor cuts it off: leave a few DIPs of room around the host. See also BorderBeam API reference Glow, whose Aura style flows colors around the whole border Electric, lightning crawling around the border Beam, light traveling between two controls Layers and hosts

docs/effects/caustics.html.title: Caustics | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/caustics.html.summary: Caustics Caustics paints the shifting web of light that water throws on the floor of a pool, over a water color, with an optional color split at the bright lines. Use it as a background for anything about water, summer or calm, or, with a transparent water color, to lay pool light over the content. It's a fill: by default it paints the host's shape under the child. Light Dark Add caustics Put the host around the panel, and leave the panel without a background so the water shows through it. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Caustics /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="260"> <TextBlock Text="Pool" Foreground="White" FontSize="28" FontWeight="Bold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Tune the web Scale is the size of the web's cells in DIPs (70 by default), and Sharpness how thin the bright lines are. Brightness scales the light, LightColor tints it, and Dispersion splits it into colors at the bright lines (0 for none). WaterColor is the water under the light, and Depth darkens it toward the bottom, as if deeper (0 for none). <fx:Caustics Scale="110" Sharpness="10" Brightness="1.2" Dispersion="0" Depth="0.2" WaterColor="#0E7490" /> Speed sets how fast the water moves. Fills run on one shared clock, so caustics on different hosts, with the same settings, shift in step. Light the content with pool light WaterColor's alpha is how opaque the water is. With a transparent water color, Placement="Over" and BlendMode="Screen", the layer lays only the light over the content, as if it sat at the bottom of a pool: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Caustics WaterColor="Transparent" Placement="Over" BlendMode="Screen" Brightness="0.8" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Image Source="/Assets/pool-tiles.jpg" Width="360" Height="240" Stretch="UniformToFill" /> </fx:FXHost> Screen brightens what is beneath without passing white, so the light shows best on mid and dark tones; over white there is nothing left to brighten. See Blend modes. Properties Property Type Default Description LightColor Color #D9FBFF The color of the web of light. WaterColor Color #0B6E8F The water under the light; its alpha is how opaque it is. Scale double 70 Size of the web's cells. Range 8–400 DIPs. Brightness double 1 How bright the web of light is (0: only the water shows). Range 0–3. Sharpness double 7 How thin the bright lines are. Range 1–20. Dispersion double 0.3 Color split at the bright lines. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Depth double 0.5 Darkening toward the bottom, as if deeper, as a share (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1. Notes Light and dark surfaces: with an opaque water color, the layer paints its own colors and looks the same on a light or a dark surface. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the web holds one fixed pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.43 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, among the heavier backgrounds. With Dispersion above 0 the shader works the web out three times a pixel, once per color; at 0 it works it out once. The cost grows with the area: on a large panel, try RenderScale="0.5", which softens the lines a little. See Performance. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which paints only the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also Caustics API reference Water, the content under a rippling surface Waves and Bokeh Blend modes

docs/effects/chromasplit.html.title: Chroma split | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/chromasplit.html.summary: Chroma split ChromaSplit pulls the red and blue channels apart from green, so edges pick up red and blue fringes, as on a misaligned screen or a cheap lens. With GlitchRate, thin slices now and then jump sideways. Use it on a bold heading, a tech or retro title, or as a hover accent. It draws over the child and works on what is drawn there: the child, and whatever shows through it. Light Dark Add a chroma split Wrap the content in a host. OffsetX and OffsetY set how far red and blue move, in opposite directions: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ChromaSplit OffsetX="2" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="Nova FX" FontSize="40" FontWeight="Bold" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Add glitch slices GlitchRate is how often slices jump sideways, from 0 (never) to 1: <fx:ChromaSplit OffsetX="3" GlitchRate="0.4" /> With slices, the layer animates and Seed and Speed apply; without them it is still and draws once. Split on hover Animate the offset from a style, so the colors pull apart while the pointer is over a host with Classes="title". Leave OffsetX unset on the layer itself, since a local value wins over a style: <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.title fx|ChromaSplit"> <Setter Property="OffsetX" Value="0" /> <Setter Property="Transitions"> <Transitions> <DoubleTransition Property="OffsetX" Duration="0:0:0.2" /> </Transitions> </Setter> </Style> <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.title:pointerover fx|ChromaSplit"> <Setter Property="OffsetX" Value="3" /> </Style> Give it sharp edges The split copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop): the child, and whatever shows through it. Content with sharp, high-contrast edges, such as bold text or icons, shows the fringes best; a flat fill shows nothing. Controls drawn after the host aren't split. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. Properties Property Type Default Description OffsetX double 2 How far red moves left and blue moves right, in DIPs; negative swaps them. Range -16 to 16. OffsetY double 0 How far red moves up and blue moves down, in DIPs; negative swaps them. Range -16 to 16. GlitchRate double 0 How often slices jump sideways (0: never). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Feather double 2 How soft the layer's edge is, in DIPs. Range 0–16. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the slices stop jumping; the split itself stays. Cost: about 0.11 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card. Without GlitchRate it doesn't animate, so it only redraws when what is under it changes. See Performance. See also ChromaSplit API reference Glitch, for a burst of torn bands and flashing rows CRT and Heat haze Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/coderain.html.title: Code rain | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/coderain.html.summary: Code rain CodeRain rains columns of glyphs down a terminal-style background. Each stream has a bright head and a fading trail, and the glyphs flip as it passes. The glyphs are dot-matrix shapes made up for each cell, not a font, so the rain looks the same on every platform. Use it behind a terminal, a "connecting" screen or a hacker-themed hero. It's a fill: it paints the host's shape under the child. Light Dark Add code rain Put the host around the panel, and leave the panel without a background so the rain shows through it. A dark, slightly see-through plate keeps text readable over the streams: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:CodeRain /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="240"> <Border Background="#CC020A06" CornerRadius="8" Padding="12,8" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <TextBlock Text="> connected" Foreground="#E6FFF0" FontFamily="Menlo, Consolas, monospace" FontSize="16" /> </Border> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Change the rain GlyphSize is the height of a glyph cell in DIPs (14 by default); columns are about two thirds as wide. Density is the share of the columns that rain, Trail the length of a stream's trail in glyphs, and ChangeRate how often a glyph flips, per second (0: the glyphs never change). Color colors the trail, HeadColor the bright head, and BackgroundColor the terminal behind them. An amber terminal with fewer, longer streams: <fx:CodeRain Color="#FFB000" HeadColor="#FFF4D6" BackgroundColor="#0A0700" GlyphSize="18" Density="0.5" Trail="22" /> Each column falls at its own pace. Speed multiplies them all, and fills run on one shared clock, so code rain on different hosts, with the same settings, falls in step. Rain over content Set BackgroundColor to a transparent color to keep only the glyphs. Under the child, they then show wherever the child is see-through; with Placement="Over", they rain over the content: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:CodeRain BackgroundColor="Transparent" Placement="Over" Density="0.3" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="320" Height="180" CornerRadius="12" Background="#0B1220" Padding="16"> <TextBlock Text="Access granted" Foreground="White" FontSize="20" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> The glyphs are added as light, so they show best over dark content. Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #3CFF8F The color of the glyphs in a stream's trail. HeadColor Color #E6FFF0 The color of the bright glyph at the head of each stream. BackgroundColor Color #020A06 The color behind the glyphs; transparent shows what is behind the host. To rain over the content, also set Placement to Over. GlyphSize double 14 Height of a glyph cell. Range 6–48 DIPs. Density double 0.7 Share of the columns raining. Range 0.05–1 (5–100%). Trail double 14 Length of a stream's trail, in glyphs. Range 2–40. ChangeRate double 3 How often a glyph flips, per second. Range 0–20. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1, and Seed picks which columns rain and their glyphs. Notes Light and dark surfaces: code rain doesn't change with the surface. Its default background is dark, so it looks the same in both themes; with a transparent background, the glyphs fade out over a light surface. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the streams and glyphs hold one fixed pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.06 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, among the cheapest layers. The cost grows with the area. See Performance. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which rains only inside the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also CodeRain API reference ASCII, which redraws what is behind it as text characters CRT and Glitch, for more of a terminal look Dot grid and Starfield, other backgrounds

docs/effects/colorfilter.html.title: Color filter | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/colorfilter.html.summary: Color filter ColorFilter recolors what is drawn within the host's shape, live: grayscale, sepia, saturation, hue, brightness and contrast with CSS's own formulas, plus temperature, tint, duotone and invert. Use it for a disabled state, a photo that stays gray until hovered, a styled thumbnail or a picture dimmed in a dark theme. It reads what is already drawn rather than a snapshot of the child, so it keeps up with whatever the child does. Where it draws decides what it recolors. Light Dark Add a color filter Wrap the content in a host. The filter starts as grayscale, so it shows something with no settings: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ColorFilter /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Image Source="/Assets/photo.jpg" Width="240" Height="140" Stretch="UniformToFill" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets A preset sets several settings at once. It applies at template priority, so a local value on any setting wins over it. None puts every setting at rest, to start from the picture as it is. Value Description Grayscale (default) Fully gray: the colors drained, the lightness kept. Sepia Toned brown, like an old photograph. Vivid More saturated, a little more contrast. Faded Washed out and lifted, like an old print. Warm A warmer white balance: redder, less blue, a little more saturated. Cool A cooler white balance: bluer, less red. Duotone Lightness mapped from a deep violet to a warm cream. Invert A negative: every color inverted. None Every setting at rest: the picture as it is. Choose what it recolors The layer works on what is drawn within the shape just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). Its placement decides what that is: To recolor Set Like CSS The child and anything that shows through it Nothing: by default it draws over the child filter Only what is behind the host, with the child unchanged on top Placement="Under" backdrop-filter Only the child's own pixels: an icon, not the card around it UseMask="True" Under the child, the filter needs something drawn behind the host, such as a picture, a list or the page's background, and the child should be see-through where the filtered backdrop is meant to show. Here a caption bar fades the photo behind it: <Grid> <Image Source="/Assets/photo.jpg" Stretch="UniformToFill" /> <fx:FXHost VerticalAlignment="Bottom"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ColorFilter Placement="Under" Preset="Faded" Brightness="0.7" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Height="56" Padding="16,0"> <TextBlock Text="Lisbon, 2019" Foreground="White" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </Grid> With UseMask, the host captures the child to learn its pixels (see Content masks), and only those pixels change: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ColorFilter UseMask="True" Preset="Duotone" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Image Source="/Assets/logo.png" Width="64" /> </fx:FXHost> Keep it gray until hover Intensity is how much of the filter shows. Fade it out while the pointer is over a host with Classes="photo": <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.photo fx|ColorFilter"> <Setter Property="Transitions"> <Transitions> <DoubleTransition Property="Intensity" Duration="0:0:0.3" /> </Transitions> </Setter> </Style> <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.photo:pointerover fx|ColorFilter"> <Setter Property="Intensity" Value="0" /> </Style> Mix your own Start from Preset="None" and set only what you need. Tint tones the picture toward a color at the same lightness, and its alpha is how much; Duotone maps lightness from ShadowColor to HighlightColor: <fx:ColorFilter Preset="None" Saturation="1.3" Contrast="1.1" Hue="-15" Tint="#40FF8A00" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset ColorFilterPreset Grayscale A set of the settings below. The default is Grayscale; None puts every setting at rest, to start from the picture as it is (a local value on any setting wins over the preset). Values: Grayscale, Sepia, Vivid, Faded, Warm, Cool, Duotone, Invert, None. Grayscale double 1 How far the colors drain to gray: 0 none, 1 fully gray (CSS grayscale()). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Sepia double 0 How far the picture tones to brown, like an old photograph: 0 none, 1 full (CSS sepia()). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Saturation double 1 1: as it is; 0: gray; above 1: more vivid. Range 0–3. Hue double 0 Turns every hue around the color wheel, degrees: 0 leaves them; positive turns red toward yellow and green, as CSS's hue-rotate does. Range -180 to 180. Brightness double 1 1: as it is; 0: black. Range 0–3. Contrast double 1 1: as it is; 0: flat gray. Range 0–3. Temperature double 0 Warmer (positive) or cooler (negative) white balance. Range -1 to 1. Tint Color #00FFFFFF A color the picture is toned toward at the same lightness; its alpha is how much. Duotone double 0 How much the picture becomes two colors, its lightness running from ShadowColor to HighlightColor. Range 0–1 (0–100%). ShadowColor Color #2B1055 The duotone color for the darkest parts; applies as Duotone rises. HighlightColor Color #FFD3A0 The duotone color for the lightest parts; applies as Duotone rises. Invert double 0 How far the colors invert: 0 none, 1 a negative; 0.5 is flat gray (CSS invert()). Range 0–1 (0–100%). UseMask bool false Recolors only the child's own pixels (text, an icon, a picture), not the shape around them. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The filter is still, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. To dim pictures in a dark theme only, give Brightness a value per theme with a theme resource, as Light and dark surfaces does for colors. Reduced motion: nothing moves, so nothing changes. Cost: it doesn't animate, so it only redraws when what it reads changes. On the benchmark card it takes about 0.11 ms of GPU time a frame. With every setting at rest it copies nothing and draws nothing. See Performance. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. A disabled style that lowers a parent's Opacity is a common case: dim with the filter's own Brightness instead. With UseMask, the host watches only the child itself. After changing something deeper inside it, call RefreshMask. See also ColorFilter API reference Old film, CRT, Dither and Halftone, which also restyle what is behind them Layers that read the backdrop Content masks

docs/effects/confetti.html.title: Confetti | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/confetti.html.summary: Confetti Confetti fires a burst of paper pieces that fly, tumble, flutter and fall: for a success, a completed order or a milestone. It is a one-shot: it draws nothing until you fire it, from code or on a press, and each burst is gone after its Duration. The pieces are drawn over the host and fly well past it. Light Dark Add confetti With FireOnPress, a press on the host fires a burst from the press point: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Confetti FireOnPress="True" Count="80" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Complete order" Padding="24,12" CornerRadius="14" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The host hears the press even when the button handles it, so the button's Click still runs. Styles Style sets where the pieces come from. Shape picks the pieces themselves: Mixed (the default), Paper or Dots. Value Description Burst (default) A cone of pieces from a point (the press point, or the shape's center). Cannons Two cannons at the shape's bottom corners, firing up and inward. Fall Pieces drifting down from above the shape. Fire from code Name the layer and call Fire() when the moment comes, for example from an event your view model raises: // In the view's code-behind; OrderPlaced is the view model's own event. viewModel.OrderPlaced += (_, _) => Celebration.Fire(); Fire(at) takes a point in the host's coordinates. Only Burst uses it, or the center of the shape without one; Cannons always fire from the bottom corners, and Fall drops from above the shape. Bursts overlap: firing again while one plays starts another beside it, up to four at once, and a fifth drops the oldest. Aim the burst Angle points the burst (0 to the right, -90 up) and Spread sets the width of its cone. Power sets the launch speed and Gravity how fast the pieces fall. Colors takes your own palette: <fx:Confetti x:Name="Celebration" Angle="-60" Spread="40" Power="1.4" Colors="#22d3ee, #a78bfa, #f472b6, #facc15" /> With Burst and Cannons, on a shape larger than about 250 × 250 DIPs, the whole burst grows up to 1.6 times as large, so it fills the shape. For a whole panel, try Cannons, or Fall for a gentle drift down. Methods Call Fire to start a burst from code. Method Description Fire(Point? at = null) Fires a burst from at (host coordinates), or the style's own origin. Properties Property Type Default Description Style ConfettiStyle Burst Where the pieces come from: a burst from a point, two cannons at the bottom corners, or a fall from above. Values: Burst, Cannons, Fall. Colors FXColorList Unset The pieces' colors. Unset: six bright party colors. Shape ConfettiShape Mixed The pieces' shape: paper strips, round dots, or a mix of both. Values: Mixed, Paper, Dots. Count int 70 How many pieces each burst throws. Range 4–200. Power double 1 Launch speed, as a multiple of a lively default. On a shape larger than about 250 × 250 DIPs the whole burst is up to 1.6 times as large (faster, with gravity to match), so it fills the shape. Range 0.2–3. Applies to the Burst and Cannons styles. Spread double 75 Width of the burst's cone, degrees, centered on Angle. Range 0–360. Applies to the Burst style. Angle double -90 Where the burst points, degrees: 0 to the right, -90 up; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Burst style. Gravity double 1 How strongly the pieces fall, a multiple of the default (0: they don't fall). Range 0–3. Size double 8 Size of a piece, DIPs. Range 2–24. Duration double 2.6 How long a burst lasts. Range 0.5–6 seconds. FireOnPress bool false Fires wherever the pointer is pressed on the host. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. While IsActive is off, presses fire nothing. Notes Light and dark. The pieces are drawn the same on both surfaces, in their own colors. Reduced motion. The pieces appear in place and fade, without flying. See the poses. Cost. Confetti is drawn as Skia shapes, not a shader: 0.1–0.5 ms of CPU time a frame while a burst plays, with almost no GPU time, and nothing between bursts. RenderScale doesn't apply. See What a layer costs. Room to fly. Pieces fly well past the host. A clipping ancestor (a ScrollViewer, a Border with ClipToBounds) cuts them, and later siblings cover them: leave room, and give the host a higher ZIndex if needed. See also Confetti API reference One-shots Fireworks and Sparkles, for other celebrations Pulse, a ripple from the press point

docs/effects/crt.html.title: CRT | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/crt.html.summary: CRT Crt shows the content as if on an old cathode-ray tube: a barrel bulge, scanlines, a color split, an aperture grille, a soft glow around bright parts, a bright bar rolling down the screen and a darker rim. Use it for a retro game screen, a terminal, a "live feed" card or a playful error page. It draws over the child and works on what is drawn there: the child, and whatever shows through it. Light Dark Add a CRT Wrap the content in a host. A picture or a dark screen with bright text suits it: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="18"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Crt Bulge="0.12" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="220" Height="130" Padding="16,12" CornerRadius="18" Background="#0B120E"> <TextBlock Text="CH 03" FontSize="15" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="#4ADE80" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Give it something to show The tube copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). Over the child, the default, that is the child and whatever shows through it. With a see-through child, the host becomes a screen over what is behind it, as on the gallery's home page, where a Border without a background shows a moving scene through the tube. Either way, something must be drawn there first: controls drawn after the host sit in front of it. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. Tune the tube Bulge sets the barrel bulge, Scanline the scanline period and ScanDepth how dark the lines are. Chroma is how far the color channels split, Glow the soft glow around bright parts, Vignette the darker rim and Roll the rolling bar: <fx:Crt Bulge="0.2" Scanline="2" ScanDepth="0.4" Chroma="1.5" Vignette="0.8" /> Keep the picture still The rolling bar is the only part that moves. With Roll="0" nothing moves, so the layer draws once and asks for no frames until what is under it changes: <fx:Crt Roll="0" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Bulge double 0.08 How far the picture bulges like a curved tube: the middle swells and the corners curve away (0: flat). Range 0–0.4. Scanline double 1.5 Scanline period. Range 1–8 DIPs. ScanDepth double 0.28 How dark the scanlines are: 0 none, 1 black between the lines. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Chroma double 0.8 How far the color channels split, DIPs. Range 0–6. Vignette double 0.6 How much the corners darken (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Glow double 0.35 The soft glow around bright parts, as a share (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Roll double 1 The bright bar rolling down the screen (0: none). Range 0–2. Feather double 2 How soft the layer's edge is, in DIPs. Range 0–16. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The tube has no randomness, so Seed doesn't apply; Speed sets the pace of the rolling bar. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the bar stops rolling; the rest of the tube stays. Cost: about 0.13 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card. See Performance. See also Crt API reference Chroma split, Glitch, Old film and ASCII Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/dither.html.title: Dither | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/dither.html.summary: Dither Retro, one-bit graphics: a tone (a ramp, a radial glow, drifting noise, or what is drawn behind the layer) is quantized into a few colors in square pixels, with an ordered pattern that turns shades into checkers and dots. Two colors give one-bit art; more give a small palette, like an old handheld's four greens. Use it for retro and game interfaces, posters and textured panels. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child. Light Dark Add a dither The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Dither /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="340" Height="190" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The default Bayer preset dithers a diagonal ramp into two colors. Presets and inputs Each preset brings a palette and sets Pattern, Input, PixelSize and Contrast. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset. Input picks the tone that is dithered. Preset Value Description Bayer (default) One-bit Bayer 4×4 over a diagonal ramp. Handheld Four greens, Bayer 8×8, over drifting noise. Grain One-bit blue noise over a radial ramp. Backdrop One-bit Bayer 4×4 over what is drawn behind it. Input Value Description Linear (default) A ramp across the shape along the angle. Radial Light at the center, dark at the rim. Noise Slowly drifting noise. Backdrop What is drawn behind the layer, by luminance: re-tones the content under the shape. Handheld drifts slowly in four greens. A label in the darkest green sits well on it: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Dither Preset="Handheld" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="120" Height="116" Padding="12"> <TextBlock Text="Handheld" FontSize="13" FontWeight="SemiBold" Foreground="#0F380F" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Use your own colors List the colors in Colors from dark to light, up to six. The darkest tones take the first color, the lightest the last: <fx:Dither Colors="#1B1530, #6D597A, #E56B6F, #FFD7A8" /> Choose the pattern and the tone Pattern sets how the shades break into pixels: Bayer2, Bayer4 and Bayer8 are ordered grids of 2×2, 4×4 and 8×8 thresholds, with more steps of shade as the grid grows; BlueNoise spreads the pixels evenly with no visible grid; WhiteNoise picks each pixel at random. PixelSize is the size of one dither pixel, in DIPs. The tone comes from Input: a Linear ramp along RampAngle, a Radial one (light in the center, dark at the rim), or drifting Noise sized by NoiseScale and moving at FlowSpeed. Bias shifts the tone lighter or darker before it is quantized, and Contrast spreads it: <fx:Dither Pattern="BlueNoise" Input="Noise" PixelSize="3" NoiseScale="140" Bias="0.1" /> Re-tone what is behind With Input="Backdrop" (or Preset="Backdrop"), the dither reads what is drawn behind it and redraws it in its colors, like a one-bit screen. Under the child (the default) it re-tones what is behind the host; with Placement="Over", it re-tones the child as well: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Dither Preset="Backdrop" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="120" Height="120" /> </fx:FXHost> Each dither pixel takes the average of what it covers. See Layers that read the backdrop for the limits. Properties Property Type Default Description Preset DitherPreset Bayer A ready-made look: sets Pattern, Input, PixelSize and Contrast, and the palette used while Colors is unset. Local values win. Values: Bayer, Handheld, Grain, Backdrop. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. Pattern DitherPattern Bayer4 The threshold pattern that spreads in-between tones over the pixels: an ordered Bayer grid, blue noise or white noise. Values: Bayer4, Bayer2, Bayer8, BlueNoise, WhiteNoise. Input FXToneInput Linear The tone that is dithered: a linear or radial ramp, drifting noise, or what is drawn behind the layer. Values: Linear, Radial, Noise, Backdrop. PixelSize double 2 Size of one dither pixel. Range 0.5–16 DIPs. RampAngle double 34 Linear input: the way the ramp runs from dark to light, degrees: 0 left to right; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Linear input. NoiseScale double 90 Noise input: feature size. Range 8–400 DIPs. Applies to the Noise input. FlowSpeed double 0.2 Noise input: drift speed. Range 0–2 per second. Applies to the Noise input. Bias double 0 Shifts the tone before quantizing. Range -1 to 1. Contrast double 1 How far the tone is stretched around its middle before quantizing: above 1 pushes it toward the darkest and lightest colors, below 1 toward the middle ones. Range 0.2–4. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Seed and Speed only matter with the Noise input. Still unless it is noise: only the Noise input moves. The others hold still and request no frames, unless what is behind a Backdrop dither changes. Text on a dither is hardest to read over the middle of the ramp, where the pattern is busiest. Put labels over its darkest or lightest part. Light and dark surfaces: the dither draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the noise holds one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.040 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. On the Backdrop input it also copies what is behind it. Leave RenderScale at 1, or the pixels soften. See also Dither API reference Halftone, the same tones as print dots ASCII, CRT and Grain gradient

docs/effects/dotgrid.html.title: Dot grid | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/dotgrid.html.summary: Dot grid DotGrid draws a grid of small squares or dots that flicker at random, each fading between levels: a quiet, technical background for a dashboard, an empty state or a sign-in page. Dots near the pointer light up and grow, and a press sends a ring out across the grid. It's a fill that draws only the dots, under the child, so whatever is behind the host shows between them. Light Dark Add a dot grid Put the host around the panel. A Transparent background on the panel lets the dots show through and makes the whole panel take presses, so a press anywhere sends a ripple. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost x:Name="DotsHost" CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:DotGrid x:Name="Dots" Spacing="12" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Height="220" Background="Transparent"> <TextBlock Text="No projects yet" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> To give the panel a color of its own, put that background on a container around the host. Shape the dots The dots are squares by default; IsRound="True" makes them round. Spacing is the distance between dot centers and DotSize their size, both in DIPs. MaxOpacity is how strong the brightest dots get at rest, and Floor the dimmest they get, as a share of the brightest. Lit dots go most of the way to full strength, whatever MaxOpacity is. FlickerRate is how often each dot changes level a second; at 0 the grid is still and asks for frames only while the pointer moves over it or a ring runs. <fx:DotGrid IsRound="True" Spacing="16" DotSize="2.5" Color="#94A3B8" MaxOpacity="0.35" FlickerRate="0" /> Light up around the pointer Dots within HoverRadius DIPs of the pointer (90 by default) light up and grow, and they ease after it as it moves. The host listens to the window's pointer, so this works over any part of the panel. Set HoverRadius="0" to turn it off. PointAt lights the dots from code, as if the pointer were there, for example around a field with keyboard focus. Pass null to let them go: EmailBox.GotFocus += (_, _) => { var center = new Point(EmailBox.Bounds.Width / 2, EmailBox.Bounds.Height / 2); Dots.PointAt(EmailBox.TranslatePoint(center, DotsHost)); }; EmailBox.LostFocus += (_, _) => Dots.PointAt(null); Send ripples With RippleOnPress on (the default), a press sends a ring out from where it lands; the dots it passes light up. RippleSpeed is how fast the ring travels, in DIPs a second, and RippleWidth how wide it is. A ring fades once it has crossed the shape, and up to four run at once: a fifth replaces the oldest. Ripple sends one from code, from a point in the host's coordinates or, without one, from the center: // New results arrived: ripple from the middle of the grid. Dots.Ripple(); Methods Call these to light the grid or send a ring from code: for keyboard focus, a guided tour, or an event in your app. Method Description Ripple(Point? at = null) Sends a ring out across the grid from at (host coordinates), or from the center. PointAt(Point? at) Lights the dots around at (host coordinates) as if the pointer were there; null lets them go. Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #7C8CFF The dots' color. Spacing double 10 Distance between dot centers, in DIPs. Range 3–60. DotSize double 3 Width of a dot, in DIPs; dots near the pointer or a ripple grow up to 1.8 times as wide. Range 0.5–30. FlickerRate double 0.8 Changes of each dot's level per second (0: still). Range 0–6. MaxOpacity double 0.5 How opaque the brightest dots are; dots near the pointer or a ripple go most of the way to full. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Floor double 0.15 The dimmest a dot gets, as a share of the brightest. Range 0–1 (0–100%). IsRound bool false Draws round dots instead of squares. HoverRadius double 90 How far from the pointer dots light up and grow, DIPs. 0: they don't follow it. Range 0–400. RippleOnPress bool true Whether a press sends a ripple out from where it lands. RippleSpeed double 420 How fast a ripple's ring travels, DIPs a second. Range 60–2000 DIPs per second. RippleWidth double 26 How wide a ripple's ring is. Range 4–120 DIPs. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1. Notes Light and dark surfaces: the dots are drawn in Color on any surface. The default blue reads on both; for other colors, pick one per theme. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: each dot holds one level, the lit dots jump to the pointer instead of easing, and presses send no ripples. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.05 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, among the cheapest layers. See Performance. Shared clock: fills run on one shared clock, so dot grids on different hosts, with the same settings, flicker in step. Pointer and presses: see One-shots and the pointer for how presses and the pointer reach a layer. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which paints only the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also DotGrid API reference Particle network and Topography, other quiet backgrounds Spotlight, which also follows the pointer Layers that follow the pointer

docs/effects/electric.html.title: Electric | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/electric.html.summary: Electric Electric draws lightning: a jagged bolt that strikes with a flash, holds, and re-strikes, mostly down the same channel, while earlier strikes linger as afterimages and forks shoot out and cool. It can crawl around the host's border, jump between two points of the shape, or run as a calm charged hairline. Use it for an overcharged or boosted state, a connection between two nodes, or a zap when something is pressed. It draws over the child. Light Dark Add lightning The default style, Border, runs lightning around the shape just outside its edge. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Electric Style="Border" Color="#4F8DFF" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="210" Height="50" CornerRadius="12" Background="#15171C"> <TextBlock Text="Overcharged" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Amplitude sets how far the bolt strays sideways, JagDensity how jagged it is, and StrikeRate how often it re-strikes. Gap moves a border bolt further out from the edge, or inside it with a negative value. Styles Value Description Border (default) Lightning crawling around the border. Arc Lightning between two points of the shape (From, To). Charged A calm, continuously crawling hairline with beads of charge: the UI variant. Charged sets a calmer set of values for the bolt (amplitude, density, strike rate, widths, forks, flicker, strands, gap, fork length and intensity) at template priority. Set any of them yourself to override it. <fx:Electric Style="Charged" Color="#7C5CFF" /> Lightning between two points With Style="Arc", the bolt runs from From to To, given as fractions of the shape: 0,0 is the top left, 1,1 the bottom right. Put the nodes it connects inside the host. <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Electric Style="Arc" From="0.1,0.5" To="0.9,0.5" Amplitude="6" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Width="230" Height="34"> <Ellipse Width="12" Height="12" Fill="#4F8DFF" HorizontalAlignment="Left" Margin="17,0,0,0" /> <Ellipse Width="12" Height="12" Fill="#4F8DFF" HorizontalAlignment="Right" Margin="0,0,17,0" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> Zap on a press Zap() fires a single strike: a flash, usually a re-strike, then an afterimage that fades. Set ZapOnPress to zap whenever the host is pressed, and turn IsContinuous off so the bolt only shows during a zap. On an arc, a zap at a point strikes from the nearer node to that point. <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Electric IsContinuous="False" ZapOnPress="True" Color="#A78BFA" CoolColor="#EC4899" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Zap me" /> </fx:FXHost> From code, call Zap() on the named layer for a strike along the style's own path, or pass a point in the host's coordinates: private void OnArcReleased(object? sender, PointerReleasedEventArgs e) { // ArcBolt is the Electric layer, ArcHost its FXHost. ArcBolt.Zap(e.GetPosition(ArcHost)); } Methods Method Description Zap(Point? at = null) One strike: a flash, usually a re-strike down the same channel, then the afterimage fades (0.5 s). On an arc, at (host coordinates) makes the strike jump from the nearer node to that point instead of between the nodes. Properties Property Type Default Description Style ElectricStyle Border Where the lightning runs: around the border, between two points, or a calm charged hairline. Choosing a style resets the bolt settings to its defaults (local values win). Values: Border, Arc, Charged. Color Color #4F8DFF The glow's color around the bolt; forks pass through it as they cool. CoreColor Color #EAF3FF The white-hot core of the channel. CoolColor Color #7A4DFF The color forks cool to. Amplitude double 5 How far the bolt strays sideways. Range 0–24 DIPs. JagDensity double 2.4 How jagged the bolt is: jags per 100 DIPs. Range 0.5–8. StrikeRate double 3.2 How often it re-strikes: about 0.55 / rate seconds between strikes. Range 0–10 per second. CoreWidth double 0.6 Width of the bolt's bright core, in DIPs. Range 0.2–3. GlowRadius double 5 How far the glow spreads around the bolt, in DIPs. Range 0.5–16. Forks double 0.55 Chance of forks at each strike. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Flicker double 0.45 How much the bolt's brightness wavers, and how bright its return strokes are (0: steady). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Arc and Border styles. Strands int 2 The live strike plus up to two afterimages. Range 1–3. Applies to the Arc and Border styles. Gap double 2 How far outside the edge a border bolt runs. Range -8 to 16 DIPs. Applies to the Border and Charged styles. ForkLength double 20 Length of the forks that shoot off the bolt, in DIPs. Range 0–80. Applies to the Border and Charged styles. Occlusion double 0.12 How much the glow also covers what is behind it. Range 0–1 (0–100%). From Point 0,0.5 Arc start, as a fraction of the shape's rect (0,0 top left; 1,1 bottom right). Applies to the Arc style. To Point 1,0.5 Arc end, as a fraction of the shape's rect. Applies to the Arc style. IsContinuous bool true Strike continuously. Off: draw only during a Zap. ZapOnPress bool false Zaps whenever the pointer is pressed on the host. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On lightning, Intensity is the strength of the light, up to 3. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the bolt adds light with a white-hot core. On a light surface its core becomes a crisp line in a deep shade of Color over a pale tint of its glow. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The continuous bolt holds one shape; a zap still strikes. See Reduced motion. One-shots. With IsContinuous off, the layer draws nothing between zaps. Zaps overlap; when too many are live, the oldest fades out. See One-shots. Cost. About 0.08 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. Electric builds its bolt paths on the CPU, so it takes more CPU time than most layers: about 0.06 ms a frame on the desktop. In the browser that work takes 0.45–0.6 ms a frame when interpreted and 0.12–0.3 ms when compiled ahead of time; compile ahead of time if the app leans on lightning and must run well on slower machines. See Performance. Room around the host. Bolts, glow and forks reach past the shape. A clipping ancestor cuts them off: leave room around the host. The border styles shade only a ring around the edge, not the interior. See also Electric API reference Fire, with its Plasma style around the border Beam, calmer light flowing between two controls Border beam, streaks running around the border One-shots and the pointer

docs/effects/fire.html.title: Fire | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/fire.html.summary: Fire Fire sets the top edge of the host's shape alight: turbulent tongues that curl, narrow and tear, a white-yellow base fading to red tips, and embers flung up to drift and cool. Use it for a trending item, a streak, a hot deal or a game-like moment. Heat is a low, warm version for buttons, Plasma a thin band of energy around the border, and Simulated and Smoke run a small fluid simulation for fire and smoke that rise, curl and drift with the wind. The flames draw under the child and rise above it. Light Dark Add flames The default style, Top, sends flames up from the top edge. Height sets how tall they are and Embers how many embers fly. Leave room above the host for the flames. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost Margin="0,90,0,0"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Fire Height="44" Embers="10" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="140" Height="58" CornerRadius="12" Background="#1C1917" Padding="12,0"> <TextBlock Text="Trending" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> LowColor, MidColor and HotColor are the temperature ramp, from the tips to the base. Scale sets the size of the turbulence, FlowSpeed how fast it rises and Warp how much it curls. Styles Each style sets its own colors, height, turbulence, embers and intensity at template priority. Set any of them yourself to override it. Value Description Top (default) Flames rising off the top edge, with embers. Heat Low, warm tongues for UI: a hot button or a streak. Plasma Contained energy hugging the border: a thin, breathing band of violet and ice-blue filaments flowing around it. Embers Embers alone, rising off the top edge. Simulated A small fluid simulation over the top edge: flames that rise, curl and tear into smoke. It carries momentum, so gusts and changes play out over time. Smoke Simulated gray smoke that rises, curls and spreads, without flames. Warm a button Heat is low and warm, with few embers: enough to mark a button without covering what is around it. <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Fire Style="Heat" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="104" Height="36" CornerRadius="18" Background="#FF5A14"> <TextBlock Text="Hot deal" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Simulated fire and smoke Simulated steps a small fluid grid above the top edge, so the flames carry momentum: a gust or a change plays out over time. Height is the height of the space the fire and smoke fill, Wind pushes them sideways (positive to the right), Buoyancy sets how strongly heat rises and Swirl how much the flow curls. Intensity is how much heat is fed in. Smoke is the same simulation with gray smoke and no flames. <fx:FXHost Margin="0,130,0,0"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Fire Style="Simulated" Height="120" Wind="0.4" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="40" CornerRadius="8" Background="#1C1917" /> </fx:FXHost> CellSize is the simulation's cell: smaller is finer and costs more. Properties Property Type Default Description Style FireStyle Top What burns: flames off the top edge, low heat for UI, plasma around the border, embers alone, or simulated fire or smoke. Choosing a style resets the other settings to its defaults (local values win). Values: Top, Heat, Plasma, Embers, Simulated, Smoke. LowColor Color #8A1405 The ramp's low end: the cool tips of the flames (deep red by default); in plasma, the glow around the band (violet by default). Applies to the Top, Heat, Plasma, and Simulated styles. MidColor Color #FF5A14 The ramp's middle: the body of the flames, or of the plasma band. Applies to the Top, Heat, Plasma, and Simulated styles. HotColor Color #FFC65A The ramp's hot end: the bright base of the flames, or the plasma's filaments. Applies to the Top, Heat, Plasma, and Simulated styles. Height double 54 Flame height; for plasma, sets the band's thickness with Sides; simulated, the height of the space above the shape the fire and smoke fill. Range 4–400 DIPs. Scale double 20 Size of the turbulence. Range 4–80 DIPs. Applies to the Top, Heat, and Plasma styles. FlowSpeed double 1.5 How fast the turbulence rises, in scales per second. Range 0–5. Applies to the Top, Heat, and Plasma styles. Embers int 16 How many embers are in the air at once (0: none). Range 0–40. Applies to the Top, Heat, and Embers styles. EmberRise double 58 How fast embers are flung up, DIPs a second; drag slows them to about a third of it. Range 0–200 DIPs per second. Applies to the Top, Heat, and Embers styles. EmberSize double 0.8 Size of an ember, in DIPs. Range 0.2–3. Applies to the Top, Heat, and Embers styles. EmberLife double 1.5 How long an ember glows, in seconds, on average; each lives 0.6 to 1.4 times this. Range 0.2–4. Applies to the Top, Heat, and Embers styles. Warp double 1 How much the turbulence curls the tongues. Range 0–3. Applies to the Top and Heat styles. Sides double 0.32 Plasma: the band's thickness, as a share of the height. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Plasma style. BaseGlow double 0.5 The fire's light on the edge it sits on. Range 0–2. Applies to the Top and Heat styles. Occlusion double 0.25 How much the flames cover what is behind them. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Top, Heat, and Plasma styles. Swirl double 0 A slow sideways swirl in the flames; faster flow in plasma; simulated, how much the flow curls. Range 0–3. Applies to the Top, Heat, Plasma, Simulated, and Smoke styles. SmokeColor Color #4A4A52 The smoke's color. Applies to the Simulated and Smoke styles. CellSize double 4 Simulation cell size: smaller is finer and costs more. Range 2–12 DIPs. Applies to the Simulated and Smoke styles. SmokeAmount double 0.6 How much smoke the fire gives off. Range 0–2. Applies to the Simulated and Smoke styles. SmokeOpacity double 0.55 How dense the smoke looks. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Simulated and Smoke styles. Buoyancy double 1 How strongly heat rises. Range 0–3. Applies to the Simulated and Smoke styles. Wind double 0 Sideways wind (positive: to the right). Range -2 to 2. Applies to the Simulated and Smoke styles. Cooling double 1 How fast heat cools into smoke. Range 0.2–3. Applies to the Simulated style. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On fire, Intensity is the strength of the flames, up to 3. Notes Light and dark surfaces. Fire reads best on dark UI. On a dark surface the flames add light. On a light surface the simulated flames draw as color over the smoke, and the procedural smoke veil and dim tips stay fainter. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The flames hold one pose and the embers stop; the simulated styles hold their current state. See Reduced motion. Cost. Procedural flames take about 0.23 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card, among the heavier layers; they only shade the area above the shape. The simulated styles take about 0.07 ms of GPU time plus the simulation step on the render thread, about 0.4 ms. In the browser the simulated fire takes 0.4–0.45 ms a frame plus 1.4–1.5 ms for its steps when interpreted, and 0.18–0.4 plus 0.35–0.8 ms when compiled ahead of time. See Performance. Room around the host. The flames and embers rise above the top edge, and the simulated box reaches Height above it and a little past the sides. A clipping ancestor, such as a ScrollViewer, cuts them off: leave room above the host. See also Fire API reference Electric, lightning around the border Glow, a steady light around the shape Heat haze, rising hot air to pair with flames Performance

docs/effects/fireworks.html.title: Fireworks | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/fireworks.html.summary: Fireworks Fireworks sends rockets up from the host's bottom edge that burst into a sphere of streaking sparks, which slow, fall, crackle and fade. Use it for a launch, a win or a celebration banner, or keep a show going behind a hero section. Shots are fired from code or on a press, or every so many seconds with Interval. They draw over the host and overlap. Light Dark Add fireworks Here a rocket goes up every 1.3 seconds over a night sky, and a press sends one more to the press point: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="10" Cursor="Hand"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Starfield Density="0.5" Twinkle="0.3" Speed="0.1" /> <fx:Fireworks Interval="1.3" FireOnPress="True" Count="80" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="360" Height="220" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The starfield is a fill, drawn under the child as its background, so the child here is an empty Border that only sets the size. Fire from code or on a press Fire(at) sends a rocket to burst at a point in the host's coordinates. Without a point, each shot picks a spot of its own in the upper half of the shape. With FireOnPress, a press on the host fires at the press point. private void OnLaunchClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) { // Three rockets across the banner. var w = BannerHost.Bounds.Width; foreach (var x in new[] { 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 }) BannerFireworks.Fire(new Point(w * x, 50)); } Fired shots overlap: up to six play at once, and one more drops the oldest. Keep a show going Interval is the time in seconds between shots of a running show. At 0, the default, rockets go up only when fired. A show keeps the layer drawing every frame, so set Interval back to 0, or IsActive to false, when the show is over. <fx:Fireworks x:Name="Show" Interval="0.8" Flight="0.9" Colors="#ffd23f, #ff4d6d, #4cc9f0" /> Shape the bursts Count is the number of sparks a burst, Power how fast they leave, Gravity how fast they fall and Size the thickness of their streaks. Duration is how long a burst lasts and Flight how long a rocket climbs (0: the burst appears at once). Each burst takes one or two of the Colors. Methods Call Fire to send a rocket from code. Method Description Fire(Point? at = null) Sends a rocket to burst at at (host coordinates), or at a spot of its own. Properties Property Type Default Description Colors FXColorList Unset Burst colors; each burst takes one or two. Unset: a bright palette. Count int 90 Sparks per burst. Range 8–240. Power double 1 Burst speed, as a multiple of a lively default. Range 0.2–3. Gravity double 1 How strongly the sparks fall after a burst, a multiple of the default (0: they don't fall). Range 0–3. Duration double 1.6 How long a burst lasts. Range 0.4–4 seconds. Flight double 0.7 How long a rocket climbs. Range 0–2 seconds. Size double 2 Thickness of a spark's streak, DIPs. Range 0.5–6. Interval double 0 Seconds between shots of a running show (0: only when fired). Range 0–10. FireOnPress bool false Fires a rocket wherever the pointer is pressed on the host. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. While IsActive is off, presses fire nothing. Notes Light and dark. On a dark surface the sparks add light; on a light one they show as color. A BlendMode other than Normal set on the layer takes over. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. There is no rocket: each burst appears in place and fades, without flying. See the poses. Cost. The sparks are drawn on the GPU as one batch of soft strips, 0.04–0.18 ms of CPU time a frame on the desktop. Without a GPU they are drawn as stroked lines. Between shots, with no Interval, the layer draws nothing. RenderScale doesn't apply. See What a layer costs. Room to burst. Bursts happen anywhere in the shape, and their sparks reach past it and fall. A clipping ancestor cuts them, so leave room around the host, or fire at points away from its edges. See also Fireworks API reference One-shots Confetti and Sparkles, for other celebrations Starfield, a night sky to fire over

docs/effects/flutedglass.html.title: Fluted glass | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/flutedglass.html.summary: Fluted glass FlutedGlass turns the host into reeded glass: parallel convex ribs, each a cylindrical lens that shows a squeezed, flipped strip of what is behind it, with a color split toward its edges, a sheen along its lit side and a shaded groove. Use it for a privacy panel, a decorative header, or a card that keeps a busy picture behind it readable. Like Glass, it draws under the child and shows what is drawn behind the host, so it needs something behind it and a see-through child. Light Dark Add fluted glass Put the host over the content it should bend, here a photo in the same Grid, and give it a child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <Grid> <Image Source="/Assets/photo.jpg" Stretch="UniformToFill" /> <fx:FXHost HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:FlutedGlass /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="220" Height="120" /> </fx:FXHost> </Grid> </UserControl> Presets Reeded has 14-DIP ribs; Fine has 6-DIP ribs that bend less; Frosted is reeded glass frosted at 0.6; Wide has 32-DIP ribs that bend further, with a stronger color split. A preset applies at template priority, so a local value wins over it. Value Description Reeded (default) Medium ribs in clear glass: the classic reeded pane. Fine Narrow ribs with a gentle bend. Frosted Medium ribs in frosted glass. Wide Broad ribs with a strong bend and more color split. Give it something to bend Fluted glass copies the region of the window behind the host just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). So: Something must be behind it: the page's background, earlier siblings in a Grid, a picture or a list. Over a flat color the ribs have nothing to squeeze, and only their sheen and grooves show. Text and sharp shapes behind it show the flip best. Keep the child see-through. The glass draws under the child, so a Background on the child hides it. Text on the child stays sharp on top of the ribs. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. Turn, frost and tint the ribs Angle turns the ribs (0 is upright, 90 lies them flat), Rib sets their width and Refraction how far each one bends the image sideways. Frost, Tint and TintAmount frost and color the glass: <fx:FlutedGlass Angle="90" Rib="10" Refraction="6" Frost="0.3" Tint="#FFFFFF" TintAmount="0.15" /> Like the other fills, fluted glass also has BorderWidth, which keeps the ribs to a band inside the edge, and UseMask (see Content masks). Properties Property Type Default Description Preset FlutedGlassPreset Reeded A starting set of Rib, Refraction, Frost and Dispersion; local values win. Values: Reeded, Fine, Frosted, Wide. Rib double 14 Width of a rib, in DIPs. Range 2–64. Angle double 0 Direction of the ribs, degrees: 0 upright; positive turns them clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Refraction double 9 How far each rib bends the image sideways, DIPs. Range 0–40. Frost double 0 How frosted the glass is: 0 clear, 1 a soft blur with lifted, richer color. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Dispersion double 0.15 Color split toward the rib edges. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Highlight double 0.5 Sheen along each rib's lit side. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Tint Color #FFFFFF A color the glass multiplies what is behind it by, as much as TintAmount says. TintAmount double 0 How much Tint colors the glass (0: clear). Range 0–1 (0–100%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. As on every fill, Intensity is the coverage, up to 1. Fluted glass is still, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Pick a Tint per theme with a theme resource (see Light and dark surfaces). Reduced motion: fluted glass has no motion of its own, so nothing changes. Cost: about 0.17 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, plus one copy of the region behind it. It doesn't animate: it redraws when what is behind it changes. See Performance. See also FlutedGlass API reference Glass, Progressive blur and Rain glass Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/fog.html.title: Fog | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/fog.html.summary: Fog Fog draws banks of mist drifting sideways across the shape, thickest at the bottom and thinning out toward the top of the bank. Use it for mood: a game's title screen, a weather card, a night scene. By default it goes over the child and hangs in front of the content; under a see-through panel, it's a background. Light Dark Add fog Put the host around a card. The mist drifts over it, clipped to its rounded shape: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Fog Height="0.7" Scale="90" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="236" Height="128" CornerRadius="14" Padding="16"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#1F2937" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#334155" Offset="0.6" /> <GradientStop Color="#0F172A" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <TextBlock Text="Morning mist" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="18" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Shape the bank Height is how far up the shape the bank reaches, as a share of its height (0.6 by default; 1 covers it all). Density is how thick the mist is, Scale the size of the wisps in DIPs, and Color the mist's color. <fx:Fog Height="1" Density="0.5" Scale="200" Color="#CBD5E1" /> The bank adapts to the shape, so the same settings work on a button and on a page. A short shape (under about 200 DIPs tall) gets a bank up to 1.6 times higher and a denser mist, so it still shows fog. And past 0.9 of the shape's height (0.6 on a short shape, and at least 24 DIPs), Scale counts only a quarter, so a small shape still shows separate banks. Set the drift DriftSpeed is how fast the mist drifts sideways, in DIPs a second: positive drifts right, negative left (18 by default). At 0 the banks stay in place but still churn slowly. <fx:Fog DriftSpeed="-40" /> Speed multiplies the whole clock, the drift and the churn, and DriftSpeed sets the drift alone; changing either never makes the animation jump. Unlike the fills, fog's clock starts when it first draws, so fog on different hosts doesn't move in step. Put the fog behind the content With Placement="Under", the mist sits behind the child instead. Leave the child without a background so the mist shows through it, and put the color on a container around the host: <Border Background="#0F172A" CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Fog Placement="Under" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="220"> <TextBlock Text="Night trail" Foreground="White" FontSize="24" FontWeight="Bold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" Margin="0,0,0,24" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </Border> Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #E8EDF2 The mist's color. Density double 0.75 How thick the mist is; at 1 its densest wisps are opaque. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Height double 0.6 How far up the shape the bank reaches (1: all of it). A short shape (under about 200 DIPs) gets up to 1.6 times this, and a denser mist, so a button still shows fog. Range 0.05–1 (5–100%). Scale double 120 The size of the wisps. Past 0.9 of the shape's height (0.6 on a shape under about 200 DIPs; at least 24 DIPs) it counts only a quarter, so a small shape still shows banks. Range 20–600. DriftSpeed double 18 How fast it drifts sideways, DIPs a second; positive drifts right, negative left. Range -120 to 120 DIPs per second. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed picks the shape of the banks. Notes Not a fill: fog has no BorderWidth or UseMask, and it runs on its own clock. Light and dark surfaces: the mist is drawn in Color on any surface. The default, a pale gray, shows best over dark or moody content and barely shows over white; over light content, pick a deeper color. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the mist holds still. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.25 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card. The cost grows with the area; the mist is soft, so on a large panel RenderScale="0.5" suits it. See Performance. See also Fog API reference Weather, rain or snow over the content Rain on glass, a misted pane with drops Light rays and Topography

docs/effects/frost.html.title: Frost | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/frost.html.summary: Frost Frost grows ice in from the shape's edges in feathery crystal branches, frosting what is under it: blurred, whitened toward Tint and dotted with glints. Amount is how far the ice has crept in, so a transition on it freezes or thaws the content. It melts in a ragged circle around the pointer and freezes back when the pointer leaves. Use it for a locked or paused state, a "cold" plan in a pricing table, or a wintry promo. It draws over the child, so it frosts the child and whatever shows through it. Light Dark Add frost Wrap the content in a host. A picture or colorful content shows the frost best: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Frost Amount="0.72" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="250" Height="150" CornerRadius="14"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#1E3A8A" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#7C3AED" Offset="0.55" /> <GradientStop Color="#F59E0B" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <TextBlock Text="Cold open" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="22" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Freeze and thaw Amount runs from 0 (no ice, and nothing drawn) to 1 (covered). Give it a transition, and every change glides: <Style Selector="fx|Frost"> <Setter Property="Transitions"> <Transitions> <DoubleTransition Property="Amount" Duration="0:0:1.2" /> </Transitions> </Setter> </Style> CardFrost.Amount = 1; // freeze CardFrost.Amount = 0; // thaw Melt it around the pointer MeltRadius is the radius of the clear patch around the pointer; 0 turns melting off. PointAt(at) melts the ice around a point from code, in the host's coordinates, for keyboard focus or a tour; PointAt(null) lets it freeze back: PlayButton.GotFocus += (_, _) => { var center = new Point(PlayButton.Bounds.Width / 2, PlayButton.Bounds.Height / 2); CardFrost.PointAt(PlayButton.TranslatePoint(center, CardHost)); }; PlayButton.LostFocus += (_, _) => CardFrost.PointAt(null); CrystalSize sets the size of the crystal pattern, Blur how frosted the content under the ice is, and Sparkle the glints. Methods Call PointAt to melt the ice without a pointer. Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Melts the ice around at (host coordinates) from code; null lets it freeze back. Properties Property Type Default Description Amount double 0.6 How far the ice has crept in from the edges; 1 covers it all. Range 0–1 (0–100%). CrystalSize double 22 Size of the crystal pattern. Range 4–80 DIPs. Blur double 6 How frosted: the blur of what is under the ice. Range 0.5–24 DIPs. Tint Color #DCECFF The color the ice whitens what is under it toward; the crystals take it too. MeltRadius double 60 Radius of the clear patch around the pointer; 0: no melting. Range 0–200 DIPs. Sparkle double 0.5 Glints in the ice. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed changes the crystal pattern; frost has no clock of its own, so Speed doesn't apply. Notes It frosts what is drawn before it.
