It copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). Over the child, the default, that is the child and what shows through it. With Placement="Under" it frosts only what is behind the host, and the child stays sharp on top. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. Light and dark surfaces: the layer knows the surface. On a light one the crystal lines darken a little, where white ice alone would vanish. Over a colorful picture in a light app they can all but vanish: set Surface="Dark" on the host, as the gallery does (see Light and dark surfaces). Reduced motion: the melt jumps to the pointer instead of easing, and appears and fades at once. Cost: about 0.63 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, including a blurred copy of what is under it. It doesn't animate, so it only redraws when what is under it changes or the melt moves. See Performance. See also Frost API reference Layers that follow the pointer Rain glass, Glass and Progressive blur

docs/effects/genie.html.title: Genie | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/genie.html.summary: Genie Genie hides the host's content by pulling it into a point, like a window minimizing into the dock, and pours it back out to show it. The sides bend in toward the point first, then the content slides down the funnel into it. Use it to send a panel to a dock icon, a file to the trash or a note into a folder. Like Reveal, it captures the content, hides the real element while it plays, and hands it back once shown. Light Dark Add a genie Set Target to the control the content goes into, and bind IsShown. Here the dock icon minimizes the note and brings it back: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <Grid RowDefinitions="*,Auto"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12" ZIndex="1" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Genie Target="{Binding #DockIcon}" IsShown="{Binding #DockIcon.IsChecked}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="176" Height="100" CornerRadius="12" Padding="12" Background="#15171c"> <TextBlock Text="Notes" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> <ToggleButton x:Name="DockIcon" Grid.Row="1" IsChecked="True" Width="32" Height="32" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,0,0,10" /> </Grid> </UserControl> The funnel draws outside the host on its way to the point. ZIndex="1" keeps the dock row, a later sibling, from covering it. Pull it into a control or a point The content goes into, and pours out of, one point: the point given to Hide(toward) or Show(from), in the host's coordinates; otherwise the center of Target, a control anywhere in the same window, such as a dock icon or a trash button; otherwise the bottom center of the content. With a Target, the funnel's neck is most of the target's width; without one it narrows to a small neck. For wide, short content, use a point well below it, so the funnel has room to bend. Genie works best on a card or a panel; bare text breaks into spikes. Show and hide from code IsShown is true by default and binds both ways, so Show() and Hide() also update a bound view-model property. Set IsShown="False" in XAML to start hidden, with no transition. private void OnDelete(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) { // Pull the card into the middle of the trash button. var center = new Point(TrashButton.Bounds.Width / 2, TrashButton.Bounds.Height / 2); CardGenie.Hide(TrashButton.TranslatePoint(center, CardHost)); } private void OnRestore(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => CardGenie.Show(); From a view model, bind IsShown to a property, such as IsNoteOpen, and set it to false to minimize the note. While hidden, the element is transparent but keeps its place in the layout, and it still takes clicks and keyboard focus. Duration is the length of one transition in seconds (0.6 by default); the layer's Speed doesn't apply, and a change applies from the next transition. With nothing to capture (no child, a child that isn't visible or isn't laid out yet, or IsActive off) the layer switches at once. To play it as a view opens, start hidden and call Show() from the view's Loaded event. Reveal shows the pattern. Methods Show and Hide play the transition from code, from or toward a point. Method Description Show(Point? from = null) Shows the content, playing the layer's transition from from (host coordinates). Null: the layer's own point. Hide(Point? toward = null) Hides the content, playing the layer's transition toward toward (host coordinates). Null: the layer's own point. Properties Property Type Default Description IsShown bool true Whether the content is shown. Setting it false pulls the content into the point; true pours it back out. Duration double 0.6 How long the transition takes, in seconds. Range 0.15–3. Target (Control, unset by default) is the element the content goes into, by its center, when no point is given. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Genie has no randomness, so Seed does nothing. Notes Light and dark. Genie draws the same on both surfaces: it shows the content as captured. Reduced motion. It becomes a fade of at most a quarter of a second. See the poses. Cost. Under 0.05 ms of GPU time a frame on a card while it plays, plus rendering the content once into an image when it starts. Otherwise it draws nothing. See What a layer costs. Clipping. The funnel reaches from the content to the point, outside the host, so a clipping ancestor between them cuts it: a ScrollViewer, or a Border with ClipToBounds. See also Genie API reference Show and hide transitions Reveal and Shatter, the other show and hide transitions Jelly, which squashes the content on a press

docs/effects/glass.html.title: Glass | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/glass.html.summary: Glass Glass turns the host into a pane of liquid glass: a beveled rim that bends what is behind it and splits it into color, a slight magnification, an optional frost, a specular rim facing the light and a soft drop shadow. Use it for floating toolbars, a now-playing card, or buttons over a picture or a moving scene. It draws under the child and shows what is drawn behind the host, so it needs something behind it and a see-through child. Light Dark Add a glass pane Put the host over the content it should bend, here a photo in the same Grid, and give it a child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <Grid> <Image Source="/Assets/photo.jpg" Stretch="UniformToFill" /> <fx:FXHost HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" CornerRadius="22"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glass /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="210" Height="96"> <TextBlock Text="Now playing" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </Grid> </UserControl> Give it something to bend Glass copies the region of the window behind the host just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). In practice: Something must be behind it. It bends what was drawn there first: the page's background, earlier siblings in a Grid, a list scrolling under it. Over a flat color there is nothing to bend, and only the rim light and the shadow show. It is at its best over a picture, text or moving content, and follows anything that moves there. Keep the child see-through. The glass draws under the child, so a Background on the child hides it. Put the label in a Border without a background, or a faintly translucent one. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. Controls drawn after the host aren't bent. They sit in front of the glass. Frost and tint it Frost goes from clear (0) to frosted (1). Tint and TintAmount color the pane; a dark tint suits a dark theme: <fx:Glass Frost="0.6" Tint="#1B1D22" TintAmount="0.3" /> LightAngle sets where the light that catches the rim comes from (-120 by default, above and to the left), and Rim how strong it is. Bring the glass in and out Presence makes the glass materialize by lensing: refraction, rim and shadow come in together. Animate it with a transition, here when a host with the toolbar class (<fx:FXHost x:Name="ToolbarHost" Classes="toolbar">) also gets shown: <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.toolbar fx|Glass"> <Setter Property="Presence" Value="0" /> <Setter Property="Transitions"> <Transitions> <DoubleTransition Property="Presence" Duration="0:0:0.4" /> </Transitions> </Setter> </Style> <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.toolbar.shown fx|Glass"> <Setter Property="Presence" Value="1" /> </Style> ToolbarHost.Classes.Set("shown", true); At a Presence of 0 the glass draws nothing and copies nothing. Properties Property Type Default Description Bevel double 14 Width of the beveled rim. Range 0.5–48 DIPs. Depth double 16 How far the rim bends what is behind it, DIPs. Range 0–48. Dispersion double 0.14 Color split at the rim. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Magnification double 1.04 How much the glass enlarges what is behind it: 1 not at all, above 1 larger, below 1 smaller. Range 0.8–1.6. Presence double 1 0..1: the glass materializes by lensing (refraction, rim and shadow together). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Frost double 0 0: clear; 1: frosted. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Shadow double 0.35 How dark the soft drop shadow under the glass is (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Rim double 1.6 Strength of the rim light. Range 0–3. LightAngle double -120 Where the light that catches the rim is, degrees: 0 to the right, -90 above; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Tint Color #FFFFFF A color the glass multiplies what is behind it by, as much as TintAmount says. TintAmount double 0 How much Tint colors the glass (0: clear). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Glass is still, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes It draws past the shape. The shadow falls about 5 DIPs down and fades out about 25 DIPs from the shape. A clipping ancestor cuts it: leave room around the host. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Pick a Tint per theme with a theme resource (see Light and dark surfaces). Reduced motion: glass has no motion of its own, so nothing changes. Cost: about 0.15–0.25 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, plus one copy of the region behind it. It doesn't animate: it redraws when what is behind it changes. See Performance. See also Glass API reference Fluted glass, Progressive blur, Frost and Magnifier Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/glitch.html.title: Glitch | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/glitch.html.summary: Glitch Glitch breaks the content up like a failing digital signal: bands tear sideways, blocks jump, the color channels split, a few rows flash in the glitch colors and scanlines show, changing in steps about 20 times a second. Use a short burst for an error or a denied action, or let it glitch now and then on its own for a "signal lost" screen. It draws over the child and works on what is drawn there, and draws nothing between glitches. Light Dark Add a glitch Wrap the content in a host. By default a press plays a short burst (TriggerOnPress is on): <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glitch /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Delete account" Padding="20,10" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Glitch on an error Turn presses off and call Trigger() when something fails. A burst covers the whole content, so it takes no point: <fx:Glitch x:Name="PasswordGlitch" TriggerOnPress="False" Duration="0.6" /> if (!await SignInAsync()) PasswordGlitch.Trigger(); Glitch now and then With IsContinuous, it glitches on its own, Frequency times a second on average. Duration and TriggerOnPress apply to bursts only: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glitch IsContinuous="True" Frequency="0.8" Displacement="18" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="230" Height="70" CornerRadius="12" Background="#0D0F14"> <TextBlock Text="SIGNAL LOST" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="20" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Displacement is how far bands tear sideways, Chroma how far the channels split, BlockSize the height of the thinnest band, and Color and SecondColor the colors of the flashing rows. Methods Call Trigger to play a burst without a press. See One-shots. Method Description Trigger() Plays a burst now (over the whole content, so it takes no point). Properties Property Type Default Description IsContinuous bool false Glitches now and then on its own, Frequency times a second on average. Off (the default): only bursts. Displacement double 16 How far bands tear sideways at full strength, DIPs. Range 0–80. Chroma double 3 How far the color channels split, DIPs. Range 0–12. BlockSize double 5 Height of the thinnest torn band, DIPs. Range 1–40. Duration double 0.45 How long a burst lasts. Range 0.1–2 seconds. Applies when IsContinuous is false. Frequency double 0.5 Glitches a second, on average. Range 0.05–4 per second. Applies when IsContinuous is true. Color Color #FF2BD6 One of the two colors thin rows flash in during a glitch. SecondColor Color #00E5FF The other color thin rows flash in; each row takes one of the two. TriggerOnPress bool true Bursts when the host is pressed. Applies when IsContinuous is false. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes It tears what is drawn before it. It copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop): the child, and whatever shows through it. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. It draws past the sides. Bands tear sideways past the left and right edges, by up to one and a half times Displacement plus Chroma. A clipping ancestor cuts them: leave room at the sides. A press must land on the host's child. A child with no background in empty areas doesn't take presses: give it a Background, even Transparent. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: a burst is a short, mild color split, and a continuous glitch stays still. Cost: about 0.11 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card while it glitches, and nothing between glitches. See Performance. See also Glitch API reference Chroma split, for a steady color split CRT, Shockwave and Jelly One-shots

docs/effects/glow.html.title: Glow | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/glow.html.summary: Glow Glow puts a bloom of light around the host's shape: a soft halo, a neon tube with a white-hot rim, or an aura of three colors flowing around the border. Use it to mark a primary action, an online status, a focused input or a prompt box. It draws under the child and follows its bounds and corner radius; the Mask style follows the child's own pixels instead, so text and icons glow letter by letter. Switched off, the light cools instead of cutting out. Light Dark Add a glow Put a Glow in the host's layers and give it a color. The host takes the corner radius from the child, so the light follows the button's rounded corners. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glow Color="#7C5CFF" Radius="16" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Generate" CornerRadius="24" Padding="40,12" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Radius sets the size of the bloom and Reach how far it fades out, in multiples of the radius. Hot sets how much of the white-hot CoreColor shows where the light is strongest. Styles Neon and Aura add a thin rim of light, as wide as RimWidth. The aura flows through Color, CoreColor and ThirdColor at AuraSpeed. Value Description Soft (default) Soft bloom around the shape. Neon A white-hot hairline rim with colored bloom on both sides. Aura A three-color spectrum flowing around the perimeter, with an inner rim light. Mask Bloom around the child's own pixels (text, icons) instead of its box. <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glow Style="Aura" Color="#7C5CFF" CoreColor="#EC4899" ThirdColor="#22D3EE" Radius="12" Inner="0.35" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBox PlaceholderText="Ask anything…" Width="270" CornerRadius="22" /> </fx:FXHost> Inner adds light inside the shape, toward its edge. Switch the light on and off Bind IsLit. When it turns off, the light shrinks, deepens and dims over Cool seconds; when it turns back on, it heats up over Attack seconds. <StackPanel Spacing="12"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glow Style="Neon" Color="#22D3EE" Cool="0.8" IsLit="{Binding #OnlineSwitch.IsChecked}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="84" CornerRadius="12" Background="#15171C" /> </fx:FXHost> <ToggleSwitch x:Name="OnlineSwitch" IsChecked="True" OnContent="Online" OffContent="Offline" /> </StackPanel> Glow around text and icons With Style="Mask", the light blooms around the child's own pixels rather than its box. Breathe makes it swell and settle every BreathePeriod seconds. <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glow Style="Mask" Color="#F472B6" Radius="10" Breathe="0.4" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="LIVE" FontSize="32" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="White" /> </fx:FXHost> The host captures the child when it changes. After changing something deeper inside it, call RefreshMask() on the host. See Content masks. Properties Property Type Default Description Style GlowStyle Soft How the light is drawn: a soft bloom, a neon rim, a flowing aura, or a bloom around the child's own pixels. Values: Soft, Neon, Aura, Mask. Color Color #7C5CFF The light's color. CoreColor Color #F4F0FF The white-hot core color. ThirdColor Color #22D3EE The aura's third color. Applies to the Aura style. Radius double 14 How wide the bloom is, in DIPs; larger is softer and spreads further. Range 1–64. Inner double 0 Light inside the shape, toward its edge. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Soft, Neon, and Aura styles. Occlusion double 0.15 How much the light also covers what is behind it. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Breathe double 0 Breathing amplitude (0 = steady). Range 0–1 (0–100%). BreathePeriod double 2.6 Seconds per breath, when Breathe is above 0. Range 0.2–8. Hot double 0.6 How much of the core color shows where the light is hottest. Range 0–1 (0–100%). AuraSpeed double 0.12 How fast the aura's colors travel around the border, in turns per second. Range 0–1. Applies to the Aura style. RimWidth double 0.6 Width of the bright hairline on the border, in DIPs. Range 0.1–4. Applies to the Neon and Aura styles. Reach double 4.5 How far the light reaches, in multiples of the radius. Range 1–8. Applies to the Soft, Neon, and Aura styles. IsLit bool true Switch the light on or off. Off, it cools over Cool seconds. Attack double 0.12 Seconds the light takes to warm up when IsLit turns on. Range 0.01–2. Cool double 0.6 How long the light takes to cool after IsLit turns off, in seconds: its heat falls to about a third in this time. Range 0.05–4. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a glow, Intensity is the strength of the light, up to 3. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the light adds to what is beneath it and its hottest parts turn white. On a light surface it draws as tinted haze in its own color. Very pale colors read weakly on white, so pick deeper colors for light themes. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The breathing and the aura's flow hold still. Switching IsLit off still cools the light, as a fade. See Reduced motion. Cost. About 0.06 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. A glow that doesn't breathe and isn't an aura draws once and then asks for no frames. See Performance. Room around the host. The light reaches past the shape by about Radius × Reach. A clipping ancestor, such as a ScrollViewer or a ContentControl, cuts it off: leave room around the host. See also Glow API reference Pulse, rings around the same shape; a glow and a radar pulse make a live status dot Ambient glow, a glow in the content's own colors Border beam, streaks of light running around the border Layers and hosts

docs/effects/grain.html.title: Grain | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/grain.html.summary: Grain Fine film grain inside the shape: specks a little lighter and a little darker than what is beneath them, one device pixel each. It adds texture to gradients, pictures and flat fills, and breaks up banding in soft color ramps. It draws over the host's child, and it is static by default, so it never shimmers and costs nothing after its first frame. Light Dark Add grain Put a Grain over a card with a picture or a gradient: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Grain Amount="0.09" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="340" Height="190" CornerRadius="16"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#7C3AED" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#EC4899" Offset="0.55" /> <GradientStop Color="#F59E0B" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The default Amount of 0.03 is subtle on purpose. Raise it for a stronger, more visible texture. Add grain to a fill Grain goes over the child and fills go under it, so a fill and a grain in the same host sandwich the content. This gives a mesh gradient a printed, analog look: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:MeshGradient Preset="Dusk" /> <fx:Grain Amount="0.05" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="116" CornerRadius="16" Padding="16"> <TextBlock Text="Dusk" FontSize="19" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="White" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Animate the grain Fps draws new grain that many times a second, like film running through a projector. At 0 (the default) the grain holds still: <fx:Grain Amount="0.08" Fps="24" /> Feather fades the grain in from the shape's edge, in DIPs. Properties Property Type Default Description Amount double 0.03 How strong the grain is: how far each pixel is lightened or darkened. Range 0–0.3 (0–30%). Fps double 0 New grain per second. 0: static. Range 0–60. Feather double 0 How far inside the shape's edge the grain fades in, in DIPs (0: a crisp edge). Range 0–24. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity multiplies Amount, up to 3. Seed picks a different grain pattern. Light and dark surfaces: grain draws the same on both. It reads best over a picture or a gradient; on a plain white card it all but vanishes. Reduced motion: animated grain holds still. See Reduced motion. Cost: among the cheapest layers, 0.019 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench, and nothing at all while static. Leave RenderScale at 1: the scale-up pass made grain slower (from about 0.07 ms to 0.10–0.19 ms on a 700×500 panel) and would soften it. See Render scale. See also Grain API reference Grain gradient, a gradient whose colors stipple into each other through grain Mesh gradient, Dither and Old film

docs/effects/graingradient.html.title: Grain gradient | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/graingradient.html.summary: Grain gradient A gradient with a printed, risograph feel: film grain scatters each point along the color ramp, so neighboring colors stipple into each other instead of blending flat, and a little brightness grain rides on top. It runs in a line, outward from a center, or around one (conic). Use it for buttons, avatars, cover art and posters. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child, or paints the child's own pixels with UseMask. Light Dark Add a grain gradient The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:GrainGradient Preset="Ember" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="220" Height="56" CornerRadius="14"> <TextBlock Text="Generate" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets and kinds Each preset brings a palette and sets Kind, Angle, Center and IsMonochrome: Ember is linear, Halo radial and Sweep conic, in color grain. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset. Preset Value Description Ember (default) A linear glow from deep plum through crimson and orange to pale gold. Halo A radial glow, pale blue-white above the middle, darkening through blue to near-black navy. Sweep A conic sweep from the top through teal, blue, violet, pink and amber, with color grain. Kind Value Description Linear (default) The colors run in a straight line across the shape, along the angle. Radial The colors run out from Center in rings. Conic Sweeps around Center, starting at the angle; loops. Pick the kind of gradient The colors in Colors run along the ramp in order, up to six: Linear runs across the shape along Angle: 0 is left to right, and positive angles turn clockwise. Radial starts at Center with the first color and runs outward. Conic sweeps clockwise around Center, starting at Angle (0 points right), and loops back to the first color, so there is no seam. Center is a point in fractions of the shape, from 0,0 (top left) to 1,1: <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="14"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:GrainGradient Kind="Radial" Center="0.5,0.35" Colors="#E9F1FF, #7AA2FF, #2A2F7A, #0B0D1F" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="80" Height="80" /> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:GrainGradient Kind="Conic" Angle="-90" Colors="#00C2A8, #3A86FF, #8338EC, #FF006E" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="80" Height="80" /> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> Tune the grain Amount sets how far the grain scatters the colors and their brightness; at 0 the gradient is smooth. GrainSize is the size of one grain in DIPs. IsMonochrome uses one grain value for all channels; turn it off for color grain. Fps is how many times a second the grain re-rolls, 12 by default; at 0 it holds still: <fx:GrainGradient Preset="Halo" Amount="0.7" GrainSize="1.5" Fps="0" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset GrainGradientPreset Ember A ready-made look: the palette used while Colors is unset, with its Kind, Angle, Center and IsMonochrome. Local values win. Values: Ember, Halo, Sweep. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. Kind GradientKind Linear The gradient's shape: linear, radial from Center, or conic around it. Values: Linear, Radial, Conic. Angle double 69 Linear: the way the colors run (0: left to right). Conic: where the sweep starts (0: to the right); it sweeps clockwise. Degrees; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Linear and Conic kinds. Center Point 0.5,0.5 Radial and conic center, 0..1 across the rect. Applies to the Radial and Conic kinds. Amount double 0.4 How far grain scatters the gradient and its brightness. Range 0–1 (0–100%). GrainSize double 0.5 Size of a grain, in DIPs. Range 0.5–8. IsMonochrome bool true One grain value for all channels; off gives color grain. Fps double 12 Grain re-rolls per second (0: static). Range 0–30. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Seed picks a different grain pattern. Idle: with Fps or Amount at 0, the gradient holds still and requests no frames. Light and dark surfaces: the gradient draws the same on both. On gradient text, pick colors that stand out from the background behind the text. Reduced motion: the grain holds still. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.073 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. Leave RenderScale at 1: it would soften the grain. Like every fill, it can paint only the child's own pixels with UseMask, or a band inside the edge with BorderWidth. See also GrainGradient API reference Mesh gradient, Grain and Dither Content masks

docs/effects/halftone.html.title: Halftone | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/halftone.html.summary: Halftone The look of print: round dots of ink on paper, laid on a rotated screen and sized by a tone, so dots grow and merge where the tone is dark and shrink to specks where it is light. The tone can be a ramp, a radial glow, drifting noise, or what is drawn behind the layer. Use it for comic and editorial styles, posters, retro buttons and textured cards. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child. Light Dark Add a halftone The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Halftone /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="220" Height="56" CornerRadius="14"> <TextBlock Text="Generate" FontWeight="SemiBold" Foreground="#1B1B1F" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> By default the tone is radial: light in the middle, where a centered label sits, and dark at the rim. Inputs Input picks the tone the dots follow. Value Description Linear A ramp across the shape along the angle. Radial (default) Light at the center, dark at the rim. Noise Slowly drifting noise. Backdrop What is drawn behind the layer, by luminance: re-tones the content under the shape. Set the ink and the paper InkColor is the dots' color and BackgroundColor the paper between them. DotPitch is the distance between dots, and ScreenAngle turns the screen; 0 puts the rows straight across, and the default is 45 degrees, as printed halftones are: <fx:Halftone InkColor="#1D4ED8" BackgroundColor="#FEF3C7" DotPitch="8" ScreenAngle="15" /> Shape the tone A Linear tone runs from dark to light along RampAngle; a Noise tone drifts, sized by NoiseScale and moving at FlowSpeed. Contrast spreads the tone, and Bias shifts it: a positive bias lightens it, which clears room for a label in the middle of a small button: <fx:Halftone Input="Linear" RampAngle="90" Bias="0.45" Contrast="1.5" /> Re-tone what is behind With Input="Backdrop", the dots follow the brightness of what is drawn behind the layer, each dot the average of its cell, like a newspaper photo. Under the child (the default) it re-tones what is behind the host; with Placement="Over", the child as well: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Halftone Input="Backdrop" InkColor="#111418" BackgroundColor="#F4EFE6" DotPitch="5" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="120" Height="120" /> </fx:FXHost> See Layers that read the backdrop for the limits. Properties Property Type Default Description Input FXToneInput Radial The tone that sizes the dots: a linear or radial ramp, drifting noise, or what is drawn behind the layer. Values: Linear, Radial, Noise, Backdrop. InkColor Color #1B1B1F The dots' color. BackgroundColor Color #F1ECE1 The color between the dots. DotPitch double 6 Distance between dots. Range 2–32 DIPs. ScreenAngle double 45 The dot screen's rotation, degrees: 0 puts the rows straight across; positive turns it clockwise. Range -180 to 180. RampAngle double 34 Linear input: the way the ramp runs from dark to light, degrees: 0 left to right; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Linear input. NoiseScale double 90 Noise input: feature size. Range 8–400 DIPs. Applies to the Noise input. FlowSpeed double 0.2 Noise input: drift speed. Range 0–2 per second. Applies to the Noise input. Bias double 0 Shifts the tone before the dots are sized: positive lightens it (smaller dots), negative darkens it. Range -1 to 1. Contrast double 1 How far the tone is stretched around its middle before the dots are sized: above 1 pushes dots toward empty or solid. Range 0.2–4. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Seed and Speed only matter with the Noise input. Light and dark surfaces: on a dark surface the dots leave a margin of paper at the edge, so the shape's outline still shows. See Light and dark surfaces. Text on a halftone: dots of either color can sit under a label, so give text a clear tone around it: ink-colored text where the tone is light, paper-colored text where it is dark. Still unless it is noise: only the Noise input moves; the others hold still and request no frames. Under reduced motion the noise holds one pose. Cost: 0.067 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. On the Backdrop input it also copies what is behind it. Like every fill, a halftone can paint only the child's own pixels with UseMask, or a band inside the edge with BorderWidth. See also Halftone API reference Dither, the same tones as square pixels ASCII, Color filter and Reveal, whose Halftone style brings content in as growing dots

docs/effects/heathaze.html.title: Heat haze | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/heathaze.html.summary: Heat haze HeatHaze makes what is behind it shimmer like hot air, wobbling in rising, turbulent noise. By default a column of hot air rises above the shape, as wide as it and strongest a little way up, so it pairs naturally with Fire. With WholeShape it fills the shape instead. Use it above flames, for an overheating warning, or on a summer or desert header. It bends what is already drawn there: the area above the host, or the host's own content. Light Dark Add heat haze Pair it with a fire: the flames draw under the child, so the haze, which draws over it, bends them as they rise: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12" Margin="0,100,0,0"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Fire /> <fx:HeatHaze Height="90" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="60" CornerRadius="12" Background="#1C1210" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Give it something to bend The haze copies the region it covers just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop), so what it bends depends on what is drawn there first: Something must be above the host: flames from a layer under the child, text, a picture or the page's own pattern. Over a flat color there is nothing to bend. The content goes first. Controls drawn after the host aren't bent: they sit in front of the haze. Leave room above. The column is drawn past the host's top edge, up to Height. A clipping ancestor, such as a ScrollViewer or a Border with ClipToBounds, cuts it. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. Here, as in the gallery, heat rises off a button and bends the line of type above it: <StackPanel Spacing="8"> <TextBlock Text="Hot air above" FontSize="28" FontWeight="Bold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" /> <fx:FXHost HorizontalAlignment="Center" CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:HeatHaze Height="100" Displacement="3" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Generate" Width="220" Height="56" /> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> Fill the shape instead WholeShape="True" puts the hot air over the shape itself, so it bends the child and whatever shows through it, and nothing above: <fx:HeatHaze WholeShape="True" Displacement="2" Scale="12" /> Displacement is how far pixels move, Scale the size of the turbulence, and FlowSpeed how fast it rises. Properties Property Type Default Description Height double 40 Height of the column of hot air above the shape. Range 4–200 DIPs. Scale double 9 Size of the turbulence. Range 2–60 DIPs. FlowSpeed double 2 How fast the hot air rises, in turbulence sizes per second (0: still). Range 0–6. Displacement double 1.1 How far pixels move. Range 0–8 DIPs. WholeShape bool false Fill the shape instead of rising above it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the haze holds still: what is behind keeps a fixed ripple instead of wobbling. Cost: about 0.15–0.25 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card. It shades only the column above the shape, not around it. With FlowSpeed or Displacement at 0 it doesn't animate. See Performance. See also HeatHaze API reference Fire, Shockwave and Chroma split Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/holofoil.html.title: Holo foil | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/holofoil.html.summary: Holo foil Holographic foil laid over the shape: rainbow bands that shift as the pointer moves across it, as if the foil tilted, with fine etched lines, glitter that flares as the angle passes each fleck, and a soft glare under the pointer. Use it for collectible cards, premium badges, membership passes and rare items. Unlike other fills, it goes over the host's child, so the content shows through the foil. At rest it holds still and costs nothing. Light Dark Add a holo foil Add a HoloFoil over a card, then move the pointer across it: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:HoloFoil /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="150" Height="200" CornerRadius="16" Background="#1D2140" Padding="14"> <StackPanel VerticalAlignment="Bottom" Spacing="2"> <TextBlock Text="RARE" FontSize="11" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="#C7D2FE" /> <TextBlock Text="Foil card" FontSize="17" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="White" /> </StackPanel> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The foil follows the pointer while it is over the shape, and settles back when it leaves. Tilt it from code PointAt tilts the foil toward a point in host coordinates, as if the pointer were there: for keyboard focus, a tour or an attract loop. Pass null to let it settle. The pointer takes over again when it moves. // CardFoil is the HoloFoil (x:Name="CardFoil") in the host named CardHost. CardFoil.PointAt(new Point(CardHost.Bounds.Width, 0)); // toward the top-right corner CardFoil.PointAt(null); Let it drift Without a pointer, on touch screens or in a list nobody hovers, Drift moves the bands on their own, in bands per second: <fx:HoloFoil Drift="0.1" /> With Drift at 0 (the default), the foil only moves with the pointer or PointAt. Make holographic text and icons With UseMask, the foil covers only the child's own pixels: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:HoloFoil UseMask="True" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="LEGENDARY" FontSize="32" FontWeight="Black" Foreground="#6366F1" /> </fx:FXHost> The foil tints the letters rather than replacing them, so give the text a color that already stands out on its background. Tune the foil Strength sets how strongly the rainbow tints what is under it, and Band the width of one rainbow band. Angle turns the way the rainbow runs, and Tilt sets how far the bands shift as the pointer crosses the shape. Glare, Glitter and Lines set the glare under the pointer, the flecks and the etched lines. On small controls, where the label is most of the shape, a fainter foil keeps the label readable: <fx:HoloFoil Strength="0.12" Glare="0.15" /> Methods Call PointAt to aim the foil without a pointer, and with null to release it. Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Tilts the foil toward at (host coordinates); null settles it. Properties Property Type Default Description Strength double 0.24 How strongly the rainbow tints what is under it; on a dark surface, how much light it adds. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Band double 140 Width of one rainbow band. Range 8–600 DIPs. Angle double 35 The way the rainbow runs, across its bands, degrees: 0 left to right (upright bands); positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Tilt double 1 How far the bands shift as the pointer crosses the shape. Range 0–3. Glare double 0.35 Strength of the soft glare under the pointer (0: none). Range 0–1.5. Glitter double 0.6 How bright the glitter flares as the angle passes each fleck (0: none). Range 0–2. Lines double 0.4 Etched lines across the bands. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Drift double 0 Bands per second drifting on their own (0: still until the pointer moves). Range 0–1. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Light and dark surfaces: on a light surface the bands are pastel colors that tint the content; on a dark one they are a thin film's cooler colors, cyan through violet to pink, added as light. See Light and dark surfaces. Pointer: the foil reacts while the pointer is over the shape. See Layers that follow the pointer. Reduced motion: the drift holds still, and the foil jumps to the pointer instead of easing toward it. Intensity is the foil's coverage, from 0 to 1. Speed doesn't change it; the foil moves with the pointer, and Drift sets its own pace. Cost: 0.060 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench, and nothing while it rests. See also HoloFoil API reference Tilt, which leans the card toward the pointer, and Spotlight Shimmer and Liquid metal

docs/effects/ink.html.title: Ink | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/ink.html.summary: Ink Ink fills the host's shape with colored fluid that answers the pointer. Moving the pointer pushes the fluid and leaves ink in a color that changes as it goes; a press throws a pinwheel splash of every color; and the ink swirls, spreads and fades. Use it on a hero, a playful empty state or a drawing surface. It draws over the child, inside the shape, and runs a small fluid simulation only while there is ink to show. Light Dark Add ink Put an Ink layer on a panel. It needs room to stir, so it suits a card or a larger surface better than a button. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Ink /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="320" Height="220" CornerRadius="12" Background="#0B0C12" Cursor="Hand"> <TextBlock Text="Move or press" Foreground="#8B90A0" FontSize="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" Margin="0,0,0,8" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Unset, the ink cycles through a bright set of five colors. Colors takes your own list, separated by commas: <fx:Ink Colors="#F43F5E, #F59E0B, #10B981" /> Tune the fluid Life is about how long the ink lasts before it has faded. SplatSize sets how wide each drop is, and Swirl how much the fluid curls into eddies. CellSize is the simulation's cell: smaller is finer and costs more. <fx:Ink Life="5" SplatSize="40" Swirl="2" /> Splash from code A press on the host throws a splash where it lands, because SplashOnPress is on by default; the press has to land on the host's content, so give it a background. Splash() throws one from code, at a point in the host's coordinates or at the center. PointAt stirs the fluid as if the pointer were there; null lifts it. // InkLayer is the Ink layer. private void OnMessageArrived(object? sender, EventArgs e) { InkLayer.Splash(); } Methods Method Description Splash(Point? at = null) Throws a splash of every color at at (host coordinates), or the center. PointAt(Point? at) Moves the ink's pointer to at (host coordinates), stirring the fluid along the way; null lifts it. Properties Property Type Default Description Colors FXColorList Unset The colors the ink cycles through; unset, a bright set of five. Life double 2.5 About how long the ink lasts before it has faded. Range 0.3–10 seconds. SplatSize double 26 How wide each drop of ink is. Range 4–120 DIPs. Swirl double 1.2 How much the fluid curls into eddies. Range 0–3. CellSize double 6 Simulation cell size: smaller is finer and costs more. Range 3–16 DIPs. SplashOnPress bool true Throws a splash where the host is pressed. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On ink, Intensity dims the layer and Seed doesn't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the ink glows as added light. On a light surface it draws as tinted haze. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The ink stays where it lands and fades. See Reduced motion. Cost. The simulation steps on the render thread only while there is ink; once it has faded, the grid clears and the layer draws nothing and costs nothing. While ink moves, about 0.02 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. See Performance. The pointer. The pointer stirs the ink while it is over the shape. See Layers that follow the pointer. Small targets. The ink covers the child while it swirls, so on a button or a field it hides the label. See also Ink API reference Water, the content under a rippling surface Trail, a ribbon or sparks behind the pointer Fire, whose Simulated style runs a similar fluid simulation One-shots and the pointer

docs/effects/innershadow.html.title: Inner shadow | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/innershadow.html.summary: Inner shadow InnerShadow puts light and shade inside the child's own shape, lit from LightAngle: pressed in (inset), raised (emboss), or pressed into the page with a fine highlight below (letterpress). Use it for an inset text field, debossed labels, raised icons or a soft, tactile look. It follows the child's pixels, not just its box: when the host captures the child, it measures how far each pixel is from the edge, so it works on glyphs as well as rounded fields. Light Dark Add an inner shadow An inset text field is the classic use. Wrap the field in a host: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:InnerShadow /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBox PlaceholderText="Ask anything…" Width="360" Height="52" CornerRadius="26" Padding="22,0" VerticalContentAlignment="Center" BorderThickness="0" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Styles Value Description Inset (default) Pressed in: the walls on the light's side cast a shadow inward. On a dark surface the far walls also catch a faint lip of light, so the recess still reads. Emboss Raised: the edges toward the light catch it, the far ones fall into shade. Letterpress Pressed into the page: an inset shadow, and a fine highlight just below the far edges. Press letters into the page On text, the shading follows each glyph. Letterpress presses the letters in and adds a highlight just below their far edges; Emboss raises them. Here the pressed letters are a gray just darker than the page: <Border Background="#DDE2E8" Padding="24" CornerRadius="12"> <StackPanel Spacing="6"> <fx:FXHost HorizontalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:InnerShadow Style="Letterpress" Depth="2" Softness="1.5" Shadow="0.5" Highlight="0.9" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="PRESSED" FontSize="40" FontWeight="Black" Foreground="#B8C0CB" /> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost HorizontalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:InnerShadow Style="Emboss" Depth="2" Softness="2" Shadow="0.5" Highlight="0.7" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="Raised" FontSize="30" FontWeight="Black" Foreground="#3B82F6" /> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> </Border> Move the light LightAngle is where the light comes from, in degrees: 0 from the right, -90 (the default) from above, positive turning clockwise. Depth is how far from an edge the shade reaches, and Softness how gradual it is: <fx:InnerShadow LightAngle="-135" Depth="8" Softness="4" ShadowColor="#1E1B4B" Shadow="0.6" /> HighlightColor and Highlight apply to Emboss and Letterpress. Properties Property Type Default Description Style InnerShadowStyle Inset The look: pressed in (inset), raised (emboss), or pressed into the page (letterpress). Values: Inset, Emboss, Letterpress. LightAngle double -90 Where the light comes from, degrees: 0 from the right, -90 from above; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Depth double 5 How deep the shape looks: how far from an edge the shade reaches, DIPs. Range 0.5–12. Softness double 7 How soft the shade's edge is, in DIPs (0: crisp). Range 0–12. ShadowColor Color #000000 The shade's color. Shadow double 0.4 Strength of the shade (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). HighlightColor Color #FFFFFF The color of the lit edges. Applies to the Emboss and Letterpress styles. Highlight double 0.6 Strength of the lit edges (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Emboss and Letterpress styles. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The inner shadow is still, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes It follows the content's pixels. See Content masks. The host watches only the child itself: after changing something deeper inside it, call RefreshMask. A field is captured again as it changes. Typing changes its Text, and a hover or focus style changes its brushes. While changes keep coming, captures are spaced about 100 ms apart, and the distance field is rebuilt once they settle. Depth is bounded. The distance field reaches 16 DIPs inside the edge, which bounds how far the shading reaches. Light and dark surfaces: the layer knows the surface. On a dark one, an inset adds a faint lip of light along its far edges, so the recess still reads. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: nothing moves, so nothing changes. Cost: drawing is cheap (about 0.03 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card) and happens once, since the layer doesn't animate. The cost is in the capture: building the distance field takes a few milliseconds on the UI thread each time the child changes, never per frame. See Content masks and Performance. See also InnerShadow API reference Outline, which strokes the same shape from outside Plastic, for a glossy or dished material fill Content masks

docs/effects/jelly.html.title: Jelly | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/jelly.html.summary: Jelly Jelly makes the element squash and wobble like jelly when pressed, then settle: a damped spring squashes it down and out and overshoots, while a bulge spreads from the press point. Use it for playful buttons, a "like" heart, toggles or game UI. While it wobbles, the layer draws a capture of the content in its place; the real content is hidden but still takes input, and it takes over again once the wobble settles. Light Dark Add jelly Wrap the control in a host. A press wobbles it from the press point (WobbleOnPress is on), and the control still gets its own click: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="26"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Jelly /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Press me" Width="190" Height="52" CornerRadius="26" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Wobble from code Wobble(at) wobbles from a point in the host's coordinates, or from the center with no point. Set WobbleOnPress="False" to wobble only from code, for example when a new message arrives: InboxJelly.Wobble(); Make it softer or stiffer Amount is how far it squashes at first, Frequency how many wobbles a second, Damping how fast it settles (the wobble shrinks by a factor of e every 1/Damping seconds), and Ripple the bulge that spreads from the press point: <fx:Jelly Amount="0.3" Frequency="3" Damping="1.5" Ripple="0.8" /> Methods Call Wobble to play the effect without a press. See One-shots. Method Description Wobble(Point? at = null) Wobbles now, from at (host coordinates) or the center. Properties Property Type Default Description Amount double 0.18 How far it squashes at first. Range 0–0.6 (0–60%). Frequency double 4.5 Wobbles a second. Range 1–12 per second. Damping double 2.5 How fast it settles: the wobble shrinks by e every 1/Damping seconds. Range 0.5–12. Ripple double 0.5 The bulge that spreads from the press point. Range 0–1 (0–100%). WobbleOnPress bool true Wobbles when the host is pressed. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The wobble runs on its own spring, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes It stands in for the content. When a wobble starts, the layer captures the content as it looks then and hides the real element, which keeps its place and still takes input. A change to the content during the wobble shows once it settles. With nothing to capture (no content, invisible, or not laid out yet), or while the layer isn't active, it doesn't wobble. The same stand-in is described for the transitions in Show and hide transitions. It doesn't read the backdrop. It works from its own capture of the content, so it needs nothing behind the host. It draws past the shape. The squash stretches the element sideways, by up to about 0.8 of Amount times half its larger side, and the bulge adds a few DIPs. A clipping ancestor cuts it: leave room around the host. A press must land on the host's child. A child with no background in empty areas doesn't take presses: give it a Background, even Transparent. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: a small, quick squash. Cost: under 0.1 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card while it wobbles, and nothing between wobbles. See Performance. See also Jelly API reference Shockwave, Pulse and Tilt Page peel and Shatter, which also stand in for the content One-shots

docs/effects/lightleaks.html.title: Light leaks | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/lightleaks.html.summary: Light leaks Light leaks brings warm film light in over the edges of the host's shape: four long, soft glows that drift along the frame and breathe in and out, whitening where they are hottest, with a faint, fast flicker. Use it on a photo, a hero card or a memories screen to give it a nostalgic, analog feel. It draws over the child, inside the shape, as added light. Light Dark Add light leaks Put the layer over a picture or a dark, moody card. The leaks show best where there is something darker for them to light. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LightLeaks /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="150" CornerRadius="14"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#2B1D16" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#51402F" Offset="0.6" /> <GradientStop Color="#1C2430" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <TextBlock Text="Summer '98" Foreground="#FFF3E0" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="22" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Color and size Color, SecondColor and ThirdColor tint the leaks; the defaults are warm oranges and pinks. Size scales the leaks with the shape, and Flicker sets the fast, faint flicker of film running through a gate (0 for none). Intensity makes the light stronger, up to 3. <fx:LightLeaks Color="#7C5CFF" SecondColor="#22D3EE" ThirdColor="#EC4899" Size="1.4" Flicker="0" Intensity="1.4" /> Light a dark picture in a light app The host picks its surface from its theme. In a light theme, light layers draw as tinted haze, which is meant for light content. When the content under the leaks is dark, set the surface yourself, so they add light as they do on a dark theme: <fx:FXHost Surface="Dark" CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LightLeaks /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Image Source="/Assets/beach-at-dusk.jpg" Width="300" Height="200" /> </fx:FXHost> Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #FF6A2B One leak's color; a fourth leak takes a mix of this and SecondColor. SecondColor Color #FFB547 Another leak's color. ThirdColor Color #FF2D6F The third leak's color. Size double 1 Size of the leaks, as a multiple of the shape's size. Range 0.2–2. Flicker double 0.3 A fast, faint flicker, like film running through a gate. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On light leaks, Intensity is the strength of the light, up to 3. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the leaks add light. On a light surface they draw as tinted haze. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The leaks hold still. See Reduced motion. Cost. About 0.1–0.2 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. The leaks move all the time, so the layer redraws every frame while it is active. See Performance. Inside the shape. The light draws only within the shape, so it needs no room around the host. See also LightLeaks API reference Light rays, shafts of light falling across the shape Old film, an old print with grain, scratches and flicker Grain, film grain over the content Light and dark surfaces

docs/effects/lightrays.html.title: Light rays | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/lightrays.html.summary: Light rays Light rays sends shafts of light across the host's shape from a source just outside it, like sun through a window: a fan of rays that shimmer and shift slowly, bright where they come in and fading with distance. Use it on a hero, a welcome card or a dark backdrop that should feel lit. It draws over the child, inside the shape, as added light. Light Dark Add light rays Put the layer over a darker surface or picture, where the light has something to show against. The host here uses the dark surface, so the rays add light even in a light theme. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14" Surface="Dark"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LightRays Angle="50" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="236" Height="128" CornerRadius="14" Padding="18"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#0B1220" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#1E293B" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <TextBlock Text="Good morning" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="20" HorizontalAlignment="Right" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Aim the light Angle is the way the light travels, in degrees: 0 to the right, 90 down, with positive angles turning clockwise. The source sits on the opposite side, outside the shape, by Distance (a share of the shape's diagonal). The default, 60, falls from the top left toward the bottom right. <!-- Light falling straight down from above the top edge. --> <fx:LightRays Angle="90" Spread="40" /> <!-- Light coming in from the top right. --> <fx:LightRays Angle="135" /> Shape the fan Spread is how wide the fan opens, in degrees, and Rays about how many rays cross it. Length is how far the light reaches, as a share of the shape's diagonal. Color tints the light and Intensity makes it stronger, up to 3. <fx:LightRays Color="#BAE6FD" Spread="90" Rays="16" Length="1.2" Intensity="1.5" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #FFF1D6 The light's color. Angle double 60 The way the light travels, degrees: 0 to the right, 90 down; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Spread double 60 How wide the fan of rays opens, degrees. Range 10–180. Rays double 9 About how many rays across the fan. Range 2–40. Length double 0.75 How far the light reaches, as a share of the shape's diagonal. Range 0.2–3. Distance double 0.1 How far outside the shape the source sits, as a share of the diagonal. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On light rays, Intensity is the strength of the light, up to 3. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the rays add light. On a light surface they draw as tinted haze, kept fainter because haze reads heavier. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The rays hold still. See Reduced motion. Cost. About 0.08 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. The rays shimmer all the time, so the layer redraws every frame while it is active. See Performance. Inside the shape. The light draws only within the shape, even though its source sits outside it, so it needs no room around the host. See also LightRays API reference Light leaks, warm film light drifting in over the edges Beams, shafts of light drifting sideways as a background Spotlight, a light that follows the pointer Light and dark surfaces

docs/effects/liquidmetal.html.title: Liquid metal | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/liquidmetal.html.summary: Liquid metal A slab of polished metal that reflects a photo studio: a bright sky above a soft horizon, strip lights and a dark floor, seen in a domed face with a rolled rim. The surface ripples and flows slowly. Use it for a premium button, a badge, an avatar, a metal border around a card, or a chrome logo. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child, or paints the child's own pixels with UseMask. Light Dark Add liquid metal The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LiquidMetal Preset="Gold" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="48" CornerRadius="24" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset sets Tint, LightColor, Iridescence and Contrast. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset; your value wins. Value Description Chrome (default) Bright, cool silver with a faint rainbow sheen. Gold Warm yellow gold under warm light, with no rainbow sheen. Rose Pink rose gold under soft, warm light. Gunmetal Dark blue-gray steel with deeper shadows, sharper highlights and a hint of rainbow sheen. Make a chrome border BorderWidth paints only a band inside the edge, shaded as a round tube, and leaves the middle clear for the content: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LiquidMetal Preset="Chrome" BorderWidth="5" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="48" CornerRadius="12"> <TextBlock Text="Chrome tube border" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Turn text or a logo into metal With UseMask, the metal paints the child's own pixels instead of its box, and goes over the child: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LiquidMetal UseMask="True" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="CHROME" FontSize="30" FontWeight="Black" Foreground="White" /> </fx:FXHost> The host captures the child to find its pixels. After changing something deeper inside the child, call FXHost.RefreshMask(); see Content masks. Pin the reflection to the window By default the reflection moves with the element, so every shape of the same size shows the same picture. With Anchor="Window", it is pinned to the window like a fixed studio light: neighboring shapes show one continuous surface, and the reflection slides over them as they scroll. <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="8"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:LiquidMetal Anchor="Window" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="56" Height="56" CornerRadius="12" /> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:LiquidMetal Anchor="Window" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="56" Height="56" CornerRadius="12" /> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> Shape the metal Tint is the metal's own color and LightColor the studio's. Flow sets how far the surface ripples, Scale the ripple size and FlowSpeed how fast they move. Bevel is the width of the rolled rim, Dome how curved the face is, and LightAngle turns the studio around. A still copper slab: <fx:LiquidMetal Tint="#D9915F" LightColor="#FFE8D6" Flow="0" Dome="0.3" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset LiquidMetalPreset Chrome The metal: sets Tint, LightColor, Iridescence and Contrast. Local values win. Values: Chrome, Gold, Rose, Gunmetal. Tint Color #E9ECF0 Reflectance at normal incidence: near white for chrome, warm for gold. LightColor Color #FFFFFF The studio lights' color. Flow double 0.3 How far the surface ripples (0: a still, polished slab). Range 0–2. Scale double 150 Ripple size. Range 10–400 DIPs. FlowSpeed double 0.35 How fast the ripples flow (0: frozen). Range 0–2 per second. Bevel double 14 Width of the rolled rim. Range 0–48 DIPs. Dome double 0.55 How domed the face is: 0 flat, 1 strongly curved; negative dishes it inward, like a keycap. Range -1 to 1.5. LightAngle double -7 Tilt of the studio around the view axis, degrees: 0 upright, its lights above; positive turns it counterclockwise. Range -180 to 180. Iridescence double 0.08 Rainbow thin-film color where the surface bends hardest (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Contrast double 1 1: studio as lit; higher deepens the floor and sharpens the lights. Range 0.5–2.5. Anchor FXAnchor Element Element (the default): the reflection moves with the element. Window: it is pinned to the window, so neighboring shapes show one continuous surface and it slides over them as they scroll, like a fixed studio light. Values: Element, Window. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1, so a transition on it fades the metal in and out. Text on the metal: the upper part reflects the studio's bright sky, and the middle sits on the horizon's dark reflections. With a light tint (chrome, gold, rose), dark text reads near the top, such as a card's title; centered labels read best in white. Light and dark surfaces: the metal draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the surface holds one pose. With Flow or FlowSpeed at 0 it is still anyway, and requests no frames. Cost: 0.312 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench, among the heavier fills. On a 700×500 panel it takes 0.73 ms, and 0.47 ms with RenderScale="0.5". See Render scale. Fills share one clock, so equal fills on different hosts move in step. See also LiquidMetal API reference Plastic, Holo foil and Silk Content masks

docs/effects/liquidprogress.html.title: Liquid progress | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/liquidprogress.html.summary: Liquid progress Liquid progress fills the host's shape with a liquid up to Level: for progress bars, gauges, and battery or storage levels. Its surface waves and bubbles rise through it, and a change of level eases in with a little overshoot and sloshes the surface. It is a fill, drawn under the child as its background, rising from the bottom or filling from the left. Light Dark Add liquid progress Bind Level, from 0 (empty) to 1 (full). Here a slider fills a tall glass: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="18" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="18"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LiquidProgress Level="{Binding #LevelSlider.Value}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="74" Height="150" CornerRadius="18" BorderBrush="#5a6170" BorderThickness="1" /> </fx:FXHost> <Slider x:Name="LevelSlider" Orientation="Vertical" Height="150" Minimum="0" Maximum="1" Value="0.6" /> </StackPanel> </UserControl> The liquid goes under the child, so the child has no background of its own: only a border line, and whatever sits on top of the liquid. Show progress Bind Level to a progress value from 0 to 1; values outside that range are clamped. Each new value eases in with a small overshoot, and Slosh sets how much the change stirs the surface (0: not at all). <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="22"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LiquidProgress Level="{Binding UploadProgress}" Orientation="Horizontal" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="240" Height="44" CornerRadius="22" BorderBrush="#5a6170" BorderThickness="1"> <TextBlock Text="{Binding UploadStatus}" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Orientation="Horizontal" fills from the left, for a bar; the default, Vertical, rises from the bottom. If your progress counts to 100, divide it by 100 in the view model or a converter. Color the liquid Color is the liquid near its surface, DeepColor the color it shades into with depth, and SurfaceColor the bright line along the surface, the wave behind it and the bubbles' rims. WaveHeight and WaveLength shape the waves, WaveSpeed sets how many pass a second, and Bubbles how many rise. <fx:LiquidProgress Level="0.42" Color="#10b981" DeepColor="#065f46" SurfaceColor="#6ee7b7" WaveHeight="6" Bubbles="0.5" /> For a liquid that stays still while the level holds, set WaveSpeed and Bubbles to 0: the layer then asks for frames only while a new level settles. Properties Property Type Default Description Level double 0.6 How full, 0..1. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Color Color #3B82F6 The liquid's color near its surface; it shades toward DeepColor further down. DeepColor Color #1E40AF The color the liquid shades to with depth. SurfaceColor Color #93C5FD The color of the bright line along the surface, the bubbles' rims and the wave behind. WaveHeight double 4 How tall the surface waves are, in DIPs (0: flat). A change of level makes them taller for a moment. Range 0–24. WaveLength double 120 Distance between wave crests, in DIPs. Range 16–600. WaveSpeed double 0.6 Waves per second (0: a still surface; with Bubbles at 0 too, no frames are drawn while the level holds). Range 0–3. Bubbles double 0.25 How many bubbles rise: the share of narrow columns that carry one (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Slosh double 1 How much a change of level stirs the surface. Range 0–2. Orientation Orientation Vertical Vertical rises from the bottom; horizontal fills from the left. Values: Horizontal, Vertical. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1. Notes Light and dark. On a light surface the wave behind the surface is drawn paler and see-through. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The level jumps to its new value, and the surface stays calm. See the poses. Cost. About 0.06 ms of GPU time a frame on a card. See What a layer costs. Shape. The liquid fills the child's bounds with the host's corner radius, so give the child the full size of the bar or the glass. BorderWidth fills only a band inside the edge, and UseMask fills the child's own pixels instead, such as the letters of a text; see Content masks. See also LiquidProgress API reference Waves, layered bands with rolling crests Water, a surface that ripples under the pointer Shimmer, a loading sweep for content that isn't ready yet

docs/effects/magnifier.html.title: Magnifier | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/magnifier.html.summary: Magnifier Magnifier is a glass loupe that follows the pointer over the host and magnifies what is under it, with a rim, a soft shadow and a slight color split toward its edge. Use it for fine print, charts, maps and product photos. It grows in when the pointer arrives and fades when it leaves, and PointAt aims it from code. It draws over the child and magnifies what is drawn there: the child and anything behind it that shows through. Light Dark Add a magnifier Wrap the content to magnify in a host: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Magnifier Radius="48" Zoom="2" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Image Source="/Assets/map.png" Width="480" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Choose what it covers It follows the pointer only over the host's shape. To magnify a whole panel, wrap the panel, not one item in it. It magnifies what is drawn before it. It copies what is under the lens just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop): the child, and whatever shows through the child's see-through parts. Controls drawn after the host sit in front of the lens and aren't magnified. The lens can reach past the shape when the pointer is near an edge. A clipping ancestor cuts it there. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. Aim it from code PointAt(at) holds the lens over a point in the host's coordinates, as if the pointer were there: for keyboard focus or a guided tour. PointAt(null) puts it away, and the pointer takes over again when it moves. This holds the lens over a label while it has keyboard focus: PriceLabel.GotFocus += (_, _) => { var center = new Point(PriceLabel.Bounds.Width / 2, PriceLabel.Bounds.Height / 2); ChartLoupe.PointAt(PriceLabel.TranslatePoint(center, ChartHost)); }; PriceLabel.LostFocus += (_, _) => ChartLoupe.PointAt(null); Size the lens Radius sets the lens's size and Zoom how much it magnifies. FollowTime is how long it takes to catch up with the pointer; 0 sticks to it. Rim, Shadow and Dispersion shape the glass: <fx:Magnifier Radius="80" Zoom="2.5" FollowTime="0.1" Dispersion="0" /> Methods Call PointAt to aim the lens without a pointer. Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Holds the lens over at (host coordinates); null puts it away. Properties Property Type Default Description Radius double 56 Radius of the lens, in DIPs. Range 12–200. Zoom double 1.8 How much the lens magnifies at its center: 1 not at all, 2 twice the size. Range 1–5. Rim double 1 Strength of the light on the lens's rim (0: none). Range 0–2. Shadow double 0.45 How dark the soft shadow around the lens is (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Dispersion double 0.2 Color split toward the rim. Range 0–1 (0–100%). FollowTime double 0.04 How long the lens takes to catch up with the pointer (a time constant). Range 0–0.5 seconds. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The lens follows the pointer, not a clock, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the lens jumps to the pointer instead of easing, and appears and fades at once. Cost: with the pointer away it draws nothing. While it shows, it shades only around the lens: about 0.08 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, plus a copy of what is under it. See Performance. See also Magnifier API reference Layers that follow the pointer Glass, Spotlight and Frost Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/meshgradient.html.title: Mesh gradient | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/meshgradient.html.summary: Mesh gradient A soft, living gradient: up to six colors, each pinned to its own point, blended smoothly into each other as the points drift slowly. The colors blend in OKLab, so the mixes between them stay clean instead of going muddy. Use it for hero cards, avatars, app backgrounds and gradient text. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child, or paints the child's own pixels with UseMask. Light Dark Add a mesh gradient The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:MeshGradient Preset="Dusk" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="116" CornerRadius="16" Padding="16"> <TextBlock Text="Dusk" FontSize="19" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="White" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset brings a palette and sets Sharpness, Drift and Warp. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset. Value Description Dusk (default) Deep indigo and violet with pink, orange and gold, like a sunset sky. Lagoon Deep blue, teal and pale aqua, like shallow tropical water. Orchid Six soft pinks, mauves, peach and slate blue, with crisper blends. Graphite Near-black and slate grays that drift less. Use your own colors Colors takes up to six colors, separated by commas, semicolons or spaces.
