Set, it replaces the preset's palette: <fx:MeshGradient Colors="#0B3D5C, #2EC4B6, #CBF3F0, #1B6CA8" /> Each color has a place in the shape, which its point drifts around: the first near the top-left corner, the second near the top-right, the third in the middle, the fourth near the bottom-left, the fifth near the bottom-right, and the sixth above and right of the middle. The points sit at fractions of the shape, so the gradient stretches with the host. From code, set an FXColorList: // Hero is the MeshGradient (x:Name="Hero"). Set Colors to null to go back to the preset's palette. Hero.Colors = FXColorList.Parse("#7c3aed, #ec4899, #f59e0b"); Make gradient text With UseMask, the gradient paints only the letters and goes over them. Choose colors that stand out from the background behind the text: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:MeshGradient UseMask="True" Colors="#7C3AED, #EC4899, #F59E0B, #22D3EE" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="Aurora" FontSize="46" FontWeight="Black" Foreground="White" /> </fx:FXHost> After changing something deeper inside the child, call FXHost.RefreshMask(); see Content masks. Make avatars and borders A CornerRadius of 999 on the host makes a circle. BorderWidth paints only a band inside the edge, for a gradient ring or border: <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="14"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:MeshGradient Preset="Lagoon" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="80" Height="80" /> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:MeshGradient Preset="Orchid" BorderWidth="4" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="80" Height="80" /> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> Shape the blend Drift sets how far the points wander from their places, as a share of the shape, and FlowSpeed how fast. Sharpness goes from wide, soft blends (1) to colors that keep to their own regions (higher). Warp bends the whole field gently with noise: <fx:MeshGradient Preset="Orchid" Drift="0.2" FlowSpeed="0.1" Sharpness="3" Warp="0.8" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset MeshGradientPreset Dusk The palette used while Colors is unset, with matching Sharpness, Drift and Warp. Local values win. Values: Dusk, Lagoon, Orchid, Graphite. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. Drift double 0.12 How far the points wander from rest, as a fraction of the rect. Range 0–0.5 (0–50%). FlowSpeed double 0.25 How fast the points drift and the warp moves (0: still). Range 0–2 per second. Sharpness double 1.6 1: wide soft blends; higher keeps each color to its own region. Range 0.5–6. Warp double 0.35 A gentle noise warp of the whole field. Range 0–2. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1, so a transition on it fades the gradient in and out. Seed changes how the points wander. Still gradients: with FlowSpeed at 0, or both Drift and Warp at 0, the gradient holds still and requests no frames. Light and dark surfaces: the gradient draws the same on both. Pick the text color by the color nearest the text. Reduced motion: the gradient holds one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.103 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. See Performance. Fills share one clock, so equal gradients on different hosts move in step. See also MeshGradient API reference Grain gradient, Swirl and Waves Grain, to add texture over the gradient Content masks

docs/effects/metaballs.html.title: Metaballs | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/metaballs.html.summary: Metaballs Glossy blobs that drift on slow paths and merge where they meet, like a lava lamp, over a base color. Each blob takes one of the colors in turn and has a soft sheen along its rim. Use it for playful cards, music and media tiles, splash screens and ambient backgrounds. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape, background included, and goes under the child. Light Dark Add metaballs The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Metaballs Preset="Lava" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="340" Height="190" CornerRadius="16" Padding="20"> <TextBlock Text="Weekly report" FontSize="17" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="White" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset brings a palette and sets BackgroundColor: Lava is warm reds and oranges on a deep plum, Mint cool greens and cyans on a deep teal. Set either yourself to adjust a preset. Value Description Lava (default) Red, orange and hot-pink blobs on dark plum, like a lava lamp. Mint Mint, aqua and lime blobs on a dark teal base. Use your own colors The blobs take the colors in Colors in turn, up to six, over BackgroundColor: <fx:Metaballs Colors="#A78BFA, #F472B6, #38BDF8" BackgroundColor="#0F0A1F" /> Pick the text color by the background: light text over a dark BackgroundColor, dark text over a light one. Shape the blobs Count sets how many blobs there are, from 1 to 8. Size sets their size relative to the shape, so the blobs fill a small badge and a large panel alike: at 0.2 they cover about two fifths of the shape. Gloss is the sheen on the blobs, and FlowSpeed how fast they drift: <fx:Metaballs Preset="Mint" Count="4" Size="0.3" Gloss="0.8" FlowSpeed="0.2" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset MetaballsPreset Lava The blob palette used while Colors is unset, with a matching BackgroundColor. Values: Lava, Mint. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. BackgroundColor Color #1A0F1F The base color behind the blobs. Count int 6 How many blobs. Range 1–8. Size double 0.2 Blob size, for any shape: the radius is 1.8 × Size times the side of the square each blob has to itself (the square root of the shape's area over the count), and at most half the shorter side. At 0.2 the blobs cover about two fifths of the shape. Range 0.05–0.5 (5–50%). FlowSpeed double 0.4 How fast the blobs drift (0: still). Range 0–2 per second. Gloss double 0.5 Sheen on the blobs. Range 0–1 (0–100%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1, so a transition on it fades the fill in and out. Still blobs: with FlowSpeed at 0, the blobs hold still and the layer requests no frames. Light and dark surfaces: the blobs draw the same on both; BackgroundColor sets the base under them. Reduced motion: the blobs hold one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.097 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. See Performance. Like every fill, metaballs can paint a band inside the edge with BorderWidth, or only the child's own pixels with UseMask. See also Metaballs API reference Voronoi, Bokeh and Mesh gradient Voice orb, another living blob of color

docs/effects/motionblur.html.title: Motion blur | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/motionblur.html.summary: Motion blur Motion blur draws a smear of the host's content along its motion, behind it, while the host moves: a slide-in, a drag, a fling, a transform animation. It reads how the host moves in its window every frame, so any movement counts, whatever moves it. Still, it draws nothing. The content itself stays sharp; the smear trails behind it like a wake. Light Dark Add motion blur Add the layer to a host that moves. Here an animation slides the host back and forth: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.RenderTransform> <TranslateTransform /> </fx:FXHost.RenderTransform> <fx:FXHost.Styles> <Style Selector="fx|FXHost"> <Style.Animations> <Animation Duration="0:0:1.2" IterationCount="INFINITE" PlaybackDirection="Alternate" Easing="SineEaseInOut"> <KeyFrame Cue="0%"><Setter Property="TranslateTransform.X" Value="-80" /></KeyFrame> <KeyFrame Cue="100%"><Setter Property="TranslateTransform.X" Value="80" /></KeyFrame> </Animation> </Style.Animations> </Style> </fx:FXHost.Styles> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:MotionBlur Shutter="0.06" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="110" Height="70" CornerRadius="14" Background="#3b82f6"> <TextBlock Text="Swoosh" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Smear a slide-in Anything that moves the host works: a transition on its RenderTransform, a change of Canvas.Left, a drag, a layout change, or a parent that moves. This drawer slides in with a transition: <fx:FXHost x:Name="Drawer" RenderTransform="translateX(-320px)"> <fx:FXHost.Transitions> <Transitions> <TransformOperationsTransition Property="RenderTransform" Duration="0:0:0.35" Easing="CubicEaseOut" /> </Transitions> </fx:FXHost.Transitions> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:MotionBlur /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="300" Height="400" Background="#15171c" /> </fx:FXHost> // using Avalonia.Media.Transformation; Drawer.RenderTransform = TransformOperations.Parse("translateX(0px)"); Tune the smear Shutter is how long the virtual shutter stays open, in seconds: longer smears further. MaxLength caps the smear in DIPs, and Strength sets how strongly it shows. <fx:MotionBlur Shutter="0.08" MaxLength="160" Strength="0.6" /> The smear is drawn from a capture of the content, which the host takes again when the content changes. After changing something deep inside it, call RefreshMask() on the host; see Content masks. Properties Property Type Default Description Shutter double 0.05 How long the virtual shutter stays open: longer smears further. Range 0.005–0.2 seconds. Strength double 0.75 How opaque the smear is (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). MaxLength double 120 The longest smear. Range 4–400 DIPs. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Motion blur follows the host, not a clock, so Speed and Seed do nothing. Notes Scrolling counts. A host in a scrolling list smears while the list scrolls. Set IsActive to false where that isn't wanted. Room behind it. The smear is drawn behind the content and reaches up to MaxLength past the host, so a clipping ancestor cuts it. Light and dark. It draws the same on both surfaces, in the content's own colors. Reduced motion. It draws nothing. See Reduced motion. Cost. About 0.15 ms of GPU time a frame while the host moves, and nothing once it stops. See What a layer costs. See also MotionBlur API reference Trail, a ribbon or sparks behind the pointer Tilt, which moves its host toward the pointer Content masks

docs/effects/oldfilm.html.title: Old film | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/oldfilm.html.summary: Old film OldFilm shows the content as an old print running through a projector: toned toward sepia, darker at the corners and grained, weaving a little in the gate and flickering at 18 frames a second, with scratches that run down it for a few frames and specks of dust that come and go. Use it for a "memories" card, a throwback hero, a retro photo viewer or a silent-movie title. It draws over the child and works on what is drawn there: the child, and whatever shows through it. Light Dark Add old film Wrap the content in a host. A photo, with tones from deep shadow to bright highlights, shows it best; a gradient works too: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:OldFilm /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="236" Height="128" CornerRadius="14"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#0EA5E9" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#22C55E" Offset="0.5" /> <GradientStop Color="#FACC15" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <TextBlock Text="The Lodger" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="22" HorizontalAlignment="Center" /> <TextBlock Text="1927" Foreground="White" FontSize="13" HorizontalAlignment="Center" /> </StackPanel> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Give it a picture The film copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop): the child, and whatever shows through it. With a see-through child, it shows what is behind the host as film. Either way, something must be drawn there first: controls drawn after the host sit in front of it. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. Tone the print Tint is the color the picture is toned toward, and Sepia how much: at 0 the picture keeps its own colors under the grain, flicker and scratches. A cooler tint gives a cyanotype: <fx:OldFilm Tint="#6B8FC9" Sepia="0.8" /> Wear and tear Grain, Flicker, Scratches and Dust run from 0 (none) to 1; Vignette darkens the corners and Weave is how far the picture moves in the gate. A lightly worn print: <fx:OldFilm Grain="0.3" Flicker="0.2" Scratches="0.15" Dust="0.2" Weave="0.5" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Tint Color #C9A36B The color the picture is toned toward. Sepia double 1 How far the picture is toned toward Tint, keeping its lightness (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Vignette double 0.6 How much the corners darken (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Grain double 0.5 How strong the film grain is (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Flicker double 0.5 How much each frame's brightness jumps (0: steady). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Scratches double 0.5 How often scratches run down the picture (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Dust double 0.5 How many specks of dust come and go (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Weave double 1.2 How far the picture weaves in the gate. Range 0–6 DIPs. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed changes where the scratches and dust fall. Notes The projector keeps its own pace. The weave, flicker, scratches, dust and grain step at 18 frames a second, whatever the display runs at. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: it holds one frame. Cost: about 0.17 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card. It animates, so it redraws while it is visible. See Performance. See also OldFilm API reference Color filter with Preset="Sepia", for a still sepia tone Grain, CRT and Light leaks Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/outline.html.title: Outline | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/outline.html.summary: Outline Outline strokes the child's own shape at an exact width: the letters of a label, an icon, a cut-out picture or any control. Use it for outlined display type, a ring around a selected icon, or a die-cut sticker with a soft shadow. It follows the child's pixels, not its box: when the host captures the child, it measures how far each pixel is from the edge, so the stroke keeps its width around any shape. Light Dark Add an outline Wrap the content in a host. Bare text shows the effect best: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Outline Color="#7C3AED" Width="3" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="Nova FX" FontSize="40" FontWeight="Black" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Styles Value Description Stroke (default) A band of an exact width around the content. Sticker A thick border with a soft shadow under it, as if cut out and stuck on the page. Make a sticker Style="Sticker" draws a thick border with a soft shadow under it, as if the content were cut out and stuck on the page. Switching to it sets Width to 6 at template priority, so a local Width still wins. ShadowColor, ShadowOffset (how far the shadow falls below) and ShadowBlur shape the shadow: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Outline Style="Sticker" ShadowOffset="4" ShadowBlur="8" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="hello!" FontSize="44" FontWeight="Black" Foreground="#EC4899" /> </fx:FXHost> Stroke outside or over the edge A stroke sits outside the content by default (Position="Outside"), so the content keeps its own size, and the layer draws under the child. Position="Center" puts the stroke half in and half out of the edge, and the layer draws over the child. Softness fades the stroke's edge: <fx:Outline Position="Center" Color="#22D3EE" Width="2" Softness="0.5" /> Position applies to the Stroke style only. Keep it in step with the content The host captures the child again when one of the child's own properties changes, but it doesn't watch the child's descendants. After changing something deeper inside it, call RefreshMask: // BadgeText is a TextBlock inside the StackPanel that is the host's child. BadgeText.Text = "PRO"; BadgeHost.RefreshMask(); Properties Property Type Default Description Style OutlineStyle Stroke A plain stroke, or a sticker: a thick border with a soft shadow. Choosing a style sets Width to 3 or 6 DIPs (a local value wins). Values: Stroke, Sticker. Color Color #FFFFFF The stroke's color; its alpha is the stroke's opacity. Width double 3 Width of the stroke, in DIPs. Range 0.5–24. Softness double 0 How far the stroke's edge fades, DIPs (0: crisp). Range 0–8. Position OutlinePosition Outside Whether the stroke sits outside the content or centered on its edge. Applies to the Stroke style. Values: Outside, Center. ShadowColor Color #5A000000 The color of the sticker's shadow; its alpha is how dark the shadow is. Applies to the Sticker style. ShadowOffset double 3 How far the sticker's shadow falls below it. Range 0–12 DIPs. Applies to the Sticker style. ShadowBlur double 6 How soft the sticker's shadow is, in DIPs. Range 0–16. Applies to the Sticker style. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The outline is still, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes It follows the content's pixels. See Content masks. A pixel counts as inside when its alpha is at least half the child's own strongest alpha, so text in a translucent color still has a shape. Width is bounded. The distance field reaches 47.75 DIPs outside the edge; Width is kept to 24 DIPs so the stroke and a sticker's shadow stay within it. It draws past the child's box by the stroke's width, plus the shadow for a sticker. A clipping ancestor, such as a ScrollViewer or a Border with ClipToBounds, cuts it: leave room around the host. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. A white outline vanishes on a white page or around white text; the gallery uses #7C3AED on light and #A78BFA on dark, from a theme resource (see Light and dark surfaces). Reduced motion: nothing moves, so nothing changes. Cost: drawing is cheap (about 0.01 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, 0.03 ms for a sticker) and happens once, since the outline doesn't animate. The cost is in the capture: building the distance field takes a few milliseconds on the UI thread each time the child changes, never per frame. See Content masks and Performance. See also Outline API reference Inner shadow, which shades the inside of the same shape Glow with Style="Mask", for a soft bloom around the content instead of a hard stroke Content masks

docs/effects/pagepeel.html.title: Page peel | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/pagepeel.html.summary: Page peel Page peel curls a corner of the element up when it is hovered, like a sticker or a page, showing its back with a shadow under the curl. It peels further as the pointer nears the corner and settles back when the pointer leaves. Use it on stickers, notes and cards, or as a hint that there is more underneath. While peeled, the layer draws a capture of the content over it. Light Dark Add a page peel Add the layer to a host around the element; hover it to peel: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:PagePeel Amount="0.22" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="120" CornerRadius="16" Background="#f97316"> <TextBlock Text="Sticker" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="18" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Hold it peeled IsPeeled holds the corner peeled without a hover, for example while a card has notes on its back: <fx:PagePeel x:Name="CardPeel" IsPeeled="{Binding HasNotes}" /> private void OnTogglePeel(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => CardPeel.IsPeeled = !CardPeel.IsPeeled; A peel set in XAML before the content is laid out waits for the first layout pass, then peels. Hovering still peels while IsPeeled is false; the corner settles back when neither holds it. Pick the corner and the curl Corner picks the corner that curls (BottomRight by default). Amount is how far it peels on hover, as a share of the shape's diagonal, and CurlRadius the largest radius of the curl. BackColor colors the back, and Shadow sets the strength of the shadow the curl casts. <fx:PagePeel Corner="TopRight" Amount="0.3" CurlRadius="14" BackColor="#f4f1ea" Shadow="0.5" /> On a round shape, such as an avatar, the corner lies mostly outside the circle: raise Amount so the peel reaches the edge. BackColor is a plain color; for a back that follows the theme, bind it to a DynamicResource color. Follow the pointer, or not With FollowPointer on (the default), the corner peels further as the pointer nears it. Turn it off for a fixed peel of Amount while hovered. Duration is how long the corner takes to peel or settle back (0.28 seconds by default); the layer's Speed doesn't apply. Properties Property Type Default Description Corner FXCorner BottomRight The corner that curls up (default: the bottom right). Values: TopLeft, TopRight, BottomRight, BottomLeft. Amount double 0.16 How far it peels on hover, as a share of the shape's diagonal. Range 0.02–0.6 (2–60%). CurlRadius double 10 Radius of the curl, at most: a short peel rolls tighter, so a flap always shows. Range 2–60 DIPs. BackColor Color #F4F1EA The color of the back. Shadow double 0.35 How dark the shadow under the curl is (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Duration double 0.28 How long it takes to peel or settle back. Range 0.05–1 seconds. FollowPointer bool true Peels further as the pointer nears the corner. IsPeeled bool false Holds it peeled without a hover. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Page peel has no randomness and no clock of its own, so Seed and Speed do nothing. While IsActive is off, it doesn't peel. Notes A capture while peeled. The capture is taken when the peel begins, and the real content is hidden under it but still takes input. Changes to the content show once the corner has settled back. Light and dark. The page draws the same on both surfaces; pick a BackColor that suits your theme. Reduced motion. A quick peel. See the poses. Cost. Under 0.1 ms of GPU time a frame on a card while it peels; flat and not hovered, it draws nothing. See What a layer costs. See also PagePeel API reference Layers that follow the pointer Jelly, which also stands in for the content while it plays Tilt and Holo foil, for cards that answer the pointer

docs/effects/particlenetwork.html.title: Particle network | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/particlenetwork.html.summary: Particle network ParticleNetwork draws dots drifting across the shape, joined by fine lines whenever two come close: the closer they are, the stronger the line. The pointer joins in as one more point and draws the nearby dots toward it. Use it as a light, technical background for a landing page, a sign-in screen or a "connected" state. It's drawn with Skia shapes rather than a shader, clipped to the host's shape, and it has no background of its own. Light Dark Add a particle network The network draws under the child, so leave the panel without a background and put the color on a container around the host: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <Border Background="#0B1220" CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ParticleNetwork Color="#CBD5E1" LineColor="#94A3B8" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="240"> <TextBlock Text="Connected" Foreground="White" FontSize="20" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </Border> </UserControl> Or draw it over a card that has its own background, as the gallery does, with Placement="Over": <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ParticleNetwork Count="46" LinkDistance="70" Color="#CBD5E1" LineColor="#94A3B8" Placement="Over" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="150" CornerRadius="14" Background="#0B1220" /> </fx:FXHost> Fit it to the shape Left unset, Count fits the shape: 60 dots, or fewer on a small shape, where the dots keep about 24 DIPs apart on average. LinkDistance, also left unset, is 100 DIPs, or less where the dots sit closer (at most 1.6 times their average spacing), so a small shape doesn't fill with lines. Set either one and it's drawn as set, however small the shape. The dots wander over the whole shape, whatever its size. DotSize is the dots' size in DIPs, and Drift about how fast they drift, in DIPs a second; at 0 they hold still. <fx:ParticleNetwork Count="120" LinkDistance="80" DotSize="1.5" Drift="20" /> Speed multiplies the clock and Drift sets the dots' own pace; changing either never makes the animation jump. Unlike the fills, the network's clock starts when it first draws, so networks on different hosts don't move in step. Follow the pointer With FollowPointer on (the default), the pointer over the shape joins the network: it links to the dots within reach and draws them a little toward it, and it eases after the pointer as it moves. Set FollowPointer="False" for a network that ignores the pointer. PointAt joins the network from code, as if the pointer were there; null leaves: Network.PointAt(new Point(120, 80)); Network.PointAt(null); Methods Call PointAt to aim the network from code: for keyboard focus, a guided tour or a demo. Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Joins the network at at (host coordinates) as the pointer would; null leaves. Properties Property Type Default Description Count int 60 How many dots. Left unset, it fits the shape: 60, or fewer on a small shape, where the dots keep about 24 DIPs apart on average. Range 4–200. Color Color #94A3B8 The dots' color. LineColor Color #94A3B8 The lines' color; each line fades as its two dots move apart. LinkDistance double 100 How close two dots must be for a line between them. Left unset, it fits the shape: 100 DIPs, or less where the dots sit closer (at most 1.6 times their average spacing), so a small shape doesn't fill with lines. Range 20–300. DotSize double 2 Diameter of a dot, in DIPs. Range 0.5–6. Drift double 14 About how fast the dots drift, DIPs a second. Range 0–120 DIPs per second. FollowPointer bool true Whether the pointer joins the network over the shape. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed picks the dots' paths. RenderScale doesn't apply, since the network is drawn as shapes. Notes Not a fill: the network has no BorderWidth or UseMask, and it runs on its own clock. Light and dark surfaces: the dots and lines are drawn in Color and LineColor on any surface. The default slate (#94A3B8) suits dark themes; the gallery uses a deeper slate (#64748B) on light ones. Pick a color for each theme with theme resources. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the dots hold still. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.09–0.32 ms of CPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, and almost no GPU time. Close pairs are found through a grid rather than by testing every pair. See Performance. See also ParticleNetwork API reference Dot grid and Topography, other quiet backgrounds Spotlight, another layer that follows the pointer Layers that follow the pointer

docs/effects/plastic.html.title: Plastic | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/plastic.html.summary: Plastic A slab of plastic under one soft light: a base that keeps its color, a highlight sized by the light and the surface's roughness, and a faint sky at grazing angles near the rim. It can be glossy or matte, domed or dished like a keycap's top. Use it for keyboard keys, tactile buttons, toggles and toy-like tiles. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child. It doesn't move, so it is drawn once and costs nothing per frame after that. Light Dark Add plastic The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Plastic Preset="Glossy" Color="#D7263D" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="56" Height="56" CornerRadius="12"> <TextBlock Text="esc" Foreground="#FFF1F2" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset sets Color, Roughness and Dome. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset, as the red key above does with Color. Value Description Glossy (default) Warm off-white with a crisp highlight, slightly domed. Matte Dark charcoal with a soft, broad sheen, slightly domed. Dished A matte face dished like a keycap's top. Make a row of keycaps Each key gets its own host and layer. Pick a text color for the plastic under it: dark on the light presets, light on Matte, which is dark gray: <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="12"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:Plastic Preset="Glossy" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="56" Height="56" CornerRadius="12"> <TextBlock Text="⌘" FontSize="20" Foreground="#4B4740" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:Plastic Preset="Dished" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="56" Height="56" CornerRadius="12"> <TextBlock Text="A" FontSize="18" Foreground="#4B4740" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers><fx:Plastic Preset="Matte" /></fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="56" Height="56" CornerRadius="12"> <TextBlock Text="⌥" FontSize="20" Foreground="#C7CAD1" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> Shape the slab Roughness goes from a small, sharp highlight (low) to a broad, soft one (high). Dome curves the face: positive values dome it, negative ones dish it. Bevel is the width of the rounded edge, and LightAngle moves the light: 0 is from above, 90 from the right. <fx:Plastic Color="#2563EB" Roughness="0.3" Dome="0.6" Bevel="10" LightAngle="0" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset PlasticPreset Glossy A starting finish: sets Color, Roughness and Dome. Local values win. Values: Glossy, Matte, Dished. Color Color #ECE8DE The plastic's color. Roughness double 0.15 How rough the surface is: low is glossy with a tight highlight, high is matte with a broad, faint one. Range 0.05–1 (5–100%). Dome double 0.35 Positive domes the face, negative dishes it. Range -1 to 1. Bevel double 6 Width of the rounded rim, in DIPs. Range 0–48. LightAngle double -29 Where the light comes from, degrees: 0 from above, 90 from the right; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Speed and Seed don't change plastic. Still: plastic has no motion, so it requests no frames once drawn, and it looks the same under reduced motion. Light and dark surfaces: plastic draws the same on both. Like every fill, plastic can paint only the child's own pixels (text, an icon) with UseMask, or a band inside the edge with BorderWidth. Cost: 0.042 ms of GPU time per redraw on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. See Performance. See also Plastic API reference Liquid metal, a moving, reflective material Inner shadow for pressed and raised shapes, and Tilt

docs/effects/pointershadow.html.title: Pointer shadow | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/pointershadow.html.summary: Pointer shadow Pointer shadow treats the pointer as a light over the page: the content casts a soft shadow away from it, in the shape of its own pixels, further and softer the further the light is. Every card on a page with the layer casts its shadow away from the same pointer, which gives a flat layout a sense of depth. With no pointer nearby, the light rests above the content and the shadow falls just below it. The shadow is drawn under the content. Light Dark Add a pointer shadow Add the layer to a host around the card, and leave room around it for the shadow: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12" Margin="48" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:PointerShadow /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="240" Height="140" CornerRadius="12" Padding="16" Background="White"> <TextBlock Text="Inbox" Foreground="#1f2937" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Lift it higher Elevation is how high the content floats over the page: higher casts a longer, softer shadow. LightHeight is how high the light is: lower casts longer shadows. MaxOffset caps how far the shadow moves from under the content, and Softness sets its blur right under it; it softens as it moves out. Darkness and Color set its tone. <fx:PointerShadow Elevation="24" LightHeight="180" MaxOffset="40" Softness="10" Darkness="0.35" /> Reach and pace Within PointerReach of the content (800 DIPs by default), the light follows the pointer across the window, even when it isn't over the host. FollowTime is how long the light takes to catch up with the pointer, and Fade how long it takes to move to the pointer when it arrives and back to rest when it leaves. Move the light yourself Set FollowPointer="False" and call PointAt(at) to place the light from code, in the host's coordinates; PointAt(null) sends it back to rest. For one light over several cards, translate the same point into each host: // LightAt is a point in Stage, the panel that holds both cards. ShadowA.PointAt(Stage.TranslatePoint(LightAt, CardHostA)); ShadowB.PointAt(Stage.TranslatePoint(LightAt, CardHostB)); With FollowPointer on, PointAt works too, and the pointer takes over when it moves within reach. Methods Call PointAt to place the light from code. Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Puts the light at at (host coordinates), as if the pointer were there. Null sends it back to rest. The pointer takes over when it moves within reach, unless FollowPointer is off. Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #000000 The shadow's color. Darkness double 0.3 How dark the shadow is (a dark page gets a deeper one, or it would not show). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Elevation double 14 How high the content floats over the page: higher casts a longer, softer shadow. Range 0–80 DIPs. LightHeight double 240 How high the light is over the page: lower casts longer shadows. Range 60–1500 DIPs. MaxOffset double 32 The furthest the shadow moves from under the content. Range 0–120 DIPs. Softness double 8 The blur of the shadow right under the content; it softens as it moves out. Range 0–40 DIPs. FollowPointer bool true Whether the light follows the pointer; off, it moves only with PointAt (a light of your own). PointerReach double 800 How far from the content the pointer still moves the light. Range 0–3000 DIPs. Applies when FollowPointer is true. FollowTime double 0.15 How long the light takes to catch up with the pointer (a time constant). Range 0–1 seconds. Fade double 0.5 How long the light takes to move to the pointer when it arrives, and back to rest when it leaves. Range 0–2 seconds. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The shadow follows the pointer, not a clock, so Speed and Seed do nothing. Notes The content's own shape. The shadow comes from the content's pixels, so transparent parts cast none and a round avatar casts a round shadow. The host captures the content; after changing something deep inside it, call RefreshMask() on the host. See Content masks. Light and dark. A dark page gets a deeper shadow, or it wouldn't show. See Light and dark surfaces. Room around it. The shadow reaches past the host by up to MaxOffset plus its blur. Leave room, or a clipping ancestor cuts it. Reduced motion. The light jumps to the pointer instead of easing. See the poses. Cost. About 0.16 ms of GPU time a frame on a card, since its shadow covers a large area. See What a layer costs. See also PointerShadow API reference Layers that follow the pointer Tilt, which leans the card toward the pointer Spotlight, a soft light that follows the pointer Ambient glow, a glow in the content's own colors

docs/effects/progressiveblur.html.title: Progressive blur | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/progressiveblur.html.summary: Progressive blur ProgressiveBlur blurs what is behind the host more and more toward one edge, from sharp to fully blurred, so content fades into a bar instead of meeting a hard line. Use it for a header or a tab bar over a scrolling list, or a caption over a photo. Every point sees a real blur, not a mix of sharp and blurred, and Tint fades toward the bar's own surface. It draws under the child and shows what is drawn behind the host, so it needs content behind it. Light Dark Add a progressive blur Lay a header over a scrolling list: the list first, then the host on top of it in the same Grid. The header's child has no background, so the blurred list shows through it: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <Grid> <ScrollViewer> <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Messages}" Margin="0,70,0,0" /> </ScrollViewer> <fx:FXHost VerticalAlignment="Top"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:ProgressiveBlur Blur="14" Tint="#99FFFFFF" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Height="70"> <TextBlock Text="Inbox" FontSize="18" FontWeight="Bold" Margin="16,12,0,0" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </Grid> </UserControl> The top margin on the list lets its first item start below the bar; as it scrolls, items slide under it. Give it something to blur The layer copies the region of the window behind the host just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). So: The content goes first. Only what is drawn before the host is blurred: put the list before the host in the Grid, or give the host a higher ZIndex. Controls drawn after the host sit in front of the bar. Keep the child see-through. The blur draws under the child, so a Background on the child hides it. The bar's title and buttons stay sharp on top. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. Choose the edge and the ramp Edge is where the blur is strongest: Top (the default) for a header, Bottom for a tab bar, Left or Right for a side panel. Ramp is how much of the shape the ramp covers from that edge, and Blur the blur at the edge: <fx:ProgressiveBlur Edge="Bottom" Ramp="0.6" Blur="24" /> Tint it per theme Tint is the color the blur fades toward at the strong edge, and its alpha is how much: the bar's own surface. Give it a value per theme, as the gallery does with #99FFFFFF on light and #991B1D22 on dark: <fx:ProgressiveBlur Tint="{DynamicResource HeaderTintColor}" /> See Light and dark surfaces for theme resources. Properties Property Type Default Description Blur double 16 Blur at the strongest edge, DIPs. Range 1–64. Edge FXEdge Top The edge where the blur is strongest. Values: Top, Bottom, Left, Right. Ramp double 1 How much of the shape the ramp covers, from the strong edge. Range 0.05–1 (5–100%). Tint Color #00FFFFFF A color the blur fades toward at the strong edge; its alpha is how much (a bar's surface). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The blur is still, so Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both; only the Tint should change. Reduced motion: the blur has no motion of its own, so nothing changes. Cost: about 1.0 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, the most of any layer, for its five copies of what is behind it (sharp, then blurred by an eighth, a quarter, a half and all of Blur). It doesn't animate, so it only redraws when what is behind it changes, such as while the list scrolls. See Performance. See also ProgressiveBlur API reference Glass with Frost, for an evenly frosted pane Frost and Color filter Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/pulse.html.title: Pulse | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/pulse.html.summary: Pulse Pulse sends light out from the host's shape. Radar rings, a breathing halo and a heartbeat run on their own and follow the shape's outline: use them for a live or recording status, an unread dot or a call to action. A ripple spreads from where the shape is tapped, inside it, like a touch response. A ping flies from the shape's edge to a point or another control, to show that something was sent. Light Dark Add a pulse The default style is Radar. Here it pairs with a glow on a recording dot; CornerRadius="999" makes the host's shape a circle, so the rings stay round. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Pulse Style="Radar" Color="#F97316" Reach="16" Width="1.5" /> <fx:Glow Color="#F97316" Radius="9" Hot="1" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Ellipse Width="20" Height="20" Fill="#F97316" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Count sets how many rings are out at once, Period how long each takes, and Reach how far they travel from the edge. Styles Radar, Breathe and Heartbeat draw under the child and run continuously. Ripple and Ping draw over it and play once each time they are fired. Value Description Radar (default) Rings that leave the shape's edge and fade as they spread. Breathe A halo that swells and settles. Heartbeat Lub-dub beats; each beat's ring keeps spreading under the next. Ripple A one-shot ripple from a point, confined to the shape. Overlapping taps overlap. Ping A comet that launches from the shape's edge, winds up, flies with a decelerating landing, then blooms and cools at its destination: Ping or PingTo. Ripple on a tap With Style="Ripple", every press on the host starts a ripple from the press point, because TriggerOnPress is on by default. Ripples overlap, so a quick double tap shows two. The press has to land on the host's content, so give it a background. <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Pulse Style="Ripple" Color="#3B82F6" Width="2.5" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="240" Height="96" CornerRadius="14" Background="White" Cursor="Hand"> <TextBlock Text="Tap anywhere" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> Unset, Reach lets a ripple spread to the farthest corner. Duration sets how long each ripple lives. Send a ping A ping winds up, flies from the shape's edge with a slowing landing, then blooms and cools where it lands. Call PingTo with the control it should land on, and give the sending host a higher ZIndex so the ping draws on top of the target: <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" Spacing="100"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999" ZIndex="1"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Pulse x:Name="Pinger" Style="Ping" TriggerOnPress="False" Color="#60A5FA" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Send" Click="OnSend" /> </fx:FXHost> <Border x:Name="Inbox" Width="120" Height="72" CornerRadius="12" Background="White" /> </StackPanel> private void OnSend(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => Pinger.PingTo(Inbox); Without a destination, Ping() flies along Direction for Travel DIPs. Set Interval to send one every so many seconds on its own. Methods Call these to fire a ripple or a ping from code, for example from a command or a network event. Positions are in the host's coordinates. Method Description Trigger(Point? at = null) Starts a ripple at at (host coordinates), or at the shape's center. Ping(Point? to = null) Fires a ping from the shape's edge to to (host coordinates), or along Direction for Travel. Pings overlap. Style must be Ping. PingTo(Control target) Fires a ping from the shape's edge to the center of target. Properties Property Type Default Description Style PulseStyle Radar The kind of pulse: radar rings, a breathing halo, a heartbeat, tap ripples, or pings that fly to a destination. Values: Radar, Breathe, Heartbeat, Ripple, Ping. Color Color #3B82F6 The color of the rings, the halo and the pings. CoreColor Color #E8F1FF The white-hot color where the light is brightest: the halo near the edge, a ripple's ring, a ping's head. Applies to the Breathe, Heartbeat, Ripple, and Ping styles. Count int 3 How many radar rings are out at once. Range 1–8. Applies to the Radar style. Period double 2.4 Seconds per cycle: one ring's trip, one breath, or one heartbeat. Range 0.3–8. Applies to the Radar, Breathe, and Heartbeat styles. Reach double 36 How far rings travel from the edge. For ripples, unset means the farthest corner. Range 4–160 DIPs. Applies to the Radar, Breathe, Heartbeat, and Ripple styles. Width double 1.6 Thickness of the rings, in DIPs; they widen as they spread. Range 0.3–8. Applies to the Radar, Heartbeat, and Ripple styles. Duration double 0.75 A ripple's life, or a ping's flight to its destination (it then blooms and cools for a while longer), in seconds. Range 0.1–3. Applies to the Ripple and Ping styles. Occlusion double 0.15 How much the light also covers what is behind it. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Direction double 0 Ping: the direction a ping flies when no destination is given, degrees: 0 to the right, 90 down; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Ping style. Travel double 160 Ping: how far a ping flies when no destination is given. Range 8–600 DIPs. Applies to the Ping style. Lag double 0.16 Ping: how far the tail trails the head, as a share of the flight. Range 0–0.5 (0–50%). Applies to the Ping style. HeadRadius double 2.6 Ping: radius of the comet's head, in DIPs; it swells as it blooms at the destination. Range 0.5–12. Applies to the Ping style. Interval double 0 Ping: fire one every this many seconds (0: only when asked). Range 0–10. Applies to the Ping style. TriggerOnPress bool true Starts a ripple (or fires a ping) whenever the pointer is pressed on the host; on by default. The other styles run on their own and ignore presses. Applies to the Ripple and Ping styles. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a pulse, Intensity is the strength of the light, up to 3. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the rings add light. On a light surface they draw as tinted haze, and the radar turns down its edge glow and the wash between rings, so the rings carry the effect. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The rings become a static halo. A ripple is a faint flash over the shape, and a ping glows up and cools at its destination without flying. See Reduced motion. One-shots. Ripples and pings draw nothing between shots. When too many are live at once, the oldest fades out. See One-shots. Cost. About 0.1 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. See Performance. Room around the host. Radar, breathe and heartbeat rings travel Reach DIPs past the shape, and a ping flies past it. A clipping ancestor, such as a ScrollViewer, cuts them off: leave room around the host. See also Pulse API reference Glow, a steady light around the same shape Sparkles and Electric, other one-shots fired on a press Beam, light flowing along a path between two controls One-shots and the pointer

docs/effects/rainglass.html.title: Rain glass | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/rainglass.html.summary: Rain glass RainGlass puts rain on a misted pane over the content: beads that come and go, fine droplets, and drops that slide down in fits and starts, leaving a clear wet trail dotted with droplets. Each drop is a small lens that shows what is behind it upside down, and Fog mists the glass between them. Use it for a weather card, a cozy header or a lock screen. It draws over the child, so it rains on the child and whatever shows through it. Light Dark Add rain Wrap the content in a host. Points of light make the lensing easy to see: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:RainGlass /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="150" CornerRadius="14" Background="#101830" ClipToBounds="True"> <Canvas> <Ellipse Canvas.Left="20" Canvas.Top="30" Width="26" Height="26" Fill="#FFB347" /> <Ellipse Canvas.Left="120" Canvas.Top="24" Width="30" Height="30" Fill="#7FD4FF" /> <Ellipse Canvas.Left="170" Canvas.Top="80" Width="22" Height="22" Fill="#FFD27F" /> <Ellipse Canvas.Left="40" Canvas.Top="100" Width="20" Height="20" Fill="#FFD43B" /> </Canvas> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Give it something to bend The pane copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). Over the child, the default, that is the child and whatever shows through it. Each drop shows what lies about two of its radii away, mirrored, so the drops read best over detail: lights, a picture, text. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. Clear or mist the glass Fog is how misted the glass is between the drops, from 0 (clear) to 1. The mist blurs what is under it, labels included: the gallery lowers it to 0.3 over a picture so its titles stay readable: <fx:RainGlass Fog="0.3" /> Change the rain Density sets how many drops there are, DropSize the radius of a typical drop, and Refraction how strongly the drops bend what is behind them (0 for none): <fx:RainGlass Density="1.6" DropSize="9" Refraction="1.4" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Density double 1 How many drops. Range 0–2. DropSize double 6 Radius of a typical drop. Range 2–16 DIPs. Fog double 0.6 How misted the glass is between the drops. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Refraction double 1 How strongly the drops bend what is behind them, a multiple: 1 shows what lies about two radii away, 0 none. Range 0–2. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed changes where the drops fall, and Speed how fast the rain runs. Notes Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the drops hold still. Cost: about 0.51 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card, including a blurred copy of what is under it. It animates, so it redraws every frame while it is visible. See Performance. See also RainGlass API reference Water, Frost and Weather Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/retrogrid.html.title: Retro grid | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/retrogrid.html.summary: Retro grid RetroGrid paints a synthwave scene: a floor of glowing grid lines running toward a horizon, a gradient sky above it and a striped sun sitting on the horizon. Use it as the background of a hero section, a splash screen or a game menu. It's a fill, so it paints the host's shape under the child and your content sits on top of it. Light Dark Add a retro grid Put the host around the panel, and leave the panel without a background so the scene shows through it. The host's CornerRadius rounds the scene's corners. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:RetroGrid /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="320"> <TextBlock Text="NIGHT DRIVE" Foreground="White" FontSize="40" FontWeight="Black" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Margin="0,40,0,0" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The scene follows the panel's size: the horizon sits at a share of its height, and the sun's radius is a share of its shorter side. CellSize is the size of a grid cell at the front (bottom) edge, in DIPs. Move the horizon and the sun Horizon is where the horizon sits, as a share of the height from the top (0.55 by default). Lower values give more floor. SunSize sets the sun's radius as a share of the shape's shorter side, and ShowSun="False" leaves the sky empty. The sun shades from SunColor at the top to SunEdgeColor at the bottom. <fx:RetroGrid Horizon="0.4" SunSize="0.2" SunColor="#7DF9FF" SunEdgeColor="#3A86FF" /> <fx:RetroGrid ShowSun="False" CellSize="24" /> Change the colors SkyColor is the top of the sky and HorizonColor the sky at the horizon, which also tints the haze along it. FloorColor fills the floor between the lines, and LineColor colors the lines. Glow sets the glow around the lines and the sun (1 by default, 0 for none, up to 2), LineWidth the lines' width in DIPs, and Fog how far below the horizon the lines fade into the haze. <fx:RetroGrid SkyColor="#020617" HorizonColor="#0EA5E9" FloorColor="#020617" LineColor="#38BDF8" SunColor="#E0F2FE" SunEdgeColor="#0284C7" Glow="0.6" Fog="0.8" /> Set the pace FlowSpeed is how many rows run toward the viewer each second (0.6 by default). At 0 the whole scene stands still and asks for no frames. Speed, which every layer has, multiplies the clock of the whole scene, the sun's drifting stripes included. To speed the floor up or slow it down while it runs, change Speed or FlowSpeed: neither makes the animation jump. <fx:RetroGrid FlowSpeed="1.5" /> <fx:RetroGrid Speed="0.5" /> Fills run on one shared clock, so retro grids on different hosts, with the same settings, move their floors in step, whenever each host was created. Properties Property Type Default Description SkyColor Color #0D0221 The sky's color at the top; it shades to HorizonColor toward the horizon. HorizonColor Color #FF2E88 The sky's color at the horizon, and the glow along the horizon. FloorColor Color #0D0221 The floor's color under the grid lines. LineColor Color #FF3CD6 The grid lines' color. SunColor Color #FFD319 The sun's color at its top. SunEdgeColor Color #FF2975 The sun's color at its bottom: it shades from SunColor at the top to this. Horizon double 0.55 Where the horizon sits, as a share of the height from the top. Range 0.1–0.9 (10–90%). CellSize double 36 Size of a grid cell at the front edge. Range 8–200 DIPs. FlowSpeed double 0.6 Rows per second running toward the viewer. Range 0–4. LineWidth double 1.5 Width of the grid lines, in DIPs. Range 0.5–6. ShowSun bool true Whether the striped sun shows above the horizon. SunSize double 0.28 The sun's radius, as a share of the shape's shorter side. Range 0.05–0.5 (5–50%). Glow double 1 The glow around the grid lines and the sun, a multiple: 1 is the default, 0 none. Range 0–2. Fog double 0.5 How far up the floor the lines fade into the haze at the horizon; more fades them from further forward. Range 0–1 (0–100%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1. Notes Light and dark surfaces: the scene is opaque and paints its own colors, so it looks the same on a light or a dark surface. Reduced motion: with FXSettings.ReducedMotion on, the floor and the sun hold one fixed pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.05 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, among the cheapest layers. The cost grows with the area. See Performance. Seed: the grid has no randomness, so Seed changes nothing. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which paints only the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also RetroGrid API reference Starfield, Beams and Bokeh, other backgrounds Layers and hosts

docs/effects/reveal.html.title: Reveal | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/reveal.html.summary: Reveal Reveal shows and hides the host's content with a transition: it dissolves into noise, burns away, closes in an iris, melts out of its place, or resolves out of noise like an image being generated. Use it wherever content arrives or goes away: a panel that opens, a draft that's discarded, a result that comes in. The layer captures the content as it looks, hides the real element, and plays the transition over it. Light Dark Add a reveal Bind IsShown to whatever says the content should be there. Here a switch burns a card away and back: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Reveal Style="Burn" IsShown="{Binding #ShownSwitch.IsChecked}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="200" Height="96" CornerRadius="14" Padding="16" Background="#15171c"> <TextBlock Text="Draft" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> <ToggleSwitch x:Name="ShownSwitch" IsChecked="True" OnContent="Shown" OffContent="Burned" /> </StackPanel> </UserControl> Styles Style picks the transition. Softness, EdgeColor, Angle, NoiseScale, CellSize and Twist each belong to some styles; the properties table lists which. Value Description Dissolve (default) The content breaks up into noise; on a dark surface its edge catches a faint light. Burn A dissolve with a glowing, charring edge. Pixelate The content coarsens into blocks, then fades. Iris A circle closes on (or opens from) the origin. Wipe A soft edge sweeps across. Melt The content melts and drips down out of its place. Radial A hand sweeps around the origin, like a clock. Diamonds Diamonds grow in a grid, in a wave across. Swirl The content twists in from a swirl as it fades in, and out into one. Halftone Halftone dots grow into the content, in a wave across. Generate Noise resolves into the content in ever finer steps, as an image being generated. Show and hide IsShown is true by default and binds both ways, so Show() and Hide() also update a bound view-model property. Set IsShown="False" in XAML to start hidden: the content is hidden at once, with no transition. While hidden, the element is transparent but keeps its place in the layout. Its own Opacity value is left alone, and it still takes clicks and keyboard focus; set IsHitTestVisible from the same property if it shouldn't. A change while a transition plays turns it around from where it is, without a jump. The capture is taken as the transition starts, so changes to the content show once it is handed back. Play it from a point Show(from) and Hide(toward) take a point in the host's coordinates. An iris opens from it or closes on it, a clock wipe (Radial) sweeps around it, and a swirl twists around it. With no point they use the center of the shape; the other styles ignore the point. private void OnCardReleased(object? sender, PointerReleasedEventArgs e) { // Close the iris on the point that was tapped. CardReveal.Hide(e.GetPosition(CardHost)); } Drive it from a view model Bind IsShown to a property and change the property: // ViewModelBase is any base class that raises PropertyChanged, // such as CommunityToolkit.Mvvm's ObservableObject. public class ComposerViewModel : ViewModelBase { private bool _isDraftShown = true; public bool IsDraftShown { get => _isDraftShown; set => SetProperty(ref _isDraftShown, value); } public void Discard() => IsDraftShown = false; public void Undo() => IsDraftShown = true; } <fx:Reveal x:Name="CardReveal" Style="Dissolve" IsShown="{Binding IsDraftShown}" /> Because the binding is two-way, a Hide(point) called from the view also sets IsDraftShown to false. Set the pace Duration is the length of one transition in seconds (0.8 by default). The layer's Speed doesn't apply. The length is read when a transition starts, so a change applies from the next one; under reduced motion it is at most a quarter of a second. Before the content is laid out A transition needs a capture of the content. With nothing to capture, the layer switches at once without playing: when the host has no child, the child isn't visible, it hasn't been laid out yet (for example, IsShown set in a view's constructor), or the layer's IsActive is false. To play an entrance as a view opens, start hidden and call Show() once the content is laid out: <fx:Reveal x:Name="WelcomeReveal" Style="Generate" Duration="1.6" IsShown="False" /> public WelcomeView() { InitializeComponent(); // Loaded is raised after the view's first layout pass. Loaded += (_, _) => WelcomeReveal.Show(); } Methods Show and Hide play the transition from code, from or toward a point. Method Description Show(Point? from = null) Shows the content, playing the layer's transition from from (host coordinates). Null: the layer's own point. Hide(Point? toward = null) Hides the content, playing the layer's transition toward toward (host coordinates). Null: the layer's own point. Properties Property Type Default Description Style RevealStyle Dissolve How the content appears and disappears. Values: Dissolve, Burn, Pixelate, Iris, Wipe, Melt, Radial, Diamonds, Swirl, Halftone, Generate. IsShown bool true Whether the content is shown. Changing it plays the transition: true reveals the content, false hides it. Duration double 0.8 How long the transition takes, in seconds. Range 0.1–4. Softness double 0.06 Softness of the edge, as a share of the transition. Range 0.01–0.4 (1–40%). Applies to the Dissolve, Burn, Iris, Wipe, and Radial styles. EdgeColor Color #FF8A2A The burning edge's color. Applies to the Burn style. Angle double 0 Direction a wipe, or the wave of diamonds or dots, sweeps (0: left to right); where a clock wipe starts (0: at the top). Degrees; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Wipe, Radial, Diamonds, and Halftone styles. NoiseScale double 26 Grain of a dissolve or burn; the width of a melt's drips. Range 4–120 DIPs. Applies to the Dissolve, Burn, and Melt styles. CellSize double 28 The coarsest block of a pixelate or a generate; the grid of diamonds or dots. Range 4–80 DIPs. Applies to the Pixelate, Diamonds, Halftone, and Generate styles. Twist double 300 How far a swirl twists the middle of the content, degrees (0: not at all); it turns counterclockwise as it hides. Range 0–1080. Applies to the Swirl style. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Light and dark. Reveal knows the surface it sits on: on a dark one, a dissolve's edge catches a faint light. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. Every style becomes a fade of at most a quarter of a second. See the poses. Cost. Each transition renders the content once into an image on the UI thread. While it plays, a reveal takes about 0.1 ms of GPU time a frame on a card (the melt 0.12 ms). Once shown and handed back, or hidden, it draws nothing. See What a layer costs. Room below a melt. Melt runs down past the content's bottom edge. Leave room below the host, or a clipping ancestor cuts the drips. Contrast. A dissolve reads by what shows through its holes. Content with the same color as the surface behind it needs an edge or a border to show the transition. See also Reveal API reference Show and hide transitions Genie and Shatter, the other show and hide transitions Spoiler, which covers content until it is tapped

docs/effects/shatter.html.title: Shatter | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/shatter.html.summary: Shatter Shatter breaks the host's content into glass shards that fly apart and fall, or turns it to dust that blows away, and brings it back together to show it. It suits delete, dismiss and undo. Like Reveal, it captures the content, hides the real element while the pieces fly, and hands it back once shown. The pieces are drawn with Skia straight from the capture. Light Dark Add a shatter Bind IsShown, or call Hide() and Show(). Here a switch breaks the card and puts it back together: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <StackPanel Spacing="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14" ZIndex="1"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Shatter Pieces="30" IsShown="{Binding #ShownSwitch.IsChecked}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="220" Height="96" CornerRadius="14" Padding="16" Background="#15171c"> <TextBlock Text="Old draft" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> <ToggleSwitch x:Name="ShownSwitch" IsChecked="True" OnContent="Whole" OffContent="Broken" /> </StackPanel> </UserControl> Styles Value Description Shards (default) Glass shards that fly apart and fall. Dust Fine dust that blows away on the wind, from one side or from the point given. Break it from a point Hide(toward) takes the point the break starts from, in the host's coordinates. Shards are cut around it, smaller near it; dust leaves from it outward. Show(from) brings the pieces back toward it. With no point, shards break from the center, and dust leaves from the side the wind blows toward (WindAngle). private void OnCardPressed(object? sender, PointerPressedEventArgs e) { var at = e.GetPosition(CardHost); if (CardShatter.IsShown) CardShatter.Hide(at); else CardShatter.Show(at); } The hidden element keeps its place in the layout and still takes presses and keyboard focus, so pressing where the card was brings it back here. Set IsHitTestVisible from the same state if it shouldn't. Delete with undo IsShown is true by default and binds both ways, so Hide() and Show() also update a bound view-model property. Bind it to a property and change that: // ViewModelBase is any base class that raises PropertyChanged. public class MessageViewModel : ViewModelBase { private bool _isShown = true; public bool IsShown { get => _isShown; set => SetProperty(ref _isShown, value); } public void Delete() => IsShown = false; public void Undo() => IsShown = true; } <fx:Shatter Style="Dust" IsShown="{Binding IsShown}" /> Set IsShown="False" in XAML to start hidden, with no transition. If the host shrinks while the pieces fly (a list row collapsing as it is removed), the pieces scale with it rather than being cut again. Set the pace Duration is the length of the break, or of the landing, in seconds (1.1 by default). The layer's Speed doesn't apply, and a change applies from the next transition. Force sets how hard the shards fly out and Gravity how fast they fall. For dust, DustSize sets the grain: larger grains keep large content quick. With nothing to capture (no child, a child that isn't visible or isn't laid out yet, or IsActive off) the layer switches at once. To play it as a view opens, start hidden and call Show() from the view's Loaded event; Reveal shows the pattern. Methods Show and Hide play the transition from code, from or toward a point. Method Description Show(Point? from = null) Shows the content, playing the layer's transition from from (host coordinates). Null: the layer's own point. Hide(Point? toward = null) Hides the content, playing the layer's transition toward toward (host coordinates). Null: the layer's own point. Properties Property Type Default Description Style ShatterStyle Shards Whether the content breaks into glass shards or blows away as dust. Values: Shards, Dust. IsShown bool true Whether the content is shown. Setting it false breaks the content apart; true brings it back together. Duration double 1.1 How long the transition takes, in seconds. Range 0.2–4. Pieces int 36 About how many shards. Range 6–120. Applies to the Shards style. Force double 1 How hard the pieces fly out: the shards' burst, or how hard the wind blows the dust away. Range 0–3. Gravity double 1 How strongly the pieces fall, a multiple of the default (dust falls only gently; 0: they don't fall). Range 0–3. EdgeHighlight double 0.5 The light catching each shard's edges. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Shards style. DustSize double 3 The size of a grain of dust (larger grains for large content, to stay quick). Range 1–8 DIPs. Applies to the Dust style. WindAngle double -25 The way the wind blows the dust, degrees: 0 to the right, -90 up; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Dust style. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed changes how the shards are cut. Notes Light and dark. On a dark surface the light catches each shard's edges in white. On a light one the edges are dark lines, and the shards cast a soft shadow on the page, so a white card's pieces still show. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. It becomes a fade of at most a quarter of a second, with no flying. See the poses. Cost. The shards are Skia paths: 0.1–0.4 ms of CPU time a frame while they fly. Dust takes 0.13–0.6 ms of CPU time while it blows. Both swing from run to run. At rest the layer draws nothing. RenderScale doesn't apply. See What a layer costs. Room to fly. Shards fly out and fall well past the host, and dust drifts past its edge. A clipping ancestor cuts them, and a later sibling covers them: leave room, and give the host a higher ZIndex. See also Shatter API reference Show and hide transitions Reveal and Genie, the other show and hide transitions Confetti, also drawn as Skia shapes

docs/effects/shimmer.html.title: Shimmer | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/shimmer.html.summary: Shimmer A soft band of light sweeps across the shape once a period, then rests off it before the next pass. Use it for skeleton loaders, a button that is working, or a "Thinking…" label while an answer streams in. It draws over the host's child, and the band starts and ends off the shape, so it never cuts in or out mid-pass. With UseMask, it sweeps across the child's own pixels instead of its box. Light Dark Add a shimmer Wrap the control in an FXHost and add a Shimmer to its layers: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Shimmer /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Classes="accent" Content="Generate" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Build a skeleton loader BaseColor paints a block under the sheen, so an empty Border becomes a placeholder bar. Each bar needs its own host and its own layer, since a layer can be in one host at a time: <StackPanel Spacing="12" Width="240"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="8"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Shimmer BaseColor="#E2E5EA" Intensity="1.6" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Height="16" /> </fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="8" HorizontalAlignment="Left"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Shimmer BaseColor="#E2E5EA" Intensity="1.6" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Height="16" Width="130" /> </fx:FXHost> </StackPanel> BaseColor is a Color, so a theme resource bound to it must be a color resource, not a brush. Transparent (the default) paints no block. To switch the placeholder off when the data arrives, bind IsActive. Layers inherit the host's DataContext: <fx:Shimmer BaseColor="#E2E5EA" IsActive="{Binding IsLoading}" /> Sweep across text With UseMask, the sheen runs over the letters only, not the text's whole box. A gray text color lets it show on both light and dark themes: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Shimmer UseMask="True" Intensity="2.5" Band="18" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="Thinking…" FontSize="16" FontWeight="SemiBold" Foreground="#8A8F98" /> </fx:FXHost> The host captures its child to find those pixels. After changing something deeper inside the child, call FXHost.RefreshMask(); see Content masks. Shape the sweep Period is the length of one pass plus its rest, in seconds, and Pause is the share of it the band spends off the shape. Band sets the band's width, Angle tilts it from upright, and Color tints it: <fx:Shimmer Period="2.4" Pause="0.5" Band="40" Angle="-15" Color="#BFDBFE" /> Feather softens the edge of the shape. It doesn't apply with UseMask, which follows the child's own edges. Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #FFFFFF The sheen's color. BaseColor Color #00FFFFFF A base color under the sheen (a skeleton block). Transparent: none. Period double 1.8 Seconds from one sweep to the next, pause included. Range 0.3–6. Band double 28 Width of the sheen band, in DIPs. Range 4–120. Angle double 20 Tilt of the band from upright, degrees: 0 upright; positive turns it clockwise (top to the right). Range -60 to 60. Pause double 0.3 Share of each period the band rests off the shape. Range 0–0.9 (0–90%). Feather double 0 How far inside the shape's edge the sheen fades in, in DIPs (0: a crisp edge). Not used with UseMask. Range 0–24. UseMask bool false Sweep across the child's own pixels (text, icons) instead of its box. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the sheen's strength, up to 3. At 0 the sheen is gone, but a BaseColor block still draws. Seed doesn't change the shimmer. Light and dark surfaces: the shimmer draws the same on both. The sheen adds light, so it shows over colored or darker content and has little to brighten on plain white; give a skeleton a BaseColor, and text a gray or colored foreground. Reduced motion: the band stops traveling, and the whole surface breathes gently instead. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.025 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card, in the gallery's bench. See Performance. See also Shimmer API reference Glow, whose Mask style blooms around text instead of sweeping it Holo foil and Grain Content masks

docs/effects/shockwave.html.title: Shockwave | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/shockwave.html.summary: Shockwave Shockwave sends out a ring of compressed air that bends everything it passes over as it spreads from a point, with a color split at its front, a highlight where there is content to catch it, and a faint rim so it still reads over a plain backdrop. Use it as press feedback on a key action, an impact in a game, or a moment when something lands. It is a one-shot: it fires on a press or from code, draws nothing between shots, and shots overlap. It draws over the child and reaches past the host, bending the host and what is around it. Light Dark Add a shockwave Wrap the control in a host. A press fires a ring from the press point (TriggerOnPress is on by default): <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14" Cursor="Hand"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Shockwave Reach="150" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Press me" Width="150" Height="48" CornerRadius="14" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Give it room and something to bend The ring copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop). So: It bends what is drawn before it: the child, and the page around the host out to Reach. Over text, edges and pictures the bend reads clearly; over a flat fill only the faint rim shows. Leave room. The ring spreads up to Reach from its origin, plus a few widths of its front, well past the host. A clipping ancestor, such as a ScrollViewer or a Border with ClipToBounds, cuts it. Controls drawn after the host cover the ring. Give the host a higher ZIndex when it should pass over its neighbors. A press must land on the host's child. A child with no background in empty areas doesn't take presses: give it a Background, even Transparent. Keep ancestors opaque. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content. Fire from code Trigger(at) fires a ring from a point in the host's coordinates, or from the shape's center with no point. Set TriggerOnPress="False" to fire only from code: private void OnTileReleased(object? sender, PointerReleasedEventArgs e) { TileWave.Trigger(e.GetPosition(TileHost)); } // From the center, when an upload finishes.
