TileWave.Trigger(); Shape the ring Reach is how far the ring spreads, Width how wide its front is, Displacement how far it bends what is behind it, Chroma the color split at the front (a share of Displacement) and Duration how long a shot lasts: <fx:Shockwave Reach="240" Width="20" Displacement="14" Chroma="0.5" Duration="1.2" /> Methods Call Trigger to fire a ring without a press. See One-shots. Method Description Trigger(Point? at = null) Fires a shockwave from at (host coordinates), or the shape's center. Properties Property Type Default Description Reach double 160 How far the ring spreads from where it starts, in DIPs. Range 16–600. Width double 14 Width of the ring's front, in DIPs; it widens as it spreads. Range 2–60. Displacement double 9 How far the front bends what is behind it. Range 0–40 DIPs. Chroma double 0.35 Color split at the front, as a share of Displacement. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Duration double 0.9 How long a ring takes to spread and fade, in seconds. Range 0.1–3. TriggerOnPress bool true Fires a shockwave wherever the pointer is pressed on the host (on by default). Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. The ring has no randomness, so Seed doesn't apply. Notes Overlapping shots: firing again while a ring is still spreading starts another one beside it. When the layer's pool of live shots is full, the oldest fades out. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: no travel: a press gives a soft brightening at its origin that cools. Cost: about 0.26 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card while a ring is live. Each frame shades only around the live rings, and between shots it draws nothing. See Performance. See also Shockwave API reference Pulse with Style="Ripple", a ripple confined to the shape Water, Jelly and Glitch One-shots

docs/effects/silk.html.title: Silk | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/silk.html.summary: Silk A background of soft satin: a few broad folds lit by one soft light, shading into their creases with a gentle sheen along the ridges, flowing slowly. It is calm enough to sit behind text, so it suits hero sections, sign-in pages, welcome screens and feature cards. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape in one color and its shades, and goes under the child. Light Dark Add silk The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Silk Preset="Midnight" Scale="120" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="240" Height="140"> <StackPanel HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" Spacing="4"> <TextBlock Text="Welcome back" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="20" HorizontalAlignment="Center" /> <TextBlock Text="Sign in to continue" Foreground="#C7D2FE" FontSize="12" HorizontalAlignment="Center" /> </StackPanel> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset sets Color and Sheen. Set either yourself to adjust a preset. Value Description Mauve (default) A muted mauve. Midnight Deep navy. Pearl A pale, warm pearl. Rose Dusty rose. Emerald Deep green. Use your own color Silk is shaded from a single Color: the folds darken into their creases and lighten along the ridges. A brand color works directly: <fx:Silk Color="#7C3AED" /> Pick the text color by the silk's: light text on every preset but Pearl, and dark text on Pearl and other pale colors. Shape the folds Scale sets how wide the folds are, Angle which way they run (0 is top to bottom), and Sheen how much light runs along the ridges. Speed sets how fast they flow: <fx:Silk Preset="Pearl" Scale="260" Angle="20" Sheen="0.5" Speed="0.5" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset SilkPreset Mauve A starting Color and Sheen; local values win. Values: Mauve, Midnight, Pearl, Rose, Emerald. Color Color #7B7481 The fabric's color; the creases shade it darker and the sheen paler. Scale double 160 How wide the folds are. Range 30–600 DIPs. Sheen double 1 The light along the ridges. Range 0–2. Angle double -30 Which way the folds run, degrees: 0 top to bottom; positive turns them clockwise. Range -180 to 180. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Seed doesn't change silk. Light and dark surfaces: silk draws the same on both; it is an opaque background in its own color. Reduced motion: the folds hold one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.057 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. See Performance. Like every fill, silk can paint only the child's own pixels with UseMask, or a band inside the edge with BorderWidth. See also Silk API reference Mesh gradient, Swirl and Aurora, other moving backgrounds Liquid metal and Beams

docs/effects/sparkles.html.title: Sparkles | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/sparkles.html.summary: Sparkles Sparkles scatters crisp four-point stars around the host's shape, each with its own size, twinkle and spin. The stars take turns, so only a few are lit at once. Use them on a "New" badge, a premium feature or a reward. A burst pops every star at once and flings it out a little, as a one-shot for a success, a like or a completed task. The stars sit just outside the shape and draw over the child. Light Dark Add sparkles The defaults suit a small pill; on a larger target, raise Count and Size. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="999"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Sparkles Count="12" Size="12" Margin="14" Color="#F59E0B" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="92" Height="38" CornerRadius="19" Background="#FEF3C7"> <TextBlock Text="New" Foreground="#B45309" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Margin is how far outside the shape the stars sit. Life is how long each star stays lit before it rests. Burst on a press Turn IsContinuous off to show stars only during a burst, and BurstOnPress on to burst whenever the host is pressed. Every burst has its own layout, so two quick presses show two different bursts. <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="10"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Sparkles IsContinuous="False" BurstOnPress="True" Count="18" Size="10" Margin="22" Color="#7C5CFF" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Like" CornerRadius="10" /> </fx:FXHost> Burst from code Name the layer and call Burst() when something worth celebrating happens, for example when a save completes: <fx:Sparkles x:Name="SaveSparkles" IsContinuous="False" /> private void OnSaved(object? sender, EventArgs e) { SaveSparkles.Burst(); } A burst takes no point: the stars sit all around the shape. Methods Method Description Burst() Pops every star once; they fly a little way out and twinkle away. The stars sit all around the shape, so a burst takes no point. Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #FFE6A8 The stars' color. Count int 6 How many stars sit around the shape; continuous stars rest between appearances, so fewer are lit at once. Range 1–32. Life double 1.5 How long a star stays lit, seconds. Range 0.3–5. Size double 7 A star's base size, DIPs: most are smaller, a few larger. Range 2–24. Margin double 10 How far outside the shape stars sit. Range 0–60 DIPs. IsContinuous bool true Twinkle forever. Off: stars show only during a Burst. BurstOnPress bool false Bursts whenever the pointer is pressed on the host. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On sparkles, Intensity is the strength of the light, up to 3, and Seed picks where the stars sit. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the stars add light and their cores turn white. On a light surface they draw as tinted haze with cores in the layer's own color, so a pale gold reads weakly on white: pick a deeper color for light themes, such as amber. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. Continuous stars hold still: a fixed handful stays lit. A burst still shows, but the stars fade in and out in place without flying or spinning. See Reduced motion. One-shots. With IsContinuous off, the layer draws nothing between bursts. When too many bursts are live at once, the oldest fades out. See One-shots. Cost. About 0.19 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. See Performance. Room around the host. The stars draw outside the shape, as far as Margin plus a star's size. A clipping ancestor cuts them off: leave room around the host. See also Sparkles API reference Trail, sparks that follow the pointer Pulse, a ripple or a ping as a one-shot One-shots and the pointer

docs/effects/spoiler.html.title: Spoiler | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/spoiler.html.summary: Spoiler Spoiler hides the host's content until it is revealed, as messaging apps hide spoilers: shimmering dust over a heavy blur, a mosaic, or a solid cover. A tap opens it in a soft circle from the tap point. Use it for spoilers, answers to a quiz, sensitive values such as a balance or a code, or redaction in screenshots and demos. It draws over the content. Light Dark Add a spoiler Wrap the text, or any element, in a host with the layer. A tap reveals it; here it covers itself again after four seconds: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="6" Cursor="Hand" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Spoiler HideAfter="4" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="It was the gardener all along." FontSize="15" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Styles Value Description Dust (default) Shimmering dust over a heavy blur of the content. Pixelate A mosaic of the content: redaction for screenshots and demos. Solid Dust over a solid cover color (no copy of what is behind). Reveal and cover from code IsRevealed is false by default and binds both ways, so a tap, Reveal() and Hide() also update a bound view-model property. Reveal(from) opens the circle from a point in the host's coordinates, or from the center without one. Hide() fades the cover back in. <fx:Spoiler x:Name="AnswerSpoiler" IsRevealed="{Binding IsAnswerShown}" /> private void OnShowAnswerClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => AnswerSpoiler.Reveal(); private void OnNextQuestionClick(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) => AnswerSpoiler.Hide(); Duration is how long the reveal takes to open, and the cover to fade back in (0.7 seconds by default). The layer's Speed paces the dust, not the reveal. Set RevealOnPress="False" when only your code should reveal it. Cover it again after a while HideAfter covers the content again that many seconds after a reveal has finished opening. At 0, the default, or Infinity, it stays revealed. For a one-time code or a balance: <fx:Spoiler Style="Pixelate" CellSize="10" HideAfter="8" /> Redact or cover Pixelate turns the content into a mosaic of CellSize cells, without dust: redaction for screenshots and demos. Solid lays a CoverColor with dust over it instead of a copy of what is behind; set it to the surface behind the content. The dust is set by Density, DustSize, DustSpeed and DustColor; a transparent DustColor, the default, contrasts with whatever it covers. <fx:Spoiler Style="Solid" CoverColor="#2a2d34" Density="0.4" /> Methods Call Reveal and Hide to open and cover from code. Method Description Reveal(Point? from = null) Reveals the content, opening from from (host coordinates) or the center. Hide() Covers the content again. Properties Property Type Default Description Style SpoilerStyle Dust How the content is hidden: dust over a blur, a mosaic, or dust over a solid cover. Values: Dust, Pixelate, Solid. IsRevealed bool false Whether the content is revealed: true opens the cover in a soft circle, false covers it again. Binds both ways, so a tap updates it. RevealOnPress bool true Reveals where the pointer is pressed on the host. HideAfter double 0 Seconds the content stays revealed, counted from when the opening finishes, before it is covered again (0 or Infinity: it stays revealed). Range 0–60. Duration double 0.7 How long the cover takes to open on a reveal, and to fade back in on a hide. Range 0–3 seconds. DustColor Color #00FFFFFF The dust's color. Transparent: contrasts with what it covers. Applies to the Dust and Solid styles. CoverColor Color #2A2D34 The cover for the Solid style (match the surface behind the content). Applies to the Solid style. Density double 0.3 How much dust there is: the share of places holding a speck (0: none). Range 0–1 (0–100%). Applies to the Dust and Solid styles. DustSize double 1.6 Size of a dust speck, in DIPs. Range 0.3–4. Applies to the Dust and Solid styles. DustSpeed double 1 How fast the dust swirls and twinkles, a multiple (0: still). Range 0–4. Applies to the Dust and Solid styles. Blur double 6 Blur under the dust. Range 1–20 DIPs. Applies to the Dust style. CellSize double 8 Mosaic cell for the Pixelate style. Range 2–40 DIPs. Applies to the Pixelate style. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Pixels only. The spoiler covers what is drawn. The content itself is still there: screen readers read it, and it takes focus and input as before. Reads the backdrop. Dust and Pixelate copy what is behind them, which holds the content. Keep ancestors opaque, or use Solid, which needs no copy. See Layers that read the backdrop. Reduced motion. Revealing and covering switch at once, and the dust holds still. See the poses. Cost. The dust over a blur takes about 0.32 ms of GPU time a frame on a card, 0.92 ms on a 700×500 panel. Once revealed, it draws nothing. See What a layer costs. See also Spoiler API reference Reveal, which shows and hides content with a transition Progressive blur and Frost, other ways to obscure what is behind Show and hide transitions

docs/effects/spotlight.html.title: Spotlight | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/spotlight.html.summary: Spotlight Spotlight is a soft light that follows the pointer across the host's shape and lights the stretch of border nearest to it. It fades in when the pointer arrives and out when it leaves, and it reacts to a pointer just outside the shape too, so the border lights up as the pointer approaches. Use it on pricing cards, feature tiles or any surface that should answer the pointer. It draws over the child, and while the pointer is away it draws nothing. Light Dark Add a spotlight Put a Spotlight in the layers of the card it should light. Radius sets the size of the light. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Spotlight Radius="140" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="230" Height="130" CornerRadius="14" Padding="18,14" Background="#15171C"> <StackPanel Spacing="6"> <TextBlock Text="Pro" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="16" Foreground="White" /> <TextBlock Text="Move the pointer over me" FontSize="12" Foreground="#A1A1AA" /> </StackPanel> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Fill is the light on the surface and Rim the light on the border near the pointer, as wide as RimWidth. Color the light for light themes The default light is white, which shows on a dark card and vanishes on a white one. On a light theme, give it a color, for example from a theme resource: <fx:Spotlight Color="{DynamicResource SpotlightColor}" Radius="140" /> Define SpotlightColor per theme, such as an accent blue for Light and white for Dark; see Theme the colors. On an accent-colored button, a light in the accent color vanishes too: use white there. Tune how it follows PointerReach is how far outside the shape the pointer still lights it, 48 DIPs by default; set it to 0 to light the card only while the pointer is over it. FollowTime is how long the light takes to catch up with the pointer, and Fade how long it takes to appear and to fade out. <fx:Spotlight PointerReach="120" FollowTime="0.15" Fade="0.5" /> Point it from code PointAt aims the light as if the pointer were there: for keyboard focus or a guided tour. Pass null to fade it out; the pointer takes over again when it moves. // CardSpotlight is the Spotlight layer, CardHost its FXHost, SaveButton a button inside the card. SaveButton.GotFocus += (_, _) => { var center = new Point(SaveButton.Bounds.Width / 2, SaveButton.Bounds.Height / 2); CardSpotlight.PointAt(SaveButton.TranslatePoint(center, CardHost)); }; SaveButton.LostFocus += (_, _) => CardSpotlight.PointAt(null); Methods Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Points the light at at (host coordinates), as if the pointer were there: for keyboard focus or a guided tour. Null fades it out. The pointer takes over when it moves. Properties Property Type Default Description Color Color #FFFFFF The light's color. Radius double 160 Radius of the light. Range 20–600 DIPs. Fill double 0.14 Light on the surface. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Rim double 0.9 Light on the border near the pointer. Range 0–2. RimWidth double 1.5 Width of the lit border, in DIPs. Range 0.5–6. PointerReach double 48 How far outside the shape the pointer still lights it. Range 0–300 DIPs. FollowTime double 0.08 How long the light takes to catch up with the pointer (a time constant). Range 0–0.5 seconds. Fade double 0.3 How long the light takes to appear and to fade out. Range 0–1.5 seconds. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a spotlight, Intensity dims the layer; Speed and Seed don't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the light adds to the card. On a light surface it draws as tinted haze in its own color; a white or gray light stays white. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The light jumps to the pointer instead of easing, and appears and fades at once. See Reduced motion. Cost. Nothing while the pointer is away. While it moves, each frame repaints only around the light: about 0.03 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. See Performance. The pointer. The host listens to the window's pointer only while a layer that follows it is active, so the child doesn't need to be hit-testable. See Layers that follow the pointer. See also Spotlight API reference Trail and Ink, other layers that follow the pointer Holo foil, a sheen that shifts with the pointer Glow, a light around the shape that doesn't need the pointer One-shots and the pointer

docs/effects/starfield.html.title: Starfield | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/starfield.html.summary: Starfield Starfield paints a night sky: twinkling stars in three depths that drift slowly, the nearer ones faster. Its Meteors style adds shooting stars now and then, and Warp sends streaks rushing out from the center. Use it behind a hero, a splash or a launch screen, or as a quiet sky under other effects such as Fireworks and Trail. It's a fill: it paints the host's shape under the child. Light Dark Add a starfield Put the host around the panel, and leave the panel without a background so the sky shows through it. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Starfield Style="Warp" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="260"> <TextBlock Text="Launching…" Foreground="White" FontSize="18" FontWeight="SemiBold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Styles Value Description Stars (default) Twinkling stars drifting in three depths. Meteors Stars, with shooting stars streaking across now and then. Warp Streaks rushing out from the center, as at warp speed. Add shooting stars With Style="Meteors", shooting stars streak across the sky over the stars. MeteorRate is about how many fly each second, MeteorAngle the way they travel in degrees (0 to the right, 90 down; the default 145 runs down and to the left), MeteorLength the length of a tail in DIPs, and MeteorColor their color. They start along the top and the side they come from. <fx:Starfield Style="Meteors" MeteorRate="1" MeteorAngle="35" MeteorLength="140" MeteorColor="#FFE9B0" /> Fit the sky to the shape Density sets how many stars there are (or, in Warp, how many streaks), StarSize how big they are in DIPs, and Twinkle how much they twinkle, from 0 (steady) to 1. The stars are scattered in cells, and on a short shape the cells shrink to its height (down to 20 DIPs), so a strip such as a header or a button still holds stars in every depth. <fx:Starfield Density="2" StarSize="1" Twinkle="0.9" /> Put the stars over your own sky BackgroundColor is the sky behind the stars (#05060D by default); its alpha is how opaque it is. A transparent sky lets what is under the host show, such as a gradient on a border around it: <Border CornerRadius="16"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="0%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#0B1026" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#3B1E5F" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Starfield BackgroundColor="Transparent" Density="0.6" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="240" /> </fx:FXHost> </Border> The stars are added as light, so keep what is under them dark. Set the pace Speed multiplies the clock: the drift, the twinkle, the shooting stars and the warp streaks. A slower sky makes a calm backdrop for other effects; the gallery puts this one under a pointer trail: <fx:Starfield Density="0.6" Twinkle="0.4" Speed="0.3" /> Fills run on one shared clock, so starfields on different hosts, with the same settings, drift in step, whenever each host was created. Properties Property Type Default Description Style StarfieldStyle Stars What the sky shows: drifting stars, stars with shooting stars, or warp streaks. Values: Stars, Meteors, Warp. StarColor Color #E8EEFF The color of the stars and of the warp streaks. MeteorColor Color #BCD4FF The color of the shooting stars. Applies to the Meteors style. BackgroundColor Color #05060D The sky behind the stars; transparent lets what is under the host show. Density double 1 How many stars (in Warp, how many streaks), a multiple of the default. Range 0.1–3. Twinkle double 0.6 How much the stars dim and brighten (0: steady). Range 0–1 (0–100%). StarSize double 1.4 Size of the stars, in DIPs; the nearest are the largest. In Warp, the width of the streaks. Range 0.3–4. MeteorAngle double 145 The way shooting stars travel, degrees: 0 to the right, 90 down; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Applies to the Meteors style. MeteorRate double 0.5 About how many shooting stars appear each second. Range 0.05–3 per second. Applies to the Meteors style. MeteorLength double 90 Length of a shooting star's tail, in DIPs. Range 10–400. Applies to the Meteors style. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1, and Seed picks where the stars are. Notes Light and dark surfaces: the starfield doesn't change with the surface. Its default sky is dark, so it looks the same in both themes. With a transparent BackgroundColor, the stars only add light, and they fade out over a light surface. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the stars hold still and stop twinkling, no shooting stars fly, and the warp streaks hold still. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.11 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card. The cost grows with the area. See Performance. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which paints only the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also Starfield API reference Fireworks and Trail, which read well over a starfield Bokeh, Beams and Retro grid, other backgrounds Layers and hosts

docs/effects/swirl.html.title: Swirl | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/swirl.html.summary: Swirl Colors stirred into a slow swirl: folded, flowing noise is twisted around the center of the shape and colored through a ramp of up to six colors, blended in OKLab. It looks like ink spreading in water or veined marble. Use it for hero cards, splash screens, cover art and gradient text. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child, or paints the child's own pixels with UseMask. Light Dark Add a swirl The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Swirl Preset="Ink" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="116" CornerRadius="16" Padding="16"> <TextBlock Text="Ink" FontSize="19" FontWeight="Bold" Foreground="White" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset brings a palette and sets Scale, Turns and Warp. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset. Value Description Ink (default) Navy, indigo and cyan swirling into white, like ink in water. Marble Cream with gray veins folded finely through it, like polished marble. Use your own colors Colors takes up to six colors, which form a ramp from the first to the last; the swirl maps its folds onto that ramp. Set, they replace the preset's palette: <fx:Swirl Colors="#1A0B2E, #C2185B, #FF8A3D, #FFE1A8" /> Stir it Turns is how far the colors twist around the center, in turns at the middle: positive values twist counterclockwise, negative ones clockwise, and 0 leaves the noise untwisted. Warp sets how much the noise folds into itself, Scale the size of its features, and FlowSpeed how fast it moves: <fx:Swirl Preset="Marble" Turns="-0.8" Warp="2" Scale="120" FlowSpeed="0.1" /> Make swirled text With UseMask, the swirl paints only the letters and goes over them. Choose colors that stand out from the background behind the text: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Swirl UseMask="True" Colors="#3B2C85, #2FB3C9, #7C3AED" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="Swirl" FontSize="46" FontWeight="Black" /> </fx:FXHost> Fill a window The swirl's cost grows with its area. On a large panel, shade it at half resolution: <fx:Swirl Preset="Marble" RenderScale="0.5" /> On a 700×500 panel this took the swirl from 0.77 ms to 0.56 ms a frame in the gallery's bench. Properties Property Type Default Description Preset SwirlPreset Ink The palette used while Colors is unset, with matching Scale, Turns and Warp. Local values win. Values: Ink, Marble. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. Scale double 140 Feature size. Range 16–480 DIPs. FlowSpeed double 0.2 How fast the colors stir (0: still). Range 0–2 per second. Turns double 0.6 How far the colors twist around the center, in turns at the middle: positive counterclockwise, negative clockwise. Range -2 to 2. Warp double 1 How much the noise folds into itself. Range 0–2.5. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Seed changes the pattern. Still swirls: with FlowSpeed at 0, the swirl holds still and requests no frames. Light and dark surfaces: the swirl draws the same on both. Reduced motion: the swirl holds one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.311 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench, one of the heavier fills. See Render scale. Fills share one clock, so equal swirls on different hosts move in step. See also Swirl API reference Mesh gradient, Silk and Waves Reveal, whose Swirl style twists content in and out

docs/effects/tilt.html.title: Tilt | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/tilt.html.summary: Tilt Tilt leans the host toward the pointer in 3D and grows it a little, while a glare slides across it with the pointer, like a card turned under a light. Use it on cards, passes, product tiles and album art. The lean is a perspective render transform on the host, so the host's other layers, such as a glow or a shadow, lean with it. The glare is drawn over the content. Light Dark Add a tilt Add the layer to a host around the card, and leave a little room around it for the lean: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16" Margin="24" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Tilt MaxAngle="14" Glare="0.45" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="196" Height="120" CornerRadius="16" Padding="16"> <Border.Background> <LinearGradientBrush StartPoint="0%,0%" EndPoint="100%,100%"> <GradientStop Color="#1e3a8a" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#7c3aed" Offset="0.6" /> <GradientStop Color="#db2777" Offset="1" /> </LinearGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <TextBlock Text="NOVA PASS" Foreground="White" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Shape the lean MaxAngle is the most the host leans, in degrees (0: it stays flat); a negative angle leans away from the pointer instead. Lift is how much it grows while pointed at (1: not at all), and Perspective how far the eye is: nearer looks deeper. <fx:Tilt MaxAngle="-8" Lift="1.05" Perspective="600" /> Glare sets the strength of the glare and GlareColor its color. On bare text, set Glare to 0: the glare would light up the text's whole box. Reach and pace The layer listens to the window's pointer, so buttons inside the card don't block it, and it reads the pointer against the host as laid out, so the lean never chases itself. PointerReach is how far outside the content the pointer still leans it (0 by default: only over it). FollowTime is how long the lean and the glare take to catch up with the pointer; once the pointer leaves, the host eases back flat. Aim it from code PointAt(at) leans the host toward a point in its own coordinates, as if the pointer were there: for keyboard focus, a tour or a demo. PointAt(null) lets it settle flat, and the pointer takes over again when it moves. PassHost.GotFocus += (_, _) => { // Lean toward the top right corner while the card has focus. PassTilt.PointAt(new Point(PassHost.Bounds.Width, 0)); }; PassHost.LostFocus += (_, _) => PassTilt.PointAt(null); Methods Call PointAt to aim the lean from code. Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Leans toward at (host coordinates) as if the pointer were there: for keyboard focus or a demo. Null lets it settle flat. The pointer takes over when it moves. Properties Property Type Default Description MaxAngle double 10 The most it leans, degrees (0: it stays flat). Negative leans away from the pointer instead. Range -30 to 30. Lift double 1.03 How much it grows while the pointer is over it (1: not at all). Range 1–1.15. Perspective double 900 How far the eye is from the content: nearer looks deeper. Range 200–3000 DIPs. Glare double 0.35 The glare's strength. Range 0–1 (0–100%). GlareColor Color #FFFFFF The glare's color. FollowTime double 0.12 How long the lean and the glare take to catch up with the pointer (a time constant). Range 0–0.6 seconds. PointerReach double 0 How far outside the content the pointer still leans it. Range 0–200 DIPs. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Tilt follows the pointer, not a clock, so Speed and Seed do nothing. Notes The host's own transform. While it leans, the tilt takes the place of a RenderTransform set on the host. The host's own value comes back once it settles flat. Don't animate the host's RenderTransform while it tilts. Room around it. Leaning and lifting swing the corners past the host's bounds. Leave a margin, or a clipping ancestor cuts them. Light and dark. The glare draws the same on both surfaces, in GlareColor. Reduced motion. The host stays flat; only the glare follows the pointer. See the poses. Cost. Under 0.05 ms of GPU time a frame on a card. The lean is eased on the UI thread's animation frames only while it moves, and the transform is removed once flat. See What a layer costs. See also Tilt API reference Layers that follow the pointer Holo foil, a sheen that shifts with the pointer Pointer shadow, a shadow cast away from the pointer

docs/effects/topography.html.title: Topography | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/topography.html.summary: Topography Topography draws the contour lines of a slowly shifting landscape, like a topographic map: thin lines of even width at any slope, with every fifth one bolder. It's a calm background for a hero, an empty state or an outdoors app. It draws under the child, and by default only the lines, so whatever is behind the host shows between them. Light Dark Add topography Put the host around the panel, and leave the panel without a background so the lines show through it. A small plate behind the label keeps it readable over the lines: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Topography Scale="110" Levels="12" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Height="220" CornerRadius="14"> <Border Background="#F1F5F9" CornerRadius="10" Padding="14,6" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <TextBlock Text="Trailheads" Foreground="#0F172A" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Set the lines Levels is how many levels the landscape is cut into: more levels give more, closer lines (14 by default). Scale is the size of the hills in DIPs (180 by default), and LineWidth the width of a line in DIPs; every fifth line, the index line, is drawn bolder. A line keeps its width on steep and gentle slopes alike, and where lines crowd closer than a pixel they fade instead of filling in. <fx:Topography Levels="20" Scale="260" LineWidth="0.75" /> The landscape shifts slowly on its own. Speed multiplies its clock; at 0 it stops. Unlike the fills, its clock starts when it first draws, so topography on different hosts doesn't move in step. Color it for each theme LineColor colors the lines (#94A3B8 by default), and BackgroundColor fills behind them (transparent by default). Pale lines suit a dark theme; the gallery draws them in a deeper slate (#64748B) in light themes. Define a color for each theme in ThemeDictionaries, as on the Weather page, and the lines change color when the theme does: <fx:Topography LineColor="{DynamicResource ContourColor}" /> A map on paper, with its own background: <fx:Topography LineColor="#8A6F4D" BackgroundColor="#F5F0E6" /> Properties Property Type Default Description LineColor Color #94A3B8 The contour lines' color; its alpha is their opacity. BackgroundColor Color #00FFFFFF Behind the lines; transparent shows the content. Levels double 14 How many levels the landscape is cut into: more, closer lines. Range 3–40. Scale double 180 The size of the hills. Range 40–800 DIPs. LineWidth double 1 Width of a contour line, in DIPs; every fifth line is 1.8 times as wide. Range 0.25–4. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Seed picks the landscape. Notes Not a fill: topography has no BorderWidth or UseMask, and it runs on its own clock. Light and dark surfaces: the lines are drawn in LineColor on any surface, so pick a color for each theme, as above. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the landscape holds still. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.36 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card, among the heavier backgrounds: it works out the landscape's height three times a pixel to find the slope. The cost grows with the area. RenderScale lowers it, but softens the thin lines. See Performance. See also Topography API reference Fog, Particle network and Dot grid, other quiet backgrounds Waves, bands of color back to front Light and dark surfaces

docs/effects/trail.html.title: Trail | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/trail.html.summary: Trail Trail leaves a mark behind the pointer as it moves over the host: a glowing ribbon that tapers and fades, or a stream of sparks that drift, twinkle and fall. It runs from the head color at the pointer to the tail color at the end. Use it on a playful hero, a game screen or a drawing surface. It draws over the child, and a still pointer leaves nothing. Light Dark Add a trail Put a Trail on the panel the pointer moves over. Width sets the ribbon's thickness and Life how long each point of the trail lasts. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="12"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Trail Color="#A78BFA" TailColor="#22D3EE" Width="6" Life="0.45" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="340" Height="220" CornerRadius="12" Background="#15171C" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Glow scales the soft light around the ribbon; 0 leaves a plain stroke. Styles Value Description Ribbon (default) A glowing ribbon that tapers and fades behind the pointer. Sparkles Sparks shed along the path that drift, twinkle and fall. <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="10"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Starfield Density="0.6" Twinkle="0.4" Speed="0.3" /> <fx:Trail Style="Sparkles" Color="#FFE08A" TailColor="#FF8FD8" Width="5" Life="0.7" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Width="340" Height="220"> <TextBlock Text="Move the pointer here" Foreground="#C9D2FF" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> Keep the trail going past the edge By default the pointer only leaves a trail while it is over the shape. PointerReach extends that some DIPs past the edge, so a trail doesn't stop abruptly where the shape ends. <fx:Trail PointerReach="40" /> Draw a trail from code PointAt moves the trail's head as if the pointer were there, adding a point each time; null lifts it and the trail fades. Use it for a demo or an onboarding hint. The pointer takes over again when it moves. // DemoTrail is the Trail layer. Sweeps a wave across the panel, then lifts. var start = DateTime.Now; DispatcherTimer.Run(() => { var t = (DateTime.Now - start).TotalSeconds; if (t > 1.2) { DemoTrail.PointAt(null); return false; } DemoTrail.PointAt(new Point(20 + t * 240, 110 + Math.Sin(t * 6) * 40)); return true; }, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(16)); Methods Method Description PointAt(Point? at) Moves the trail's head to at (host coordinates), as if the pointer were there, adding a point to the trail; null lifts it and the trail fades. Properties Property Type Default Description Style TrailStyle Ribbon What follows the pointer: a glowing ribbon, or a stream of sparks. Values: Ribbon, Sparkles. Color Color #A78BFA The ribbon's color at its head; each spark takes a mix of this and TailColor. TailColor Color #22D3EE The color the ribbon fades to at its tail. Width double 6 Width of the ribbon at its head, in DIPs (it tapers behind); for sparks, their size. Range 1–30. Life double 0.45 How long a point of the trail lasts. Range 0.1–2 seconds. Glow double 0.8 The soft light around the ribbon, a multiple: 1 is full, 0 none. Range 0–2. Applies to the Ribbon style. PointerReach double 0 How far outside the shape the pointer still leaves a trail. Range 0–200 DIPs. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a trail, Intensity dims the layer and Seed doesn't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the trail adds light. On a light surface it draws as tinted haze in its own colors. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. There is no trail: it only exists as motion. See Reduced motion. Cost. Nothing while the pointer is still or away. While it moves, about 0.17 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. The trail keeps the pointer's last 32 positions. See Performance. The pointer. The host listens to the window's pointer while the layer is active and passes it on within the shape plus PointerReach. See Layers that follow the pointer. Room around the host. Sparks fall and the glow spreads a little past the shape. A clipping ancestor cuts them off. See also Trail API reference Sparkles, stars twinkling around a shape Ink, colored fluid stirred by the pointer Spotlight, a light that follows the pointer One-shots and the pointer

docs/effects/voiceorb.html.title: Voice orb | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/voiceorb.html.summary: Voice orb Voice orb draws a living sphere of color: three soft lights drift inside a glassy orb, their colors meeting smoothly, with a glow around it. Bind Level to the microphone and the orb swells, its edge rolls and the lights drift faster as the voice rises. Use it as the face of a voice feature, a dictation button or a call screen. The orb is centered on the host's shape and draws under the child, so an icon or initials can sit on top. Light Dark Add a voice orb Give the host a square child; the orb's radius is a share of its smaller half-size (Size). Here a microphone icon sits on the orb. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="56" Margin="40"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:VoiceOrb Level="{Binding MicLevel}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="112" Height="112"> <Path Data="M12,3 A3,3 0 0 0 9,6 L9,12 A3,3 0 0 0 15,12 L15,6 A3,3 0 0 0 12,3 Z M18,12 A6,6 0 0 1 6,12 M12,18 L12,21" Stroke="White" StrokeThickness="2" StrokeLineCap="Round" Width="26" Height="26" Stretch="Uniform" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Follow the voice Level runs from 0 (quiet) to 1 (loud). Set it from your microphone meter as often as you get readings; the layer eases changes, rising quickly and falling more slowly, so a jumpy reading looks like a smooth swell. // Orb is the VoiceOrb layer; called whenever the audio meter reports a new peak (0..1). private void OnMeterLevel(double peak) { Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(() => Orb.Level = peak); } Color and shape Color, SecondColor and ThirdColor are the three lights; they blend through their own middle rather than through gray. Size sets the orb at rest, Glow the light around it (0 for none), and Turbulence how much the lights bend as they drift. <fx:VoiceOrb Color="#34D399" SecondColor="#22D3EE" ThirdColor="#A78BFA" Size="0.7" Glow="1.4" Turbulence="0.6" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Level double 0 How loud, 0..1: bind it to the microphone level. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Color Color #7C5CFF The first light's color. SecondColor Color #22D3EE The second light's color. ThirdColor Color #EC4899 The third light's color. Size double 0.8 The orb's radius at rest, as a share of the shape's smaller half-size. Range 0.3–1 (30–100%). Glow double 1 The glow around the orb, a multiple: 1 is the default, 0 none. Range 0–2. Turbulence double 1 How much the lights bend as they drift. Range 0–2. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On the orb, Intensity dims the layer, and Seed sets where each light starts its orbit, so two orbs never move in step. Notes Light and dark surfaces. The orb looks much the same on both; its glassy rim is fainter on a light surface. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The colors hold still, and the orb still swells with Level. See Reduced motion. Cost. The orb moves all the time, even at a Level of 0, so it redraws every frame while it is active. Its glow covers more area than most layers (about 0.8 Mpx on the bench's 340×190 card), and the cost grows with the area. Set IsActive to False while the app isn't listening. See Performance. Room around the host. The glow reaches past the shape by about the orb's radius. A clipping ancestor cuts it off: leave room around the host. See also VoiceOrb API reference Voice wave, glowing waves that swell with the same level Pulse, a breathing halo for a simpler listening state Glow, light around a shape

docs/effects/voicewave.html.title: Voice wave | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/voicewave.html.summary: Voice wave Voice wave draws glowing waves across the host's shape in three colors, crossing each other under an envelope that pinches them to nothing at both ends. Quiet, they lie almost flat and drift slowly; bind Level to the microphone and they swell and drift faster as the voice rises. Use it under a dictation field, in a call bar or beside a voice orb. The waves fill the shape from side to side and draw under the child. Light Dark Add a voice wave The waves span the child's width and rise into its height, so give the child the size the waves should take. An empty Border is enough. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <StackPanel Spacing="6"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="0"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:VoiceWave Level="{Binding MicLevel}" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="250" Height="96" /> </fx:FXHost> <TextBlock Text="Listening…" HorizontalAlignment="Center" Opacity="0.6" /> </StackPanel> </UserControl> Follow the voice Level runs from 0 (quiet) to 1 (loud). Set it from the microphone meter as often as readings arrive; the layer eases changes, rising quickly and falling more slowly, and speeds up the drift without the waves jumping. // Wave is the VoiceWave layer; called whenever the audio meter reports a new peak (0..1). private void OnMeterLevel(double peak) { Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(() => Wave.Level = peak); } To pair it with a voice orb, bind both to the same level. Color and size Color, SecondColor and ThirdColor are the three waves. Amplitude is how high they rise at full level, as a share of the half height. LineWidth sets the thickness of each line and Glow the light around it (0 for none). <fx:VoiceWave Color="#F472B6" SecondColor="#FBBF24" ThirdColor="#34D399" Amplitude="0.6" LineWidth="1.5" Glow="1.3" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Level double 0 How loud, 0..1: bind it to the microphone level. Range 0–1 (0–100%). Color Color #7C5CFF The first wave's color. SecondColor Color #22D3EE The second wave's color. ThirdColor Color #EC4899 The third wave's color. Amplitude double 0.8 How high the waves rise at full level, as a share of the half height. Range 0.1–1 (10–100%). LineWidth double 2 Width of each wave's line, in DIPs. Range 0.5–8. Glow double 1 The glow around the waves, a multiple: 1 is the default, 0 none. Range 0–2. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a voice wave, Intensity dims the layer and Seed doesn't apply. Notes Light and dark surfaces. On a dark surface the waves add light. On a light surface they draw as tinted haze in their own colors. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion. The waves hold still, and they still swell with Level. See Reduced motion. Cost. About 0.05 ms of GPU time a frame on the bench's 340×190 card. The waves drift even at a Level of 0, so the layer redraws every frame while it is active: set IsActive to False while the app isn't listening. See Performance. Inside the shape. The waves draw only within the shape, so they need no room around the host; Amplitude is a share of the shape's half height. See also VoiceWave API reference Voice orb, an orb that swells with the same level Pulse, a breathing halo for a simpler listening state Waves, layered color bands as a background

docs/effects/voronoi.html.title: Voronoi | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/voronoi.html.summary: Voronoi A mosaic of cells around points that orbit slowly, so the cells shift and trade space with their neighbors. Each cell takes one of the colors and is shaded toward its rim, and thin seams run between them, like tiles, cracked glaze or stained glass. Use it for game and achievement cards, decorative headers and playful buttons. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child, or paints the child's own pixels with UseMask. Light Dark Add a Voronoi fill The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Voronoi Preset="Cells" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="120" Height="116" CornerRadius="16" Padding="12"> <TextBlock Text="Cells" FontSize="13" FontWeight="SemiBold" Foreground="White" VerticalAlignment="Bottom" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset brings a palette and sets SeamColor, CellSize, Seam and Depth: Cells is large tiles in shades of blue, Stained smaller cells of colored glass. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset. Value Description Cells (default) Tiles in four shades of navy blue with dark seams. Stained Small red, orange, purple, teal and lime panes with dark leading, like stained glass. Use your own colors Each cell takes one of the colors in Colors, up to six. Set, they replace the preset's palette: <fx:Voronoi Colors="#FDE68A, #FCA5A5, #A7F3D0, #BFDBFE" SeamColor="#FFFFFF" Seam="2.5" /> Shape the cells CellSize sets the size of the cells, in DIPs. Seam is the width of the seams between them (0 for none) and SeamColor their color. Depth shades each cell toward its rim; at 0 the cells are flat. FlowSpeed sets how fast the points orbit: <fx:Voronoi Preset="Stained" CellSize="28" Seam="3" Depth="0" FlowSpeed="0.1" /> Make mosaic text With UseMask, the cells fill only the letters and go over them. Large, bold type with small cells shows the pattern best: <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Voronoi Preset="Stained" UseMask="True" CellSize="10" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <TextBlock Text="LEVEL UP" FontSize="44" FontWeight="Black" /> </fx:FXHost> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset VoronoiPreset Cells The palette used while Colors is unset, with matching SeamColor, CellSize, Seam and Depth. Local values win. Values: Cells, Stained. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. SeamColor Color #0B0F1A The color of the seams between cells. CellSize double 36 Average size of a cell, in DIPs. Range 6–200. FlowSpeed double 0.25 How fast the seed points orbit, reshaping the cells (0: still). Range 0–2 per second. Seam double 1.5 Seam width (0: none). Range 0–8 DIPs. Depth double 0.4 Shading toward each cell's rim, as a share (0: flat cells). Range 0–1 (0–100%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Seed changes the layout of the cells. Still cells: with FlowSpeed at 0, the cells hold still and the layer requests no frames. Light and dark surfaces: the cells draw the same on both. Reduced motion: the cells hold one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.258 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench, one of the heavier fills. On a 700×500 panel it takes 0.76 ms, and 0.40 ms with RenderScale="0.5". See Render scale. See also Voronoi API reference Metaballs, Halftone and Swirl Shatter, which breaks content into Voronoi shards

docs/effects/water.html.title: Water | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/water.html.summary: Water Water puts the content under a sheet of water: moving the pointer over it drags ripples across the surface, a press drops a splash, and Rain lets drops fall on their own. The waves bend what is under them and catch the light. Use it for a playful hero, a calm "drop files here" area, or a pool on a game screen. A small wave simulation runs only while the water moves, and calm water draws nothing. It draws over the child, so it bends the child and whatever shows through it. Light Dark Add water Wrap the content in a host. Move the pointer over it for ripples, and press for a splash: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="14"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Water /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="260" Height="150" CornerRadius="14"> <Border.Background> <RadialGradientBrush> <GradientStop Color="#22D3EE" Offset="0" /> <GradientStop Color="#0E7490" Offset="1" /> </RadialGradientBrush> </Border.Background> <TextBlock Text="Touch the water" Foreground="White" FontWeight="Bold" FontSize="20" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Give it something to bend The water copies what is under it just before it draws (see Layers that read the backdrop): the child, and whatever shows through it. Text, edges and pictures show the waves best. A press splashes only when it lands on the host's child, so give a see-through child a Background, even Transparent. Inside an offscreen layer (an ancestor with Opacity below 1, an effect, or a clip that needs a layer) the copy can't see that ancestor's content, so keep such ancestors opaque. Splash from code Splash(at) drops a splash at a point in the host's coordinates, or at the center with no point. Set SplashOnPress="False" to stop presses from splashing: // A splash where a drag ends over the pool. private void OnPoolReleased(object? sender, PointerReleasedEventArgs e) { PoolWater.Splash(e.GetPosition(PoolHost)); } // A splash in the middle when a task completes. PoolWater.Splash(); Let it rain Rain is how many drops fall a second on their own; Seed places them. With rain, the water keeps moving and keeps drawing: <fx:Water Rain="1.5" /> Tune the surface Damping sets how long ripples last, Refraction how strongly the waves bend what is under them (1 is natural water), Stir how hard the pointer pushes, and Highlight the light on the waves. Tint colors the water where it rises, and its alpha is how much. CellSize is the simulation's cell size: smaller is finer and costs more. <fx:Water Damping="0.992" Refraction="1.5" Stir="1.4" Tint="#4022D3EE" /> Methods Call Splash to make waves without a press. Method Description Splash(Point? at = null) Drops a splash at at (host coordinates), or the center. Properties Property Type Default Description Damping double 0.985 How long ripples last: each 60th of a second keeps this share of the wave. Range 0.9–0.999. Refraction double 1 How strongly the waves bend what is under them, a multiple: 1 is natural water, 0 none. Range 0–3. Stir double 1 How hard the pointer pushes the water. Range 0–3. Rain double 0 Drops a second falling on their own. Range 0–20 per second. CellSize double 4 Simulation cell size: smaller is finer and costs more. Range 2–12 DIPs. Highlight double 1 Highlights on the waves. Range 0–2. Tint Color #303AA0FF A color where the water rises; its alpha is how much. SplashOnPress bool true Drops a splash where the host is pressed. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes The pointer: ripples follow it while it is over the shape. See Layers that follow the pointer and One-shots. Light and dark surfaces: it draws the same on both. Reduced motion: gentler ripples and splashes, and no rain. Cost: about 0.13 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark card while the water moves. The simulation steps at 60 Hz on the render thread; once the surface is flat it clears and stops, so calm water costs nothing. See Performance. See also Water API reference Rain glass, Shockwave, Ink and Caustics Layers that read the backdrop

docs/effects/waves.html.title: Waves | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/waves.html.summary: Waves Layered bands of color, one per color, stacked from back to front, with rolling, swaying crests; each band in front shades the one behind it. It reads as a sea, a range of dunes or hills. Use it for headers, weather and travel cards, footers and calm backgrounds. It is a fill: it paints the host's shape and goes under the child, or paints the child's own pixels with UseMask. Light Dark Add waves The fill goes under the child, so leave the child without a background: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Waves Preset="Sea" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="120" Height="116" CornerRadius="16" Padding="12"> <TextBlock Text="Sea" FontSize="13" FontWeight="SemiBold" Foreground="#0A2649" VerticalAlignment="Top" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Presets Each preset brings a palette and sets Amplitude, Crests and FlowSpeed. Set any of them yourself to adjust a preset. Value Description Sea (default) Pale sky blue at the back to deep navy in front, with lively crests. Dunes Sand cream to deep rust, with broad, slow crests. Use your own colors Each color in Colors is one band, up to six. The first is the band at the back, at the top of the shape, and the last the one in front, at the bottom. A dusk sea: <fx:Waves Colors="#FFD6A5, #F28482, #84A59D, #3D5A80, #1D2D44" /> Text sits on the band at its height, so pick its color by that band: dark text near the top of the Sea preset, light text lower down. Shape the crests Amplitude is the height of the crests, as a share of the shape, and Crests how many cross it. FlowSpeed sets how fast they roll, and Softness how soft the edges between bands are. Angle turns the direction the bands stack along; 0 is top to bottom, and positive angles turn clockwise: <fx:Waves Preset="Dunes" Amplitude="0.1" Crests="2.5" Softness="0.02" Angle="90" /> Properties Property Type Default Description Preset WavesPreset Sea The palette used while Colors is unset, with matching Amplitude, Crests and FlowSpeed. Local values win. Values: Sea, Dunes. Colors FXColorList Unset The colors (up to six). Unset: the preset's palette. Amplitude double 0.05 Crest height, as a fraction of the rect. Range 0–0.25 (0–25%). Crests double 1.6 Crests across the rect. Range 0.2–6. FlowSpeed double 0.4 How fast the crests roll and sway (0: still). Range 0–2 per second. Angle double 0 Direction the bands stack along, degrees: 0 top to bottom; positive turns clockwise. Range -180 to 180. Softness double 0.006 Edge softness, as a fraction of the rect. Range 0–0.1 (0–10%). BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. Notes Intensity is the fill's coverage, from 0 to 1. Still waves: with FlowSpeed or Amplitude at 0, the bands hold still and the layer requests no frames. Light and dark surfaces: the waves draw the same on both. Reduced motion: the bands hold one pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: 0.073 ms of GPU time per frame on a 340×190 card in the gallery's bench. See Performance. Like every fill, waves can paint only the child's own pixels with UseMask, or a band inside the edge with BorderWidth. See also Waves API reference Swirl, Mesh gradient and Silk Topography and Retro grid

docs/effects/weather.html.title: Weather | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/effects/weather.html.summary: Weather Weather lets rain streaks or snowflakes fall across the host's shape in three depths, slanted by the wind. Use it on a weather card, over a photo or a hero section, or for a seasonal touch. Unlike the other fills, it goes over the child by default and draws only the drops, so the content stays visible between them. Light Dark Add rain Put the host around the card. The card keeps its own background, and the rain falls over it, clipped to its rounded shape. <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Weather /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="340" Height="190" CornerRadius="16" Background="#1E293B" Padding="20"> <TextBlock Text="Showers until 6 PM" Foreground="White" FontSize="18" FontWeight="SemiBold" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> Styles Value Description Rain (default) Thin streaks falling fast. Snow Soft round flakes drifting slowly down, swaying as they fall. Snow drifts down slowly, and each flake sways a little as it falls: <fx:Weather Style="Snow" Density="1.4" Size="1.2" /> Slant it and set the fall WindAngle slants the fall, in degrees from straight down: positive slants it to the right, negative to the left (12 by default). Density sets how many drops or flakes fall, and Size how big they are, as a multiple (1 is natural). FallSpeed multiplies how fast they fall; at 0 they hold still and the layer asks for no frames. <fx:Weather WindAngle="-25" Density="2" FallSpeed="1.4" /> To change the pace while it falls, change Speed or FallSpeed; neither makes the animation jump. Fills run on one shared clock, so weather on different hosts, with the same settings from the start, falls in step. Pick a color for each theme The default color, a pale blue (#CFE3FF), reads on dark content but all but vanishes on a white card. Give the layer a deeper color in light themes; the gallery uses #5878B0. With theme resources, it changes when the theme does: <Application.Resources> <ResourceDictionary> <ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries> <ResourceDictionary x:Key="Light"> <Color x:Key="RainColor">#5878B0</Color> </ResourceDictionary> <ResourceDictionary x:Key="Dark"> <Color x:Key="RainColor">#CFE3FF</Color> </ResourceDictionary> </ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries> </ResourceDictionary> </Application.Resources> <fx:Weather Color="{DynamicResource RainColor}" /> Fall behind the content With Placement="Under", the weather falls behind the child instead, like the other fills. Leave the child without a background so the drops show through it, and put any background on a container around the host: <Border Background="#0F172A" CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="16"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Weather Style="Snow" Placement="Under" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Grid Height="220"> <TextBlock Text="Winter sale" Foreground="White" FontSize="28" FontWeight="Bold" HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center" /> </Grid> </fx:FXHost> </Border> Properties Property Type Default Description Style WeatherStyle Rain What falls: rain streaks or snowflakes. Values: Rain, Snow. Color Color #CFE3FF The color of the drops or flakes. Density double 1 How much falls, a multiple of the default. Range 0.1–3. FallSpeed double 1 How fast it falls, a multiple of the default (0: it hangs still). Range 0–3. WindAngle double 12 Slant from straight down, degrees: 0 falls straight down; positive slants the fall to the right (counterclockwise), negative to the left. Range -60 to 60. Size double 1 Size of the drops or flakes, a multiple: 1 is natural. Range 0.3–4. BorderWidth double 0 Width of a band inside the edge, DIPs. 0: the whole shape. Range 0–48. UseMask bool false Paints only the child's own pixels (text, icons, a logo) instead of the shape: gradient text, a liquid-metal logo, holographic icons. It then goes over the child unless Placement says otherwise. The host captures the child to know its pixels: call RefreshMask after changing something deep inside it. Every layer also has the common properties: Intensity, Opacity, Speed, Seed, IsActive, Placement, BlendMode and RenderScale. On a fill, Intensity is its coverage, up to 1. Notes Light and dark surfaces: the drops are drawn in Color on any surface, so pick a color for each theme, as above. See Light and dark surfaces. Reduced motion: the rain or snow holds one fixed pose. See Reduced motion. Cost: about 0.07 ms of GPU time a frame on the benchmark's 340×190 card. The cost grows with the area. See Performance. Room: the drops are clipped to the host's shape. Rain needs some height to read as rain, so it suits a card or a panel more than a button. Bands and masks: like every fill, it has BorderWidth, which paints only a band inside the edge, and UseMask, which lets it fall only on the child's own pixels, such as large text. See Content masks. See also Weather API reference Rain on glass, drops beading on a pane over the content Fog and Water Starfield, another sky to put behind content

docs/gallery.html.title: Gallery | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/gallery.html.summary: Gallery The Nova.Avalonia.FX gallery lets you try every effect layer, change its settings and copy its XAML. It runs in your browser as well as on the desktop. Open the WebAssembly gallery What is in it Home shows curated demos on real controls. Effect pages show one layer on a target you pick (a button, card, field, pill, avatar or text), with its one-shots, its XAML and its settings. The settings panel only shows the settings that do something for the current style. Glass and distortion pages put a drifting scene behind the target so there is something to bend. The settings flyout switches the theme (light, dark or the system's), motion (full or reduced) and dither. Under 880 pixels wide, as on a phone or a tablet, the sidebar slides in over the page from the menu button at the top left, and picking a page closes it. When the page itself is narrow, its settings fold into a drawer that the settings button at the right of the page header opens. A press outside it or Escape closes it. The gallery uses the Nova.Avalonia.UI gallery theme: Fluent, the Nova palette and the shared Nova shell. Run on the desktop dotnet run --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop The gallery itself is samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery (the app, pages and styles). The desktop app around it, samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop, adds the tools below. Run in the browser samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Browser runs the same gallery in the browser (WebAssembly, drawn with WebGL). Install the WebAssembly tools once, then run the browser host: dotnet workload install wasm-tools dotnet run -c Release --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Browser Then open http://localhost:5240. The page takes these options in its address: Option What it does ?effect=glow Opens an effect page; ?effect=fire:Simulated opens it in a style. ?check Compiles every shader at start and reports any that fail in the browser's console. ?tour Opens every effect page in turn and fires its one-shot; ?tour=5&only=glass,fire shows some, 5 seconds each. ?verify Opens every effect in every style, fires its one-shot, checks that it drew, and prints the ones that didn't. ?bench Times every effect, as the desktop's --bench does; ?bench=glow,fire:Simulated times some, &seconds=3 each. ?check, ?verify and ?bench also show their results on the page (click to hide), for browsers without a console at hand. global.json asks for the .NET 10.0.100 SDK or a later 10.0 feature band. Publish the browser gallery A Release publish compiles the .NET code ahead of time, which keeps every effect smooth on slower machines at the cost of a larger download (see Performance): dotnet publish -c Release samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Browser -o publish/browser Then serve publish/browser/wwwroot with any static web server. The page loads everything by relative path, so it works under any path. The documentation workflow publishes it the same way and deploys it under /gallery/, next to this documentation, whenever a push to main passes the build and tests. Tools The desktop app has command-line tools for snapshots, checks and timing. Pass them after --. Snapshots: --snap dotnet run --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --snap gallery.png --theme dark --time 2.3 Renders the gallery headless, through Skia, at a fixed time, and exits. Add: --effect electric to open an effect page, and --target 1 to pick its target: 0 button, 1 card, 2 field, 3 pill, 4 avatar, 5 text, 6 panel. --reduced for the reduced-motion poses. --size 1380x900 to set the size. --set Style=Heat to set any parameter of the effect page's layer. --frames 96 --fps 24 to write a numbered frame sequence. --fire to fire the page's one-shot (a splash, a reveal) on the first frame, and --fire-every 4 to fire it again every 4 frames. --settings to open the settings drawer in a narrow window. The animated images in the README are frame sequences made this way. Every effect on every target: --sweep dotnet run -c Release --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --sweep sweep Renders every effect on every target in both themes, in one run (about five minutes), with one-shots caught mid-flight: sweep/<effect>/<theme>-<target>.png, plus a labeled sheet per effect, sweep/<effect>.png, for checking that every demo reads well. --only glow,beam limits it to some effects. Timing: --bench dotnet run -c Release --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --bench bench.csv Times every layer in a real window on the GPU the app uses, and writes the results to a CSV file. Performance covers its options and how to compare a run with the baseline. The settings panel: --audit-panel dotnet run --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --audit-panel panel-audit.md Drives every editor of every effect page headless (a slider moved, a toggle flipped, a choice picked, a color typed), checks that its property changed, and writes a report. It also checks the settings drawer in a narrow window. The build workflow runs it on Windows, Linux and macOS. Checks and tours: --verify and --tour dotnet run --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --verify dotnet run --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --tour 3 --verify opens the gallery and checks that every effect and style draws, as ?verify does in the browser. --tour 3 walks through every page, 3 seconds each. Documentation images: --docs dotnet run -c Release --project samples/Nova.Avalonia.FX.Gallery.Desktop -- --docs docs Writes the parts of this documentation that come from the code: each effect's tables of properties, styles and methods under docs/includes/, and its light and dark images under docs/images/effects/, on the target the gallery opens it on. --only glow,border_beam limits it to some effects, and --no-images writes only the tables (in under a second). A full run takes about six minutes, and running it twice gives the same files.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Follow these steps to install Nova.Avalonia.FX, wrap a control in an FXHost and give it its first layers. Prerequisites Avalonia 12.1.5 or later in the Avalonia 12 release line, with the Skia renderer (the default) .NET 8 or later The layers draw on the desktop and in the browser (WebAssembly, with WebGL). On another rendering backend they draw nothing rather than fail. Install the NuGet package The package is in preview, so include prerelease versions. From your application project: dotnet add package Nova.Avalonia.FX --prerelease There are no styles to register. The library has no control templates: FXHost is a plain control and the layers are styled elements, so nothing needs to go in Application.Styles. Declare the XAML namespace Every layer, the host and the catalog are in one XAML namespace. Map it to the fx prefix: xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX" Wrap a control in an FXHost FXHost takes one child and draws its layers around it. Add layers to FXHost.Layers. This puts a neon glow around a card: <UserControl xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:fx="https://github.com/jsuarezruiz/Nova.Avalonia.FX"> <fx:FXHost HorizontalAlignment="Center" VerticalAlignment="Center"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Glow Style="Neon" Color="#22d3ee" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Width="220" Height="96" CornerRadius="14" Background="#101217" /> </fx:FXHost> </UserControl> The layers follow the child's bounds and corner radius. The host reads the corner radius from a Border or a templated control; for anything else, or to override it, set FXHost.CornerRadius. CornerRadius="999" makes a capsule or a circle. A glow spills past the child, and it is drawn outside the host's bounds. A clipping ancestor cuts it: a ScrollViewer, a Border with ClipToBounds, or Fluent's ContentControl, which clips by default. Leave room around the host, or set ClipToBounds="False" where that is safe. Stack several layers A host can hold any number of layers. Each one draws under the child or over it (its placement), and within each placement they paint in the order you list them. Here a liquid-metal fill goes under the label and sparkles go over it: <fx:FXHost CornerRadius="26"> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:LiquidMetal Preset="Gold" /> <fx:Sparkles BurstOnPress="True" IsContinuous="False" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Border Padding="40,14"> <TextBlock Text="Upgrade" /> </Border> </fx:FXHost> The sparkles only show when the host is pressed, because IsContinuous is off and BurstOnPress is on. Layers and hosts explains placement, blend modes and the properties every layer shares. Set properties Layer settings are Avalonia styled properties, so you can set them in XAML, bind them, take them from resources and animate them: <fx:Glow Style="Neon" Color="{DynamicResource SystemAccentColor}" IsLit="{Binding IsOnline}" Cool="0.8" /> Switching IsLit off cools the glow over Cool seconds instead of cutting it off. Styles reach layers too. This fades a glow up while the pointer is over the host: <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.hover fx|Glow"> <Setter Property="Intensity" Value="0.2" /> <Setter Property="Transitions"> <Transitions> <DoubleTransition Property="Intensity" Duration="0:0:0.3" /> </Transitions> </Setter> </Style> <Style Selector="fx|FXHost.hover:pointerover fx|Glow"> <Setter Property="Intensity" Value="1.3" /> </Style> From code, create a host and its layers like any other control: using Avalonia; using Avalonia.Controls; using Avalonia.Media; using Nova.Avalonia.FX; var host = new FXHost { CornerRadius = new CornerRadius(14), Child = new Button { Content = "Generate" }, }; host.Layers.Add(new Glow { Style = GlowStyle.Neon, Color = Color.Parse("#22d3ee") }); A layer can be in one host at a time. Adding a layer that is still in another host's Layers throws an InvalidOperationException. Fire a one-shot from code Some layers play a moment when asked: a ripple, a burst of confetti, a zap. Name the layer and call its method. Points are in the host's coordinates; leave them out to use the layer's own spot. <fx:FXHost> <fx:FXHost.Layers> <fx:Confetti x:Name="Celebration" /> </fx:FXHost.Layers> <Button Content="Save" Click="OnSave" /> </fx:FXHost> private void OnSave(object? sender, RoutedEventArgs e) { Celebration.Fire(); } Most one-shot layers can also fire on a press of the host, such as Confetti.FireOnPress or Pulse.TriggerOnPress. One-shots and the pointer lists them all. Next steps Browse the Effects pages to see each layer's settings and examples. Read Light and dark surfaces if your app has a light theme. Run the gallery to try every layer and copy its XAML.

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Nova.Avalonia.FX
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Nova.Avalonia.FX adds GPU effects to Avalonia controls. You wrap a control in an FXHost and give the host one or more layers. Each layer is an SkSL shader (or, for a few, shapes drawn with Skia) that the host draws under the control, like a glow or a background, or over it, like a sheen, grain or a ripple. The layers run on the composition render thread and only ask for frames while something moves. A layer with nothing to animate, a hidden host and a host scrolled out of view cost nothing. Highlights 70 layers in 12 groups: light, surface, materials, gradients, patterns, color, shape, glass, distortions, moments, depth and backgrounds. The home page lists them all. Lights that cool: a Glow switched off shrinks, deepens and dims instead of cutting off, and on a light surface light layers draw as tinted haze instead of vanishing into white. Effects that follow the content: a mask glow, a text shimmer, gradient text, an Outline or an InnerShadow follow the child's own pixels, not just its box. Glass and distortions: Glass, frost, rain, water and the distortions bend and blur what is drawn behind them. Moments: one-shots such as ripples, confetti and fireworks that overlap, and transitions such as Reveal, Shatter and Genie that show and hide the content. Ordinary Avalonia properties: layers are styled elements, so styles, bindings, dynamic resources and transitions apply to them like any other property. A catalog: FXCatalog describes every layer with its parameters, ranges and choices, and writes a layer back as XAML. Reduced motion: every layer has a calm pose, switched on for the whole app with FXSettings.ReducedMotion. How to use these docs Start with Getting Started to install the package and put a first layer on a control.
